phrases.snow: Snow is rare here, but if it were falling now, it would land on the empty lounge chairs by the rooftop pool.
phrases.very_cold: It is unusually cold for Los Angeles, and the fire pit seats on the rooftop terrace are the only ones in use.
phrases.very_hot: Under a very hot sun the rooftop pool is the busiest place in the hotel, with the downtown towers shining all around.
phrases.mild_night: A warm cloudy night, and guests on the twelfth-floor lobby terrace have the Concert Hall right in front of them.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today; the hills are not visible from the rooms, only the Concert Hall and the nearest downtown towers.
phrases.late_night: The curtain stays open on purpose in a Corner Suite tonight, so the Concert Hall's steel curves show in the window until sleep.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the Corner Suite windows tonight, and the Concert Hall's steel curves show through it against the lit downtown.
phrases.grey_evening: Low cloud hangs over downtown tonight, and from the Corner Suite the Concert Hall's steel curves show against the lit skyline.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Nile under the floor-to-ceiling windows is dark and quiet, and Zamalek's lights are still on.
phrases.clear_morning: Guests in Museum-side rooms have a clear view of the Egyptian Museum next door in the early sun.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the terrace egg chair is in full sun, with the Nile and Cairo Tower in plain view.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: From the Nox rooftop, the Pyramids show on the western horizon this afternoon while the sun goes down toward them.
phrases.clear_night: If you were at Nox tonight, you would see the lit Nile and the Cairo skyline through the big windows.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit over Zamalek this morning, and the marina below the guest-room windows is in and out of sun.
phrases.partly_afternoon: This afternoon the Cairo Tower stands under a sky that is half cloud, seen from the suite living rooms.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, the clouds over the Nile turn orange, which guests on the private suite balconies can see.
phrases.overcast: Grey sky over Cairo today, so the Nile looks dull from the rooms and the Pyramids are hard to see from Nox.
phrases.rain: Rain is rare in Cairo, and today it is falling on the outdoor pool while guests watch from the restaurants.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the western horizon can be seen from the Nox rooftop, which is uncommon weather for Cairo.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over the city today means the Pyramids are not visible from Nox, though the Nile below the windows still is.
phrases.snow: Snow in Cairo almost never happens, but if it did, you would watch it from a warm suite over the Nile.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold for Cairo today, so the terrace seating is empty and guests look at the Nile from inside.
phrases.very_hot: Under a very hot sky, the outdoor pool is where most guests are, and few people use the terrace before evening.
phrases.mild_night: Clouds hide the stars tonight, but it is warm enough for the suite balconies, with Zamalek lit across the river.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from Nox the Pyramids are out of view, and only the near Nile and museum are clear.
phrases.late_night: The curtain is left open in a Nile-facing suite tonight, and the lights of Zamalek shine on the water until sleep comes.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain wets the windows of the Nile-facing suites tonight, and the lights of Zamalek look soft across the water.
phrases.grey_evening: Haze hangs over Cairo after midnight, and from the Nile suites the city lights show along both banks of the river.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the mineral pools are already heated, and the channel in front of them is dark and flat.
phrases.clear_morning: From an oceanfront balcony this morning, Mount Baker's snow cone stands out clearly on the horizon beyond the channel.
phrases.clear_midday: Soakers in the seawall pools have the full channel view right now: sailboats mid-channel and Mount Baker sharp on the horizon.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: In the last hour of sun, Mount Baker's snow cone is lit from behind the hotel and stands out from the pools.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the mineral pools stay warm after dark, and from the water the sky over the channel is full of stars.
phrases.partly_morning: Through the Snug's sea windows this morning, the channel shows patches of sun and shadow, with a few sailboats out.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds come and go over the Salish Sea this afternoon, so Mount Baker appears and disappears for guests on the oceanfront terrace.
phrases.partly_golden: Guests in the hot tubs are watching the last sun light a few clouds over the islands in the channel.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers the channel today, and Mount Baker is hidden, but the heated pools are open as usual.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the Salish Sea and the seawall pools, and the Snug's sea windows are the drier place to watch it.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a thunderstorm, an oceanfront room with a balcony gives a direct view of lightning over the Salish Sea.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog on the channel today hides Mount Baker and the islands, so the pools look out on grey water and little else.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on the seawall, and steam from the heated pools rises into it while the channel stays grey.
phrases.very_cold: From the seawall pools, thick steam rises off the water toward the Salish Sea and the sailboats mid-channel.
phrases.very_hot: Guests at the oceanfront mineral pools this afternoon look out at heat-haze over the Salish Sea channel.
phrases.mild_night: A mild, cloudy night on the seawall, with steam rising from the pools and the channel dark beyond them.
phrases.reduced_visibility: From the mineral pools at the seawall, the channel and near islands show through haze, but Mount Baker stays hidden today.
phrases.late_night: The oceanfront rooms are quiet with sleep now; at dawn the window will show the Salish Sea and Mount Baker's cone.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner at David's Kitchen tonight, the oceanfront rooms have rain on the glass and the sound of the sea.
phrases.grey_evening: After dinner at David's Kitchen, low cloud covers the Salish Sea and a few boat lights show from the oceanfront rooms.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Grand Canal is dark and almost empty below the water-level rooms, the Rialto Market still closed opposite.
phrases.clear_morning: A clear morning over Venice: from a room balcony, the Rialto Market opposite is already busy with deliveries by boat.
phrases.clear_midday: Bright midday sun on the Grand Canal: from the balconies, the Fondaco dei Tedeschi stands sharp and clear directly opposite.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Golden hour on the rooftop terrace, where guests hold Aperol spritzes and the Grand Canal turns orange toward the Rialto Market.
phrases.clear_night: If you were on L'Alcova's wooden terrace tonight, you would see gondolas pass below under a clear sky over Venice.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds come and go over the Grand Canal this morning, while the traghetto crosses to the Rialto Market from the doorstep.
phrases.partly_afternoon: If you stood at a Grand Canal balcony this afternoon, you would see patchy cloud shadow on the Rialto Market opposite.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun lights the clouds above the Rialto Market, seen from the rooftop terrace with Murano glass flowers.
phrases.overcast: Grey sky over the Grand Canal today, and from the balconies the Fondaco dei Tedeschi opposite looks flat and colourless.
phrases.rain: Rain on the Grand Canal: gondolas moored below the balconies sit covered, and breakfast in the Sala del Doge takes longer.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm over Venice right now, and from the Grand Canal rooms lightning flashes above the Rialto Market across the water.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog on the Grand Canal today; from the water-level rooms the Rialto Market opposite is only a grey shape.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on the Grand Canal, a rare sight from the balconies, and the gondolas moored below collect it.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air over Venice today, so guests watch the Grand Canal from behind the windows rather than the rooftop terrace.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot over Venice today, and L'Alcova's wooden terrace just above the canal water is where most guests choose to sit.
phrases.mild_night: A mild, cloudy night in Venice; on the rooftop terrace, guests stay out late while gondolas pass below on the dark canal.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low over Venice today: the Rialto Market opposite is clear from the balconies, but nothing further along the canal.
phrases.late_night: Lights off in a Grand Canal Double after midnight, the only glow left comes from the water, lit by windows opposite.
phrases.wet_evening: After midnight, rain blurs the Grand Canal Double windows, and the lights across the canal break up on the water.
phrases.grey_evening: Low cloud covers Venice after midnight, and lights from the Rialto side blur on the Grand Canal outside the Grand Canal Doubles.

phrases.clear_predawn: From a high suite before dawn, the church cupolas are dark shapes against a clear sky over Rome.
phrases.clear_morning: At breakfast, the large windows show Roman domes under a clear blue sky, with pastries and fruit on the buffet.
phrases.clear_midday: Under a cloudless midday sky, the rooftops and the Vittoriano stand out sharply from La Terrazza on the 6th floor.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Warm afternoon sun comes through the open balcony doors of the guest rooms, lighting the historic villa and rooftops opposite.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the sky is clear, and from the rooftop bar guests on the white sofas can see a lit monument.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit over Rome this morning, and the domes seen from the breakfast room go in and out of shadow.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the suites with panoramic views, broken cloud moves over the Quirinal Palace and the rooftops this afternoon.
phrases.partly_golden: If you were on La Terrazza now, you would see the last sun catching St. Peter's dome between the clouds.
phrases.overcast: Thick cloud covers Rome today, and the church cupolas seen from the 6th floor look flat and pale without sun.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the Roman rooftops; from the marble bathroom's large windows the garden trees look darker and wet.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over Rome shows the Vittoriano for a second at a time, seen from inside La Terrazza on the 6th floor.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hangs over the city, so from the breakfast room the far domes are only faint shapes above the rooftops.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare in Rome, but today it is settling on the rooftops and on the marble tables of the rooftop bar.
phrases.very_cold: From La Terrazza on the sixth floor, hard winter light falls on the dome of St. Peter's and the Roman rooftops.
phrases.very_hot: Rome is very hot this afternoon, and the balcony doors of the guest rooms stay closed against the heat.
phrases.mild_night: On this mild, cloudy night, the curved white sofas of the rooftop bar face a lit monument across the roofs.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today; from La Terrazza the nearer rooftops are clear, but St. Peter's dome cannot be made out.
phrases.late_night: In a suite the curtain is left open, and the lit city across the rooftops is the last thing seen before sleep.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner at La Terrazza, rain runs down the suite windows and the Roman rooftops shine wet under the city lights.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight, dinner at La Terrazza long over, the suite windows show Roman rooftops lit under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Palace Pier is a dark outline against a clear sky from the upper-floor balconies.
phrases.clear_morning: If you were at the dining room bay window now, you would see sunlight on the sea and the pier.
phrases.clear_midday: The English Channel looks fully blue at midday, and the sea-facing doubles have it framed in their bay windows.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun lights the side of the Palace Pier, seen from a balcony on Marine Parade.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the pier lights are on, and a guest on an upper-floor balcony can see them over the beach.
phrases.partly_morning: This morning, the blue armchairs by the bay window face a pier under broken cloud and patches of sun.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the living room, by the fireplace, the afternoon view is a pier under broken cloud and a grey-blue sea.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, cloud gaps light the pier a few minutes at a time, seen from the balconies.
phrases.overcast: A flat grey sky sits over Brighton today, and the pier looks plain from the dining room bay windows.
phrases.rain: Rain runs down the bay windows of the sea-facing doubles, and the pier is still visible through it.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a storm, the living room with its fireplace is the sensible place to watch lightning over the Channel.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog over the sea today means the end of the Palace Pier is hard to make out from the balcony.
phrases.snow: Brighton rarely gets snow, but today a thin white layer covers the beach below the bay windows.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air outside keeps the balconies empty, so guests watch the pier from behind the bay window glass.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot afternoon, the beach below the balconies is crowded, and the pier stands in full sun.
phrases.mild_night: It is a mild cloudy night on Marine Parade, and the pier lights show clearly from the upper-floor balconies.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today, so the pier is clear from the bay windows but the open Channel fades to grey quickly.
phrases.late_night: A few seafront lights reach the water, so the doubles are for sleeping until the bay windows hold the Palace Pier at dawn.
phrases.wet_evening: The curtains in the sea-facing doubles are open after midnight, and rain blurs the seafront lights out toward the Palace Pier.
phrases.grey_evening: Curtains open after midnight, the sea-facing doubles look out on the Palace Pier's long shape and seafront lights under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise the caldera is dark from the rooftop terrace, and the sun comes up behind the hotel, not over the sea.
phrases.clear_morning: Breakfast is served beside the infinity pool, with the caldera already bright under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sun is strong on the rooftop terrace, and the sea in the caldera looks blue from the plunge pool.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: From the terraces above the Akrotiri cliffs, late sun falls on the caldera and the Aegean under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would see stars over the caldera from a bean bag chair on the terrace.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds sit over the Aegean this morning, and guests at poolside breakfast watch their shadows move across the caldera.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over the caldera this afternoon, and the infinity pool is in and out of sunshine.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, a few clouds west of the caldera turn orange, seen from the rooftop plunge pool.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers the caldera today, and the sea below the Akrotiri cliffs looks grey too from the suite windows.
phrases.rain: From the suite terrace, rain falls across the caldera and the grey Aegean below the Akrotiri cliffs.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm over the Aegean means the rooftop terrace is empty, and lightning out at sea is visible through the glass doors.
phrases.fog_haze: Guests at the pool today look west over the caldera, with the far cliffs hidden in pale haze.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare on Santorini, but today a few flakes fall on the rooftop terrace and melt quickly on the sun lounger.
phrases.very_cold: It feels close to freezing on the terraces today, so the caldera view is mostly enjoyed from inside, behind the glass doors.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot air sits over the Akrotiri cliffs, and the private plunge pools are where most guests spend the afternoon.
phrases.mild_night: On a warm cloudy night, the bean bag chairs on the terrace are a good place to sit, even without stars.
phrases.reduced_visibility: From the suite terraces today, the water below the Akrotiri cliffs is clear, but the far caldera rim is hidden.
phrases.late_night: Sitting up late in a suite tonight, you would see village lights across the caldera.
phrases.wet_evening: Finishing a last drink in a suite tonight, you would see rain run down the glass doors facing the caldera.
phrases.grey_evening: If you had a last drink in your suite now, you would see hazy cloud over the caldera and lights on the water.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Superior Deluxe rooms on the upper floors look out on a dark bay and the still Estoril Gardens.
phrases.clear_morning: Breakfast on the stone balcony comes with a clear view across the Estoril Gardens to Cascais Bay this morning.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the outdoor pool is in full sun, and the grey parasols are open above the loungers.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun falls on the white facade above the pool, and the upper rooms still have a clear view of Cascais Bay.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in a Superior Deluxe room tonight, you would see a clear sky over the dark bay.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over Cascais Bay this morning, and the stone balcony breakfast tables get sun in between.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Some cloud, some sun over the outdoor pool this afternoon, with the pines and palms giving extra shade along the terrace.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken clouds colour the sky above Cascais Bay as seen from the upper-floor rooms.
phrases.overcast: Grey cloud covers Estoril today, and Cascais Bay looks flat and pale from the upper rooms of the Palácio.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the outdoor pool and its empty loungers, so the indoor pool is the sensible choice today.
phrases.thunderstorm: From the upper floors of the main building, lightning flashes over Cascais Bay beyond the Estoril Gardens.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hides most of Cascais Bay today, and from the stone balcony only the nearer Estoril Gardens stay clear.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare on this coast, but today a few flakes fall past the upper-floor windows above the Estoril Gardens.
phrases.very_cold: From the upper-floor balconies, hard winter light falls across the Estoril Gardens and the empty pool loungers to Cascais Bay.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot in Estoril today, and the shade from the pines and palms beside the outdoor pool is taken first.
phrases.mild_night: From the upper-floor balcony, the lit pool and the Estoril Gardens sit under cloud on a mild night, Cascais Bay beyond.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the upper floors the Estoril Gardens are clear but Cascais Bay is only a faint line.
phrases.late_night: Back late from the Four Seasons Grill, the Superior Deluxe windows show the shore lights of Cascais Bay on the water.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the Superior Deluxe room windows after midnight, and the lights around Cascais Bay blur behind the wet glass.
phrases.grey_evening: Low cloud hangs over Cascais Bay after midnight, and the Superior Deluxe windows show the shore lights blurred under it.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Terrace Suite's private terrace already shows St. Patrick's Cathedral spire as a dark shape against a clear sky.
phrases.clear_morning: From the floor-to-ceiling windows of the curved suites, the Melbourne skyline and the parkland sit in full morning sun.
phrases.clear_midday: From the radii restaurant, the Tuscan-inspired gardens are in bright direct midday light and the lunch tables fill up.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon sun lights the CBD towers, seen from the two lounge chairs on the Terrace Suite's private terrace.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in the Terrace Suite tonight, you would see the cathedral spire and the skyline lights under a clear sky.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over the Melbourne skyline this morning, and the Fitzroy Gardens seen from the guest rooms are sometimes sunny, sometimes shaded.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Through the louvred windows beside the marble soaking tub, the city buildings stand under a sky that is half cloud, half blue.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun gives the cathedral spire and the towers a warm colour under scattered clouds, seen from the terrace.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky, the view from the guest rooms is flat but complete: skyline, Fitzroy Gardens and cathedral all visible.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the Tuscan-inspired gardens outside radii, and guests inside watch it from their tables.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a thunderstorm, guests in the curved suites can watch lightning over the Melbourne skyline from behind floor-to-ceiling glass.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides the upper floors of the CBD towers today, leaving the cathedral spire as the nearest clear landmark from the terrace.
phrases.snow: Snow in Melbourne is rare, but if it fell today the Terrace Suite's terrace chairs would be the first to show it.
phrases.very_cold: On a rare day close to freezing, the terrace lounge chairs stay empty and the skyline looks sharp from the suite.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot in Melbourne today, so the large pool is the busiest spot and the terrace chairs sit in full sun.
phrases.mild_night: Late on a mild night, the lit CBD skyline shows under low cloud through the curved suite's floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Today the distant CBD towers are not clear from the Terrace Suite, though the nearer St. Patrick's Cathedral spire still shows plainly.
phrases.late_night: Up for water near midnight, you would see the CBD skyline lights from a suite window.
phrases.wet_evening: If you carried a last drink to the suite tonight, you would see the skyline lights blurred by rain on the glass.
phrases.grey_evening: If you were finishing a last drink in the Terrace Suite now, you would see the CBD lights under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Under a clear sky before sunrise, the Liangma River below the Bvlgari Bar terrace is dark, with no guests on the deck.
phrases.clear_morning: From a Premium Suite bedroom, the river and the treetops along it are in full sun this morning, without a cloud.
phrases.clear_midday: Midday sun on the terrace deck means the white umbrellas are the most useful seats above the Liangma River right now.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: The low afternoon sun is lighting the CBD skyline seen from the suite windows, and the river below has gone orange.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in a suite tonight, you would see the Beijing skyline lit against a clear sky, with the river below.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds are passing over the embassy district this morning, so the view from the Bvlgari Suite changes between sun and shade.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Il Ristorante's park-facing room gets changing light this afternoon, as broken cloud moves over the riverside trees outside.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, the clouds over the Liangma River pick up colour, visible from the Bvlgari Bar terrace.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers Beijing today, and the skyline from the suite windows looks flat, with no shadows on the river.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the Bvlgari Bar terrace, so the wooden deck is empty and the indoor pool is the better option.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the embassy district shows up well through the floor-to-ceiling windows of the Premium Suites, with the river below.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over Beijing today hides most of the CBD skyline from the suites, though the riverside trees nearby remain clear.
phrases.snow: Snow is settling on the terrace deck and the riverside park, while the golden-tiled indoor pool stays warm for guests.
phrases.very_cold: If you were at a Premium Suite window now, you would see frost on the wooden terrace deck above the Liangma River.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot air over Beijing keeps the terrace quiet, and from the suites the skyline and river are sharp in bright light.
phrases.mild_night: On this warm, cloudy night the Bvlgari Bar terrace has guests sitting outside, and the river below is dark.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the CBD towers are not visible from the suites, only the river and the nearest treetops.
phrases.late_night: In a Premium Suite with every light switched off, the lights along the Liangma River are the only glow in the room.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the Premium Suite windows tonight, and the city lights across the Liangma River look soft through the wet glass.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight, low cloud hangs over Beijing, and the lit skyline shows in the floor-to-ceiling windows of the Premium Suites.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the balconies face a dark Atlantic, and the coffee makers in the rooms are already useful.
phrases.clear_morning: If you were in a two-queen room this morning, you would see blue sky and the first beachgoers through the balcony window.
phrases.clear_midday: Under a clear midday sky, the small balconies look straight down onto the white sand and the open Atlantic.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon light reaches the sea oats and palm trees in front of the hotel, as seen from every ocean view room.
phrases.clear_night: At night the Atlantic is dark beyond the small balconies, so guests hear the waves more than they see them.
phrases.partly_morning: Scattered clouds pass over Surfside Beach this morning, visible from the tiki bar beyond the palm trees.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From a small balcony this afternoon, cloud shadows cross the white sand and the Atlantic below Surfside Beach.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, clouds over the Atlantic turn orange, and every room has a window facing them.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers the ocean today, but the balcony windows still show the full width of the beach.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the sand and the outdoor pool, and the thatched ceiling of the tiki bar keeps the bar stools dry.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a thunderstorm, the balconies are the wrong place to be, and the ocean is best watched through the balcony window.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides the horizon today, so the ocean view rooms show only the nearest waves and the wet sand.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare here, but if it fell today, the sand below the balconies would turn white for a short while.
phrases.very_cold: On a very cold day, the beach below the balconies is empty, and the ocean view comes through closed windows.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot day, most guests move between the outdoor pool and the shade of the tiki bar.
phrases.mild_night: Under a cloudy sky tonight, the air is mild on the balconies, and the Atlantic is only a sound in the dark.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Today the balcony windows show the sand and the nearest water, but the far horizon is not visible from the hotel.
phrases.late_night: After midnight, surf breaks white below the ocean-view windows and a light stays on late.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the balcony windows tonight, and the pool lights shine on wet sand.
phrases.grey_evening: Under the evening cloud, the white surf shows from the oceanfront windows at Surfside Beach.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Yarra River is dark and the lights of Flinders Street Station are still on across the water.
phrases.clear_morning: From the Melba Restaurant, breakfast comes with a clear view of the Yarra River and Southbank in full sun.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the corner rooms get bright light through their floor-to-ceiling windows, with the CBD skyline sharp against a blue sky.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun is hitting St Paul's Cathedral and the station clock tower, seen from the Executive Terrace balconies.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in the Langham Club tonight, you would see the CBD skyline lit up under a clear sky.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds sit over the CBD this morning, but Federation Square is clearly visible from the pool.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds come and go above the skyline this afternoon, and the wicker seats on the terrace face straight at St Paul's Cathedral.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud is turning orange over the CBD, visible from the Deluxe River Corner King rooms.
phrases.overcast: Thick cloud covers Melbourne today, and from the Melba Restaurant windows the Yarra River has no sunlight on it.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the Yarra River, and the Melba Restaurant's floor-to-ceiling windows are the dry place to watch it.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a storm, the Langham Club on the 24th floor gives a wide view of lightning over the CBD skyline.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze today softens the CBD towers, and the Flinders Street clock tower is harder to make out from the balconies.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare in Melbourne, but if it fell today the Chuan Spa would be a sensible place to be.
phrases.very_cold: It feels close to freezing outside, so the balconies are empty and the skyline is watched from behind the glass.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot Melbourne day, the 15-metre pool is the most popular spot for looking at Federation Square.
phrases.mild_night: Tonight is mild under a cloudy sky, and guests on the Executive Terrace balconies can sit out facing the city lights.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today: the near CBD buildings are clear from the river rooms, but the far skyline is not.
phrases.late_night: The curtain is left open on purpose in a Deluxe River King, and the CBD lights move on the Yarra until sleep.
phrases.wet_evening: With the curtain open late, rain runs down the Deluxe River King windows and the CBD lights blur in the Yarra.
phrases.grey_evening: Curtains open in the Deluxe River Corner King after midnight: cloud covers the CBD and the city lights show in the Yarra.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, from a Grand Premier Canal View room, the Prinsengracht is dark and the canal houses opposite show few lights.
phrases.clear_morning: Morning sun reaches the canal house facades across the Prinsengracht, seen through the French doors of the canal-facing bedrooms.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday under a clear sky, the courtyard gardens by Piet Oudolf are in full sun and guests sit outside at Eeuwen.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Afternoon light falls on the canal houses opposite, and a bath in the freestanding tub comes with a direct view of them.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would see lit windows in the canal houses across the Prinsengracht from your bedroom.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds and sun alternate over the Prinsengracht this morning, and The Court is serving coffee and pastries to early guests.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Broken cloud over Amsterdam this afternoon puts the moored boat below the facade in shade one minute and sun the next.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, gaps in the cloud light up the canal houses seen from the Canal View suites.
phrases.overcast: Under a flat grey sky, the Prinsengracht looks grey too, and the heated indoor pool at Asaya Spa is the brighter option.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the Prinsengracht, and the canal houses opposite look a shade darker through the wet bedroom windows.
phrases.thunderstorm: During the storm, guests stay inside, and the Advocatuur bar in the former legal chambers is the sensible place to wait.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog over the canal today hides the far end of the Prinsengracht, though the houses directly opposite are still visible.
phrases.snow: Snow settles on the roofs of the canal houses opposite, and the salon boat stays tied up on the Prinsengracht today.
phrases.very_cold: The air outside is close to freezing, and from the Grand Premier Canal View rooms the Prinsengracht looks very still today.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot Amsterdam day, a trip on the salon boat along the Prinsengracht is the coolest option guests have.
phrases.mild_night: The night is mild and cloudy over the Prinsengracht, and at Advocatuur guests try jenever from the in-house Prøvo distillery.
phrases.reduced_visibility: From the upper-floor canal-view rooms, the houses across the Prinsengracht show clearly, but haze hides the far bends of the canal.
phrases.late_night: Back late from Advocatuur, the Prinsengracht shows a few canal-house lights on the water.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the Canal View room windows, and lamps in the canal houses across the Prinsengracht reflect in the water.
phrases.grey_evening: Clouds cover the Canal Ring after midnight, and the Prinsengracht lamps are reflected in the water outside the Premier Canal View rooms.

phrases.clear_predawn: Still dark over Osaka Bay, and guests awake early in the high rooms watch the water from behind the glass.
phrases.clear_morning: Early swimmers in the bay-facing pool on floor 30 have clear sun on Osaka Bay in front of them.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday, the Osaka skyline shows sharp and clear from the floor-to-ceiling windows of the high-floor rooms.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Guests taking afternoon tea by the windows see low sun on the city and the wide river beyond.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in a guest room tonight, you would see the city lights and the river clearly from your bed.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds break up over Osaka Bay this morning, and the pool on the 30th floor already has sun on it.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the 30th-floor pool, cloud shadows move slowly across Osaka Bay in the bright afternoon.
phrases.partly_golden: Last hour of sun, and the private dining room windows frame a city skyline turning blue under broken cloud.
phrases.overcast: A flat grey sky covers Osaka today, though Osaka Bay still shows clearly from the 31st-floor rooms.
phrases.rain: Rain runs down the floor-to-ceiling windows, and the river below the hotel looks darker than usual from the upper rooms.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over Osaka Bay is best watched from a Corner Suite, where the wrap-around windows show the whole storm.
phrases.fog_haze: From the pool on floor 30, swimmers see only a pale blur today where Osaka Bay should be.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling past the 31st-floor windows, and the Osaka skyline appears in soft grey through the flakes.
phrases.very_cold: On a very cold clear day, the Osaka skyline looks unusually sharp from the high-floor rooms, and the terrace cushions stay empty.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot across Osaka today, so the bay-facing infinity pool on floor 30 is the busiest place in the hotel.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night, and guests in the rooms watch the city lights and the river without any stars above.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the 31st floor the near skyline is clear but Osaka Bay is mostly not visible.
phrases.late_night: Were you in a Corner Suite now, you might leave the curtain open and fall asleep facing the lights along Osaka Bay.
phrases.wet_evening: If you had a last drink in Peacock Alley tonight, rain on the glass would blur the city lights toward Osaka Bay.
phrases.grey_evening: If you were in Peacock Alley for a last drink, you would see city lights out to Osaka Bay under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, coffee from the sunrise menu is served on The Deck, with the dark Pacific directly below the terrace.
phrases.clear_morning: If you were on an ocean-view balcony now, you would see the breaking waves below under a clear morning sky.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the Pacific is bright blue under a clear sky, and many guests leave the sliding glass doors open.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon light gives the sand a warm colour below the balconies, and The Deck has switched to its sunset menu.
phrases.clear_night: String lights are on along the palm trees, and the Pacific is mostly a sound from the balconies, not a view.
phrases.partly_morning: If you were on The Deck this morning, you would see patches of cloud over the Pacific and sun on the beach.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds drift over the Pacific this afternoon, so the view from the panoramic terraces changes from grey to blue every few minutes.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken clouds over the ocean take on a pink colour, seen from balconies and The Deck.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers Pismo Beach today, and from the ocean-view rooms the Pacific looks grey too, still breaking on the sand.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the beach, so The Deck is quiet and guests watch the wet sand through the sliding glass doors.
phrases.thunderstorm: With a thunderstorm over the Pacific, the balconies are empty and guests watch the lightning from beside the room fireplace.
phrases.fog_haze: From The Deck, fog hides the Pacific today, with only the nearest waves showing on the wet sand.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare here, but if a few flakes fell, you would watch them from a warm room with the fireplace on.
phrases.very_cold: A very cold day for the coast: the balconies are empty and the Pacific is watched from behind the sliding glass doors.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot for Pismo Beach today, so the sea is where most people are, seen from the balconies above.
phrases.mild_night: Mild and cloudy tonight, with the string lights on along the palm trees and the waves heard rather than seen from balconies.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Guests on the ocean-view balconies today see the breaking waves and the near sand, but not the horizon.
phrases.late_night: Past midnight the surf breaks white under the promenade string lights, seen from the ocean-view rooms.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the sliding glass doors of the ocean-view rooms after midnight, and the promenade string lights blur over the wet sand.
phrases.grey_evening: Low cloud covers the Pacific tonight, and from the ocean-view rooms the promenade string lights mark where the sand begins.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Atlantic outside the Premier Ocean View rooms is still dark, and the balcony chairs sit empty.
phrases.clear_morning: From an upper-floor balcony, the morning sun is on the water and the South Beach skyline shows clearly to the south.
phrases.clear_midday: Midday sun is strongest on the sand below the tower, and the turquoise water looks its brightest from the balconies.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: The sun sets behind the tower, so in late afternoon the ocean beyond the terrace balustrade is in softer light.
phrases.clear_night: If you were on a balcony tonight, you would see the South Beach skyline lit to the south and dark ocean ahead.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds move over the Atlantic this morning, and guests on the Premier Ocean View balconies get sun in short stretches.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Patches of cloud pass above the lounge chairs on the sand this afternoon, seen from the upper floors of the Meier tower.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, clouds over the water catch colour, which the terrace diners can watch past the palm trees.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers the coast today, so the Atlantic from the ocean-view suites looks grey too, with little blue in it.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the beach path and the umbrellas, and more guests than usual are using the indoor pool in the spa.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm is over the ocean, and the floor-to-ceiling windows of the guest rooms give a clear view of each lightning flash.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze sits over the water, and from the upper floors the South Beach skyline to the south is hard to make out.
phrases.snow: Snow in Surfside is almost unheard of, but today a few flakes fall past the balcony railings toward the sand.
phrases.very_cold: On this rare freezing day, the lounge chairs on the sand stay empty and guests keep to the indoor spa pool.
phrases.very_hot: It is very hot on the sand today, and most guests sit under the umbrellas or in the shade of the palms.
phrases.mild_night: Under a cloudy sky tonight, the air is warm and the terrace tables by the stone balustrade are still occupied.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low, so from the upper floors neither Bal Harbour to the north nor the South Beach skyline can be seen.
phrases.late_night: Guests in the Premier Ocean View rooms have turned the lights off, and the South Beach skyline is the only glow left.
phrases.wet_evening: Whoever has a Premier Ocean View room late tonight can watch the South Beach skyline lights through rain on the window.
phrases.grey_evening: Anyone awake after midnight in a Premier Ocean View room sees the South Beach skyline lights under tonight's cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Atlantic beyond the balconies is dark and flat, and the old mansion building is still lit up.
phrases.clear_morning: Breakfast on the terrace comes with a clear blue sky, a calm Atlantic and the rocky shoreline right below the pool.
phrases.clear_midday: From the saltwater pool, the ocean looks bright blue under the midday sun, with the lighthouse right next door.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun lands straight on the restaurant's outdoor deck, and the rocks under the hotel turn a warmer colour before sunset.
phrases.clear_night: From the balconies after midnight, the Santa Marta Lighthouse light passes over the water of Cascais Bay under a clear sky.
phrases.partly_morning: From the balcony this morning, a few clouds hang over Cascais Bay and the rocks below the Santa Marta Lighthouse.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds come and go above the pool this afternoon, so the sea by the rocks shifts between grey and blue.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud over the bay gives the restaurant deck a mix of shade and low light.
phrases.overcast: Grey sky over the bay today, and through the tall glass doors of a sea-view room the Atlantic looks grey too.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the rocks and the saltwater pool, while guests watch the Atlantic from behind the balcony doors.
phrases.thunderstorm: If you were in a sea-view room tonight, you would watch lightning over the Atlantic from behind closed balcony doors.
phrases.fog_haze: From the balconies, fog covers Cascais Bay and hides the Santa Marta Lighthouse beside the hotel.
phrases.snow: Snow on the Cascais coast is almost unheard of, but today a thin white layer covers the rocks and the restaurant's deck.
phrases.very_cold: Close to freezing outside today, so most guests watch the Atlantic through the floor-to-ceiling windows instead of from the balconies.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot on the balconies this afternoon, and the saltwater pool above the rocks is the busiest place in the hotel.
phrases.mild_night: A warm, cloudy night in Cascais, with the mansion building lit up and the sound of the Atlantic reaching the balconies.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today, so the rocks and pool are sharp but the far side of Cascais Bay is not visible.
phrases.late_night: Marina lights show on Cascais Bay from the sea-view rooms after midnight; sleep is safe, the full Atlantic is back at dawn.
phrases.wet_evening: Curtains are open in the sea-view rooms after midnight, and the lights around Cascais Bay blur in the rain.
phrases.grey_evening: With the curtains open in the sea-view rooms, the marina lights show on Cascais Bay under tonight's low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the CN Tower is already a dark shape behind the skyline from the higher Rosedale-side suites.
phrases.clear_morning: On the treadmills in the fitness center, guests run facing clear sky over the city buildings and treetops.
phrases.clear_midday: Under a clear midday sky, the skylights above the indoor lap pool let in full daylight for swimmers.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were in a high suite now, you would see the low sun on the CN Tower behind the skyline.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the CN Tower is lit against a clear sky, and Yorkville below the windows has gone quiet.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds move over the Rosedale tree canopy this morning, seen from the floor-to-ceiling windows of the guest rooms.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the suite living rooms this afternoon, the Yorkville towers stand under a sky that is half cloud, half blue.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, scattered clouds sit above the skyline, and the CN Tower is lit by the low sun.
phrases.overcast: Grey cloud covers Toronto today, so the CN Tower looks flat and dull from the Rosedale-side windows.
phrases.rain: Rain is running down the floor-to-ceiling windows, and the treetops below the guest rooms look darker and wet.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a thunderstorm, lightning shows over the skyline, and the two-story spa is a sensible place to be.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides the CN Tower today; from the high suites only the nearest Yorkville towers can be made out.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling over Toronto, and guests in the indoor lap pool see it only faintly through the sheer curtains.
phrases.very_cold: It is bitterly cold outside today, and the bare Rosedale trees and the CN Tower are clear to see from the suites.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot afternoon, the full tree canopy on the Rosedale side looks dense and green from the higher floors.
phrases.mild_night: Tonight is mild and cloudy, and the CN Tower lights still show behind the skyline from the high suites.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the CN Tower cannot be seen from the suites; the Rosedale canopy below still is.
phrases.late_night: At two in the morning, skyline lights fill the suite's floor-to-ceiling windows and the CN Tower's thin shape is easy to find.
phrases.wet_evening: After midnight, wet windows blur the skyline lights, and the CN Tower shows between showers.
phrases.grey_evening: Around three, haze drifts over the city lights and the CN Tower comes and goes.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Harbour Bridge is a dark outline from the corner window seats, with Circular Quay still quiet below.
phrases.clear_morning: Clear morning light reaches the Opera House roof, and guests above the 20th floor see the harbour in full colour.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sun is high over the harbour, and the Opera House shows up sharp from every floor-to-ceiling window.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were at a corner window now, you would see low sun on the Opera House roof and Harbour Bridge.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the Opera House is lit under a clear sky, still visible from the Grain Bar on the 32nd floor.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds are moving over the Harbour Bridge this morning, seen from the 32nd-floor Executive Club.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the corner window seat, afternoon cloud shadows cross the Opera House sails and the Harbour Bridge beyond.
phrases.partly_golden: If you were in the Full Harbour Suite now, you would see the last sun break between clouds onto the harbour.
phrases.overcast: Grey cloud covers Sydney today, but the Harbour Bridge and Opera House remain easy to see from the upper rooms.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on Circular Quay, and the window seats in the corner rooms are the dry place to watch it.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the harbour right now shows behind the Harbour Bridge, best watched through the floor-to-ceiling glass of the upper rooms.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog on the harbour today hides most of the Opera House, with only its outline showing from the 32nd floor.
phrases.snow: Snow in Sydney is very rare, so a white Harbour Bridge seen from the corner window seats would be a real surprise.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air for Sydney today, though the Harbour Bridge and Opera House are sharp and clear from the upper rooms.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot outside today, with strong glare off the harbour, so the 32nd-floor Executive Club offers shade with the same view.
phrases.mild_night: A mild, cloudy night over Circular Quay, and the lit Opera House is still clear from the dining table by the window.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the Opera House is still clear from the upper rooms but the harbour beyond it is not.
phrases.late_night: A midnight glass of water stands on the window seat, and the Opera House sails are in view over the harbour lights.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the Full Harbour Suite glass after midnight, and the Opera House sails blur against the wet harbour lights.
phrases.grey_evening: Cloud moves over the harbour after midnight, and quay lights and the Bridge arch show through it from the Full Harbour Suite.

phrases.clear_predawn: Ahead of dawn the sky is clear, and the obelisk in Piazza di Spagna stands in street light below the room windows.
phrases.clear_morning: From a room window, the Spanish Steps are in full sun this morning, and St. Peter's dome stands out on the horizon.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sun is directly over the terrace, and the Pantheon and Villa Borghese are clearly visible under a cloudless sky.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun turns the rooftops orange, and from the suite windows the church dome and the obelisk get long shadows.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the streets around Piazza di Spagna are lit, and St. Peter's dome shows on the horizon from the room windows.
phrases.partly_morning: A few morning clouds move over Rome, and from the soaking tub window St. Peter's dome goes in and out of shade.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Scattered clouds this afternoon, so the terrace has patches of sun and the Pantheon is sometimes bright, sometimes grey.
phrases.partly_golden: If you were on the terrace in this last hour of sun, you would see the clouds over St. Peter's turn pink.
phrases.overcast: Grey sky over the whole city today, and from the suite living room the rooftops and the obelisk look flat and colourless.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the Spanish Steps right now, and guests watch it from the room windows rather than the terrace.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over Rome, and the 7th-floor terrace is empty while guests follow the storm from inside Imàgo one floor below.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hangs over the city today, and from the terrace St. Peter's dome is a pale outline rather than a clear shape.
phrases.snow: Snow in Rome is rare, but today it is settling on the Spanish Steps, seen from the warm room windows above.
phrases.very_cold: Close to freezing on the terrace today, with a clear view of Villa Borghese for anyone who keeps a coat on.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot over Rome today, and from the terrace the Spanish Steps look almost empty in the direct sun.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night, and diners at Imàgo have the lit dome of St. Peter's in the window but no stars.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the terrace the Spanish Steps are clear but St. Peter's dome cannot be made out.
phrases.late_night: Anyone up late in a piazza room watches the lit streets and St Peter's dome.
phrases.wet_evening: Whoever has a room over Piazza di Spagna tonight can watch rain fall on the lit square and the wet Spanish Steps.
phrases.grey_evening: Whoever has a room over Piazza di Spagna tonight can watch the streetlights under the cloud, St Peter's dome on the horizon.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, guests in Palace Bosphorus suites see the 15 July Martyrs Bridge as a dark outline over the strait.
phrases.clear_morning: Sunrise puts the 15 July Martyrs Bridge in the windows of Palace Bosphorus rooms; breakfast is set on the waterside terrace.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the marble infinity pool reflects a blue strait, and the red-and-white umbrellas give the only shade on the loungers.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Afternoon sun comes through the arched windows of the guest rooms, with the Asian shore in sharp detail across the water.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the terrace tables have candles, and the city lights across the strait show clearly from the waterside seats.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds break up the morning sky over the Bosphorus, but the bridge still appears in the frame of the Palace Bosphorus terraces.
phrases.partly_afternoon: If you were there this afternoon, you would see cloud shadows moving over the Asian shore from the arched windows.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun lights the pale pink palace façade and the pink flowering trees in the courtyard between passing clouds.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the strait looks grey too, so the red-and-white umbrellas by the outdoor pool are the brightest colour around.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the 200-metre terrace and the outdoor loungers, while the indoor pool under its skylight stays in use.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a thunderstorm the arched windows of the guest rooms give a wide view of lightning over the Asian shore.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides the Asian shore today; from the terrace, only the nearest part of the Bosphorus is visible.
phrases.snow: Snow settles on the loungers and the striped umbrellas, while the indoor pool with its turquoise mosaic floor stays warm.
phrases.very_cold: The outdoor pool area is empty on this very cold day, and guests watch the strait through their arched windows.
phrases.very_hot: In this very hot weather, the loungers under the red-and-white umbrellas are the only ones in use beside the infinity pool.
phrases.mild_night: Mild and cloudy tonight on the 200-metre terrace, where torches are lit and city lights show across the strait.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Low visibility today, so from the guest-room windows the Asian shore is a faint outline and the bridge details are lost.
phrases.late_night: Back from a late dinner, you would see the Asian shore lights across the strait from a Palace Bosphorus room's arched windows.
phrases.wet_evening: If you had a last drink in your room tonight, rain on the arched windows would blur the lights across the Bosphorus.
phrases.grey_evening: If you had a last drink in a Palace Bosphorus room now, you would see the Asian shore lights under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Spanish Steps outside the four rooms are empty, and the Sallustiano Obelisk stands dark against a clear sky.
phrases.clear_morning: From the room windows this morning, Trinità dei Monti is in full sun and the early visitors are on the Spanish Steps.
phrases.clear_midday: Under a clear midday sky, the rooftop terrace is in full sun and the Spanish Steps below are crowded.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: The late sun makes the ochre buildings around the Spanish Steps look warmer in colour, seen from the terrace tables.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would look straight at the Spanish Steps from your room, clear sky above.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds come and go over Trinità dei Monti this morning, and the terrace petunias are in and out of sun.
phrases.partly_afternoon: This afternoon the Spanish Steps are half in shade from passing clouds, watched from the terrace tables with their red placemats.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud leaves patches of light on the ochre buildings facing the terrace.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers Rome today, and the Sallustiano Obelisk looks flat and pale from the room windows.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the Spanish Steps right now, and the terrace tables stand empty while guests watch from inside.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a storm, the room windows give a direct view of lightning over Trinità dei Monti, with no need to go outside.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over Rome today softens the outline of the Sallustiano Obelisk, which is only a short distance from the windows.
phrases.snow: Snow in Rome is rare, but if it fell today, you would see it settle on the Spanish Steps from your room.
phrases.very_cold: On a very cold clear day like this, the terrace is empty and the Spanish Steps are watched from behind glass.
phrases.very_hot: With Rome very hot today, the Spanish Steps are in full sun and the rooms are the cooler place to watch from.
phrases.mild_night: It is a mild cloudy night in Rome, and the terrace dining tables above the Spanish Steps are still in use.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the Spanish Steps and the Obelisk are close enough to see well, but little beyond them.
phrases.late_night: Back from dinner in the dining room, every window shows the Spanish Steps with only a few people left after midnight.
phrases.wet_evening: With the curtain open after midnight, rain runs down the window and the Spanish Steps show wet in the city lights.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight, the curtains in the rooms are open to the Spanish Steps, and haze softens the city lights around the obelisk.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the corner windows of the guest rooms already show the outline of Osorno against a clear sky.
phrases.clear_morning: From the Mirador del Lago this morning, the bay is flat and Osorno stands snow-capped on the far shore.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday under a clear sky, the pool windows show Lake Llanquihue over the Puerto Varas rooftops, with snow on Osorno beyond.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were on the Terraza Ailén now, you would watch the late sun colour the snow on Osorno.
phrases.clear_night: A clear night over Lake Llanquihue, and from the guest-room windows the water is dark and the stars are easy to see.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds move across the far shore this morning, so Osorno appears and disappears from the dining room windows.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Some cloud, some sun on the lake this afternoon; guests on the stone terrace have the volcano about half the time.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun turns the clouds pink above Osorno, as seen from the stone terrace facing the lake.
phrases.overcast: Grey sky today, so there is no volcano, only Lake Llanquihue under the windows of the Mirador del Lago.
phrases.rain: Rain on Lake Llanquihue, and guests in the heated indoor pool watch it fall through the floor-to-ceiling glass.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder over the lake; from the guest-room corner windows, lightning shows above the far shore where Osorno usually stands.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog today hides Osorno completely, and from the indoor pool the lake seems to end somewhere short of the far shore.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on the cedar shingles and on Puerto Varas below, while the indoor pool stays heated behind its glass.
phrases.very_cold: Guests at the corner windows this morning look past frost on the glass to Lake Llanquihue and the snow on Osorno.
phrases.very_hot: Unusually hot for Puerto Varas; on the Terraza Ailén, the lake in front is the only thing that looks cool.
phrases.mild_night: A mild night with cloud over the lake, and the pendant lights of the dining room show in its windows.
phrases.reduced_visibility: From the guest-room windows, Lake Llanquihue shows past the rooftops today, with Osorno hidden in the haze beyond the far shore.
phrases.late_night: Guests in the corner rooms are likely asleep now, wisely, since the window can show Osorno across the lake at dawn.
phrases.wet_evening: Low cloud hides Osorno tonight, so whoever has a corner room watches rain over Lake Llanquihue and the town lights.
phrases.grey_evening: Whoever has a corner room tonight sees the lights of Puerto Varas below and the lake under low cloud, Osorno hidden.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the outline of Mount Agung is already visible from the infinity pool, while the Indian Ocean stays dark.
phrases.clear_morning: From the dining terrace, breakfast comes with a clear view of the green hills, and Mount Agung has no cloud on it.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sun is directly over the infinity pool, and the wicker loungers in the shallow water are the coolest seats.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were in the pool now, you would see Mount Agung and the Indian Ocean together under low sun.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the sky over eastern Bali is clear, and from the bedroom terraces the stars show clearly above the ocean.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds sit around the top of Mount Agung this morning, but the summit shows between them from the infinity pool.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds cross the hillside this afternoon, so the egg-shaped chairs in the pavilion get shade one minute and sun the next.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, the clouds near Mount Agung turn orange, and the infinity pool reflects the same colour.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the Indian Ocean looks grey too, but Mount Agung is still visible from the pool, just without shadows.
phrases.rain: If you were at the infinity pool now, you would see rain falling across the Indian Ocean and Mount Agung.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm is over the ocean right now, and the pool area is empty while lightning is visible from the bedroom windows.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze covers Mount Agung today, so the dual view from the infinity pool is, for now, only the ocean.
phrases.snow: Snow in eastern Bali would be a first; whatever is falling, the infinity pool still faces Mount Agung and the ocean.
phrases.very_cold: Close to freezing is not normal for this hillside, so the wicker loungers in the shallow pool water are empty today.
phrases.very_hot: The air over eastern Bali is very hot today, and the shallow water around the wicker loungers is the most popular place.
phrases.mild_night: A warm, cloudy night in Manggis: no stars from the pool, but the sound of the Indian Ocean below is clear.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so Mount Agung cannot be seen from the pool; the ocean and the near hillside are still visible.
phrases.late_night: The bedroom curtain is left open on purpose, so Mount Agung's outline is visible against the night sky over the sea.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner, rain runs down the bedroom glass, and the outline of Mount Agung shows through it above the hillside.
phrases.grey_evening: After dinner, the bedroom window shows the ocean, and the shape of Mount Agung under a low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Harbour Bridge is still lit against a dark sky, seen from the Harbour View Suites in North Sydney.
phrases.clear_morning: Clear morning light shows the sailboats moored in Lavender Bay from the hotel room windows, with the bridge behind them.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sky is plain blue, and the CBD skyline stands sharp across the water from the Harbour View Suites.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: On the rooftop terrace the late sun is on the steel arch, which turns warm in colour before its lights come on.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the arch is lit up, and guests at LB's Restaurant see it through the floor-to-ceiling windows while they eat.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds sit over the harbour this morning, but the bridge is fully visible from the hotel rooms in North Sydney.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Broken cloud moves over Lavender Bay this afternoon, so the moored sailboats go in and out of sun below the windows.
phrases.partly_golden: If you were on the rooftop terrace now, you would see the last sun on the bridge between patches of cloud.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky today, the steel arch looks darker than usual from the dining room at LB's Restaurant.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on Sydney Harbour, and guests watch it from behind the floor-to-ceiling windows of the restaurant, not the rooftop.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm is over the harbour, and from the Harbour View Suites the bridge appears for a moment with each flash.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hangs over the harbour today, and from the hotel rooms the CBD skyline is a faint outline behind the bridge.
phrases.snow: Snow almost never reaches Sydney, but if it did today, guests in the Harbour View Suites would watch it over the bridge.
phrases.very_cold: It is unusually cold for Sydney, so the rooftop seating stands empty and guests look at the arch from indoors.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot air sits over Sydney, and the potted trees on the rooftop terrace give only small patches of shade.
phrases.mild_night: On this mild cloudy night, the lit arch shows clearly from the rooftop terrace seating, with no stars above it.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the bridge still shows from the hotel rooms but the CBD skyline behind it does not.
phrases.late_night: Near midnight, a glass of water in a Harbour View Suite comes with the steel arch across the harbour lights.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the Harbour View Suite windows after midnight, and the Bridge's arch blurs above the lights on the water.
phrases.grey_evening: Low cloud moves across the harbour after midnight, and from the Harbour View Suites the bridge arch shows against the city lights.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Arts Centre spire is still lit against a dark clear sky from the Diplomatic Suite corner window.
phrases.clear_morning: From the Grand Suite King, the floor-to-ceiling windows show the Melbourne skyline sharp and clear this morning.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sun is high over the Yarra River, and the Diplomatic Suite window has the full skyline in clear light.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun lights the Arts Centre spire and the river, both visible from the Diplomatic Suite corner window right now.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in the lounge bar tonight, you would see the lit CBD skyline sharp under a clear sky.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit over the Melbourne skyline this morning, with the Yarra River in sun from the corner window.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Guests on the 31st floor Grand Club watch cloud shadows move across the skyline in all directions this afternoon.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud turns orange above the Arts Centre spire, seen from the hotel's windows.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the skyline looks flat today, though the Yarra River is easy to see from the Diplomatic Suite.
phrases.rain: Rain is running down the floor-to-ceiling windows of the marble bathroom, and the city skyline is grey behind it.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the Melbourne skyline is visible from every side of the 31st floor Grand Club during this storm.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides the top of the Arts Centre spire today, and the skyline is only partly visible from the corner window.
phrases.snow: Snow almost never falls in Melbourne, but if it did today, the indoor pool and sauna would stay warm.
phrases.very_cold: A rare near-freezing day in Melbourne, and the clear air makes the Yarra River and skyline very sharp from the corner window.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot over Melbourne today, and heat shimmer softens the far edge of the skyline seen from the 31st floor.
phrases.mild_night: On a mild cloudy night, the lit skyline shows through the two windows of a guest room, Arts Centre spire included.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Low visibility today: the far edges of the Melbourne skyline are missing, though the nearby Yarra River remains in view.
phrases.late_night: A glass of water around midnight in the Diplomatic Suite, and the corner window shows city lights on the Yarra River.
phrases.wet_evening: Back from dinner after midnight, the Diplomatic Suite's corner window shows the skyline lights blurred by rain over the Yarra.
phrases.grey_evening: After dinner, the Diplomatic Suite's corner window frames the Yarra and the lit CBD skyline under a low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Horseshoe Falls is still just a pale shape from a Falls View corner suite window.
phrases.clear_morning: Breakfast guests have waffles with both falls in full daylight through the floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the spray over the Horseshoe Falls is bright white, seen from the rooftop pool terrace.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Low afternoon sun lights the American Falls on the left side of a corner suite balcony door.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight diners at Massimo's look out at the falls lit in blue under a clear sky.
phrases.partly_morning: If you were in the soaking tub this morning, you would see clouds moving over the Niagara River gorge.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over the falls this afternoon, and from the rooftop bar the water changes from grey to white.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, the hydrotherapy tub at Christienne Spa gives a view of both falls under broken cloud.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky sits over Niagara today, and the falls look flat and white from the corner suites.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the Juliette balconies, and the spray from the Horseshoe Falls is hard to tell from the weather.
phrases.thunderstorm: During the storm, guests watch lightning over the Niagara River gorge from behind the floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.fog_haze: If you were at a Falls View corner suite window now, you would see fog hiding most of the Horseshoe Falls.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling past the suite windows, and the parkland behind the falls has turned white.
phrases.very_cold: On a day this cold, the spray freezes along the edges of the gorge, visible from the high-floor suites.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot outside, so most guests are in the rooftop pool, with the Horseshoe Falls straight ahead.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night, and the Juliette balcony doors stay open to the sound of the falls.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the Horseshoe Falls still shows from the suites but the far side of the gorge does not.
phrases.late_night: A glass of water near midnight, and in the corner suite window the Horseshoe Falls shows white and blue.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner at Massimo's, rain runs down the Falls View suite glass, and the Horseshoe Falls shows as white spray behind it.
phrases.grey_evening: Dinner at Massimo's is over, and after midnight the corner suite's window frames the Horseshoe Falls' white water under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, guests on the oceanfront balconies can see the sky over the Atlantic slowly turning pale.
phrases.clear_morning: Over breakfast time, the sun sits low over the Atlantic and the wide sandy beach is still almost empty.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the outdoor lazy river is the busiest place, with the Atlantic bright blue under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were on a high balcony now, you would see the sand turn golden while the Atlantic stays blue.
phrases.clear_night: The fire pit is lit, and from the terrace the Atlantic is only a dark line with a few stars above it.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over the Atlantic this morning, and from the balconies the light on the beach changes every few minutes.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the balcony this afternoon, cloud shadows move over the wide sand and the blue Atlantic.
phrases.partly_golden: From a balcony chair right now, broken clouds over the Atlantic show orange and pink edges as the sun drops.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky sits over the Atlantic today, and the ocean-view fitness center has a flat, even light for a workout.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the beach, so guests have moved to the indoor pool and the indoor lazy river.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the Atlantic is best watched from behind the sliding glass doors of the suites, not from the balconies.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over the water today means the Atlantic is visible from the balconies, but without a clear horizon.
phrases.snow: Snow on Myrtle Beach is rare, but the sand looks pale from the balconies and the indoor pool is the obvious choice.
phrases.very_cold: The air outside is very cold today, so the beach chairs sit empty and guests watch the Atlantic through the suite windows.
phrases.very_hot: Under a very hot sun, the sun deck is quiet and most guests are in the outdoor pool or the lazy river.
phrases.mild_night: Tonight is mild and cloudy, so the terrace fireplace is lit and the Atlantic is more heard than seen.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Today the Atlantic horizon is hidden, and from the balconies only the sand and the nearest water are sharp.
phrases.late_night: Night surf shows white through the suite's sliding doors, easy to watch longer.
phrases.wet_evening: After midnight, rain runs down the sliding glass doors of the oceanfront suites, and the Boardwalk lights blur along the beach.
phrases.grey_evening: Clouds hang over the Atlantic after midnight, and through the open suite curtains the Boardwalk lights line the beach toward the SkyWheel.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the ocean off the Kuta Peninsula is still dark, and the private pools lie quiet outside each villa.
phrases.clear_morning: If you were there this morning, you would see the whole southern coast from an Ocean Villa pool, with no cloud anywhere.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sun is directly over the villas, and most guests stay in their private pools rather than on the terraces.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: The late sun is dropping toward the Indian Ocean, and the tables at cliff-top Akasa have the long Uluwatu sunset view.
phrases.clear_night: Under a clear sky tonight, the fire pit at the beachfront lounge gives the brightest light near the dark ocean.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit over the Kuta Peninsula this morning, but the sea below the Sunset Villas is still bright blue.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over the lagoon pool this afternoon, so swimmers get short periods of shade between stretches of strong sun.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, the clouds over the Indian Ocean turn orange, best seen from a Sunset Villa pool.
phrases.overcast: Grey cloud covers the whole coast today, so the ocean from the villas looks flat and silver rather than turquoise.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the private pools and the gardens, and guests watch the grey sea from inside their villas.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm is over the Indian Ocean right now, and lightning shows up well from the cliff-top terraces when it strikes.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hangs over the southern coast, and the far end of the Kuta Peninsula is hard to make out from the villas.
phrases.snow: Guests at the beachfront lounge after midnight watch snow fall into the fire pit glow beside the Indian Ocean.
phrases.very_cold: From the cliff-top Akasa terrace, the Indian Ocean lies in hard cold daylight past the empty dining tables.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot afternoon like this one, the private pool is the most comfortable spot outside each villa before dusk.
phrases.mild_night: Clouds hide the stars tonight, but the air is warm, and dinner tables on the Akasa terrace are set as usual.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Guests at the villa pools today look out on the near sea only, with the far coast lost in low visibility.
phrases.late_night: After a late dinner at Akasa, the Ocean Villas face the Indian Ocean, and white surf shows along the coast after midnight.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the glass of the Ocean Villas tonight, and the Indian Ocean shows grey under low cloud at dusk.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight the cloud hangs low over the Indian Ocean, and the surf shows white from the Ocean Villas.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the harbor outside the balconies is still dark and quiet, with no boats passing yet.
phrases.clear_morning: From the upper canal-side rooms, the church spires of Christianshavn stand sharp in the clear morning light.
phrases.clear_midday: From a canal-side balcony, boats pass close on the harbor under a clear midday sky toward Christianshavn.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun reaches the harbor-facing balconies, and the glass buildings across the canal turn orange for an hour.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in a corner suite tonight, you would see the lights of boats moving slowly along the dark harbor.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds drift over the harbor this morning, and the restaurant tables by the windows get sun one minute, shade the next.
phrases.partly_afternoon: On the balconies, two chairs face a harbor where patches of sun move across the water between slow clouds.
phrases.partly_golden: The last sun slips between clouds and lands on the church spires, seen from the upper canal-side rooms.
phrases.overcast: Under a flat grey sky, the harbor looks like metal from the balconies, and the boats pass without shadows.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the harbor and the wooden dock, while guests watch the boats from behind the restaurant windows.
phrases.thunderstorm: A storm sits over Copenhagen, and from the corner suite windows lightning shows the harbor for a second at a time.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides Christianshavn and its spires today; from the balconies only the nearest boats and the dock are visible.
phrases.snow: Snow falls on the wooden dock and the balcony chairs, and the harbor water stays dark and open below.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air over the harbor today; from the upper canal-side rooms the spires and glass buildings look unusually sharp.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot day, the outdoor pool with its harbor water is the busiest spot at the hotel.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night over the harbor; a few guests sit out on the balconies and watch late boats pass.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today, so the church spires across the harbor are not visible; only the nearest boats still are.
phrases.late_night: In the sleeping hours, harbour lights shine on the water outside the corner suite, and the church spires come back at dawn.
phrases.wet_evening: Curtains open in a canal-side room after midnight, rain runs down the glass and the city lights blur across the harbour.
phrases.grey_evening: With the curtains open after midnight in a canal-side room, the city lights show under low cloud across the harbour water.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Gulf around the overwater villas is dark and flat, with no mainland lights anywhere in view.
phrases.clear_morning: From the spa treatment room windows, the morning sea is bright turquoise and completely calm under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the white sand beach is very bright, and most guests are under the thatched umbrellas or in the water.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun reaches across the infinity pool on the overwater terrace, and the blue pergola makes long shadows on the loungers.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in a floating villa tonight, you would see stars on every side and no city glow at all.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds sit over the Gulf this morning, and the padel court is already busy before the heat arrives.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over the island this afternoon, so the lagoon pool is sometimes in sun and sometimes in shade.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, the clouds over the water turn orange, seen from the wooden loungers on the beach.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers the whole Gulf today, and from the overwater villas the sea looks grey too, still calm.
phrases.rain: Rain is rare in Doha, but today it falls on the island, and the spa treatment room windows show a wet sea.
