phrases.late_night: After midnight the shore lights across Lake Zurich reflect in the water, and the window of room 304 is hard to leave.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner at La Muña, rain runs down the glass in the lake-view rooms, and shore lights blur across Lake Zurich.
phrases.grey_evening: Dinner at La Muña is finished, and from room 304 the shore lights reflect in Lake Zurich under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the corner window of a City room already shows Kyoto Tower's white spire against a dark, clear sky.
phrases.clear_morning: From the river-room balconies, the Higashiyama mountains stand sharp behind the Kamo River while breakfast is served upstairs.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday, full sun falls on the Sky Forest Garden, and the low Shimogyo rooftops look flat and bright from the railing.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were on the rooftop terrace now, you would see low afternoon light on the Higashiyama mountains across the river.
phrases.clear_night: Kyoto Tower is lit tonight, and the City rooms' corner window frames it against a clear, dark sky over Shimogyo.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over the Higashiyama mountains this morning, and breakfast on the Sky Forest Garden alternates between sun and shade.
phrases.partly_afternoon: This afternoon, cloud shadows move across the Shimogyo rooftops, and Kyoto Tower's white spire goes bright, then dull, from the corner window.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud takes some colour over the Higashiyama mountains, seen from the rooftop with sunset drinks.
phrases.overcast: Under a flat grey sky, the Kamo River below the river-room balconies looks dull, and the mountains are a plain dark line.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the Kamo River today, so guests sit in the Genji Lounge and watch the Zen garden get wet.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a thunderstorm the rooftop Sky Forest Garden is empty, and from the river rooms lightning shows over the Higashiyama mountains.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog over Shimogyo today hides Kyoto Tower from the City rooms, leaving only the nearest rooftops in the corner window.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on Kyoto, and from the river-room balconies the Higashiyama mountains turn white above the Kamo River.
phrases.very_cold: It feels close to freezing outside, so the rooftop wicker chairs stay empty and guests take breakfast quickly before going back inside.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot Kyoto afternoon, the rooftop wicker chairs stand empty, and guests watch Kyoto Tower from inside the City rooms.
phrases.mild_night: A mild, cloudy night, and the river-room balconies over the Kamogawa are a comfortable place to sit with the window open.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low, so from the river rooms the Kamo River is clear but the Higashiyama mountains are only a faint shape.
phrases.late_night: The City rooms' curtain is left open on purpose tonight, Kyoto Tower's white spire in the corner window above the lit rooftops.
phrases.wet_evening: The curtain is open late in a City room, and through the rain Kyoto Tower's white spire shows above the lit rooftops.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight, with the curtain open, the City rooms' corner window shows Kyoto Tower's spire against low cloud over the lit rooftops.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the docked boats in the marina sit still under a clear sky, seen from the Waterfront View King windows.
phrases.clear_morning: From the Waterfront View King rooms, docked boats sit on the Washington Channel under a clear morning sky.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sun is high over the Washington Channel, and the sage green umbrellas give shade to the teak chairs.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: As the sun drops, guests at Whiskey Charlie on the roof look over the Washington Channel to the monuments.
phrases.clear_night: Up on the rooftop terrace, the fire feature is lit and the city skyline stands out against a clear night sky.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds, some sun over the marina this morning, and the boats are easy to see from the Waterfront View King rooms.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Under partly cloudy skies, the terrace with its sage green umbrellas has a clear look at the Potomac River this afternoon.
phrases.partly_golden: If you were at Whiskey Charlie now, you would see the last sun light up the clouds over the monuments.
phrases.overcast: If you stood at a floor-to-ceiling window now, you would see flat grey cloud over the Potomac River and the marina.
phrases.rain: If you were at a Waterfront View King window now, you would see rain dotting the Washington Channel around the docked boats.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the Potomac River is best watched from behind the floor-to-ceiling windows, not from the rooftop terrace.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog sits over the Washington Channel today, so the docked boats near the hotel are visible but the monuments are not.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on the marina, and the teak chairs on the terrace are collecting a thin white layer.
phrases.very_cold: It is very cold outside today, so the view of the Washington Channel is best taken from a Waterfront View King room.
phrases.very_hot: The Wharf is very hot this afternoon, and the sage green umbrellas are the only shade on the terrace.
phrases.mild_night: Tonight is mild under cloud, and guests sit by the lit fire feature on the rooftop terrace facing the city skyline.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today: the boats in the marina are clear from the windows, but the monuments across the water are not.
phrases.late_night: With the room lights off in a Waterfront View King, you would see only the boat lights on the Washington Channel.
phrases.wet_evening: If you were at Whiskey Charlie for a last drink tonight, rain on the glass would blur the lights along the Potomac.
phrases.grey_evening: Back from Whiskey Charlie in a Waterfront View King room, you would see the marina lights on the Potomac under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Royal Floor balconies on the 12th floor already show both falls as grey shapes under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_morning: Breakfast in the Rainbow Room has a clear view of Horseshoe Falls and its mist rising in full sun.
phrases.clear_midday: From the Fallsview rooms at midday, a tour boat is visible below Horseshoe Falls, and the mist is bright white.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun reaches the brick terrace, where guests in rattan chairs watch the mist over Horseshoe Falls turn orange.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the American and Horseshoe Falls are lit blue, and diners at Prime Steakhouse see them through panoramic windows.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over Niagara Falls this morning, and the Horseshoe Falls view from the king rooms changes with each gap of sun.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Afternoon tea in the Fallsview Tea Room comes with a mixed sky behind both falls and sunlight on the water at moments.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, clouds over the 11th-floor balconies take some colour while the Horseshoe Falls mist stays visible.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers both falls today, and from the Royal Floor rooms the mist is hard to tell from the cloud.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the open Fallsview Balconies, so guests watch Horseshoe Falls from inside the floor-to-ceiling windows instead.
phrases.thunderstorm: If you were there during this storm, you would see lightning over the American Falls from a Prime Steakhouse table.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog mixes with the falls' own mist today, and from the 12th-floor balconies the Horseshoe Falls is only a pale shape.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on Niagara Falls, and the indoor walkway to Christienne Fallsview Spa means nobody needs a coat.
phrases.very_cold: The air outside is well below freezing, so the Fallsview Balconies stay empty and the falls are watched through the window.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot day, the mist reaching the 11th-floor balconies from both falls is the most welcome thing in Niagara.
phrases.mild_night: The night is warm enough to sit out on a Royal Floor balcony under cloud and watch the blue-lit falls.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low, so from the Fallsview rooms both falls appear softened and the tour boat below is hard to make out.
phrases.late_night: Whoever has a Royal Floor room tonight has turned the lights out, and the room now takes its light from the falls.
phrases.wet_evening: After midnight, rain runs down the Royal Floor windows, and any guest awake there watches Horseshoe Falls through the wet glass.
phrases.grey_evening: Anyone awake after midnight on the Royal Floor can watch low cloud pass over the Horseshoe Falls, spray rising white into it.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the balcony chairs outside the Boutique Sea View rooms face a dark, quiet Llandudno Bay.
phrases.clear_morning: Breakfast in the on-site restaurant comes with a clear view of the water and the promenade this morning.
phrases.clear_midday: Under a clear sky, the binoculars by the window let guests pick out details on the Great Orme headland.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun falls on the wicker chairs of the balcony, and the headland turns a deeper green before sunset.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would see stars over Llandudno Bay from the seafront terrace, and a quiet promenade below.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds drift over Llandudno Bay this morning, and the French doors of the Sea View rooms stand open to the terrace.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the iron balcony, the afternoon view mixes patches of sun and shadow across the water toward the Great Orme.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun lights the bay in stripes between clouds, best watched from a wicker chair on the balcony.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky sits over the promenade today, so the water in front of the terrace looks grey too.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the promenade, and guests watch it through the French doors of the Boutique Sea View rooms.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder over Llandudno Bay keeps the terrace empty, while the storm is easier to follow from inside the restaurant.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides the Great Orme headland today, and from the window the binoculars only show the nearest part of the promenade.
phrases.snow: Snow is settling on the promenade and the iron balcony railing, an unusual sight from the Sea View rooms.
phrases.very_cold: On a day close to freezing, the wicker chairs on the balcony stay empty and the bay is watched from indoors.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot weather for Llandudno, and the seafront terrace gets whatever breeze comes in off the bay.
phrases.mild_night: A mild night under cloud lets guests leave the French doors open and hear the water from the Sea View rooms.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the Great Orme headland is not clear from the balcony, though the promenade and nearby water are.
phrases.late_night: The Boutique Sea View rooms face Llandudno Bay, where the promenade lights show on the water after midnight.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the Boutique Sea View windows after midnight, and the promenade lights look wet and blurred along Llandudno Bay.
phrases.grey_evening: Cloud moves slowly over Llandudno Bay after midnight, and the promenade lights show on the water from the Boutique Sea View rooms.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Penthouse terrace is empty and St Stephen's spire stands dark against a clear sky over Vienna.
phrases.clear_morning: Clear morning light reaches the Opera façade, and from the suites' tall windows the Ringstrasse has no cloud above it.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the white parasol on the rooftop terrace is in use, and the Steffl is sharp over the rooftops.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: From the seventh-floor terrace, low afternoon sun lights the spire of St Stephen's Cathedral above the rooftops under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would see the illuminated State Opera from your window under a clear, dark Vienna sky.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds move over the Ringstrasse this morning, and the Opera façade is in sun one moment, shade the next.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the Penthouse terrace this afternoon, St Stephen's spire stands between broken clouds, with a few patches of blue sky.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, guests on the lower floors see the Albertina's neoclassical profile under a half-covered sky.
phrases.overcast: From the Penthouse rooftop terrace, St Stephen's spire stands dark against a low grey sky over the Vienna rooftops.
phrases.rain: Rain on Philharmonikerstrasse today, so the wicker seats on the rooftop terrace are wet and guests sit in the Grüne Bar.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder sounds over the Ringstrasse, and from the suite windows the Opera façade shows up briefly in each flash of lightning.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hangs over Vienna today, and from the Penthouse terrace St Stephen's spire is only a faint outline, if visible at all.
phrases.snow: Snow is settling on the wicker seats of the rooftop terrace, and the Opera roof across the street is turning white.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air outside, so the Penthouse terrace stays empty and guests watch the Opera façade from behind tall suite windows.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot afternoon, the white parasol on the rooftop terrace is the only shade with a view of the Steffl.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night in Vienna, and the illuminated Opera on Opernring is the brightest thing seen from the suite windows.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the Penthouse terrace the near Opera is clear but St Stephen's spire is hard to see.
phrases.late_night: After midnight, St Stephen's spire shows above the lit rooftops from the Penthouse windows, and there is no hurry to turn away.
phrases.wet_evening: With the curtain open past midnight, rain streaks the Penthouse glass and the cathedral spire shows above the wet lit rooftops.
phrases.grey_evening: With the Penthouse curtains open after midnight, the Steffl's spire is visible above the lit rooftops under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, through the floor-to-ceiling windows, the North Shore Mountains stand as a dark outline against a clear paling sky.
phrases.clear_morning: From a -01 suite above the 20th floor, the sun lights the North Shore Mountains and BC Place's dome in one frame.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday, guests in the 17th-floor spa recline in pod-like chairs facing a clear view across Vancouver.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: The wedge-tower corner suites get the late sun now, with the North Shore Mountains and False Creek in the curved windows.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight Science World's sphere glows against a clear sky, and many rooms have it framed in their floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over the North Shore Mountains this morning, and guests in the -01 suites can still see most peaks.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Patches of sun and shadow move across False Creek this afternoon, easy to follow from the suite living areas.
phrases.partly_golden: If you were in a corner suite for the last hour of sun, clouds would turn orange above BC Place's dome.
phrases.overcast: Under a full grey sky, the North Shore Mountains look flat and dull from the suites, with False Creek closer and clearer.
phrases.rain: Rain streaks the floor-to-ceiling windows, and the soaking tub beside them is a reasonable place to watch the wet skyline.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the North Shore Mountains shows clearly from the corner suites, where the 270-degree view covers most of the storm.
phrases.fog_haze: Today's fog removes the North Shore Mountains from the view, leaving the -01 suites with BC Place's dome and nearby towers.
phrases.snow: Snow falls over downtown Vancouver, and guests at the 17th-floor spa watch it from the pod-like chairs by the windows.
phrases.very_cold: Close to freezing outside, the air is very clear, and the North Shore Mountains look sharp from the suites' curved windows.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot for Vancouver today, and the North Shore Mountains stay plainly visible from the -01 suites through the strong afternoon light.
phrases.mild_night: A mild night under cloud, and from the suite windows the city lights and Science World's glowing sphere stand out.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the North Shore Mountains are missing from the suite windows while BC Place's dome remains clear.
phrases.late_night: Whoever has an -01 suite tonight sleeps with the lights off, city glow toward the North Shore Mountains the only light left.
phrases.wet_evening: After midnight, anyone awake in an -01 suite watches rain cross the glass, city lights spread out toward the North Shore Mountains.
phrases.grey_evening: Anyone awake in an -01 suite tonight watches low cloud cover the North Shore Mountains, the False Creek lights showing beneath it.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Eiffel Tower is already a clear dark shape from the Penthouse windows, and the rooftop bar is still closed.
phrases.clear_morning: Breakfast trays with croissants go out to the upper floors, where the Eiffel Tower stands sharp against a clean blue sky.
phrases.clear_midday: Under a cloudless midday sky, the rooftop restaurant has every table in bright sun and the Paris rooftops show every detail.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: On the 7th-floor rooftop, the sunset crowd is already in place, and the Eiffel Tower turns orange above the Paris rooftops.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the Eiffel Tower is lit against a clear black sky, and guests on the heated terrace keep their coats on.
phrases.partly_morning: From the Exclusive Eiffel Suite this morning, a few white clouds pass behind the Eiffel Tower, and the armchairs face the window.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over Paris this afternoon, and from the rooftop the Eiffel Tower is in sun one minute, shade the next.
phrases.partly_golden: If you were on the balcony now, you would see the last sun colour the clouds behind the Eiffel Tower.
phrases.overcast: Guests on the rooftop terrace today see the Eiffel Tower above the grey Paris roofs under low cloud.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the Paris rooftops, and most guests watch the wet Eiffel Tower through the restaurant's floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm is over the city, the rooftop terrace is empty, and the Eiffel Tower shows up more clearly with each flash.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hangs over Paris today, so from the suite windows the Eiffel Tower is only a faint grey shape.
phrases.snow: From the seventh-floor rooftop, snow falls over the Paris rooftops and the Eiffel Tower rises grey above them.
phrases.very_cold: From the 7th-floor rooftop, the Eiffel Tower stands over Paris in hard winter light, with the heated terrace empty.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot Paris afternoon, the red curtains in the rooms stay drawn, and the Eiffel Tower shimmers in the heat.
phrases.mild_night: If you were on the seventh-floor rooftop now, you would see the Eiffel Tower lit beneath low night cloud over Paris.
phrases.reduced_visibility: From the balcony's red bistro table, the nearest roofs are clear, but the Eiffel Tower is only a dim outline today.
phrases.late_night: Past midnight, back from a cocktail on the seventh-floor rooftop, the Exclusive Eiffel Suite windows show the tower above the city lights.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the Exclusive Eiffel Suite window after midnight, the curtain open on wet city lights around the Eiffel Tower.
phrases.grey_evening: Curtains apart in the Penthouse, the Eiffel Tower rises over Paris lights under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the suite windows on the Prime Ocean View floors show Diamond Head as a dark shape against the sky.
phrases.clear_morning: From a balcony table, the morning view takes in Fort DeRussy Park, Waikiki Beach and a clear Pacific horizon.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the ocean below the floor-to-ceiling windows is turquoise, and Diamond Head stands sharp without a cloud near it.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon sun lights the palm trees and sandy beach below the balconies, with the Pacific horizon still clear.
phrases.clear_night: If you were on a balcony tonight, you would see a clear sky over the dark Pacific and the Waikiki shoreline.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit over the ocean this morning, seen from the suite living rooms above Fort DeRussy Park.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over Diamond Head this afternoon, and the beach below the tower changes between shade and sun.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, guests on west-facing balconies watch the clouds over the Pacific turn orange.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky, Waikiki Beach and Diamond Head are still fully visible from the upper floors, just with flatter colours.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on Fort DeRussy Park, and the full kitchens in the suites get more use than the balconies today.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm is over the Pacific, so the balcony chairs are empty and lightning is watched through the floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over the water today makes Diamond Head look faint from the ocean-view suites, though Waikiki Beach below stays clear.
phrases.snow: Snow over Waikiki Beach would be a historic event; from the balconies, palm trees and sand are still the normal view.
phrases.very_cold: If it ever felt close to freezing in Honolulu, guests would watch Diamond Head from inside the suites rather than the balconies.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot over Waikiki today, so the shaded balcony chairs get more use than the sandy beach below them.
phrases.mild_night: On this warm cloudy night, guests at the balcony tables look out at the dark Pacific with no stars above it.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so Diamond Head is hard to make out; Waikiki Beach and Fort DeRussy Park below are still clear.
phrases.late_night: Up for water after midnight on a Prime Ocean View floor, you would see the Waikiki Beach lights ending at Diamond Head.
phrases.wet_evening: With a last drink in an ocean-view suite, you would see rain on the glass and Waikiki's lights toward Diamond Head.
phrases.grey_evening: If you had a last drink by a Prime Ocean View window now, you would see the Waikiki shoreline lights under cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the street lamps of Gran Vía are still on, and from the balconies the Metrópolis dome is a dark shape.
phrases.clear_morning: Morning sun lights the gilded dome of the Metrópolis Building, clearly visible from the room balconies above Gran Vía.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the Royal Palace and the tree-lined plaza stand in full sun, as seen from the desk in the palace-facing rooms.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun turns the red-tiled rooftops orange, and the two white chairs on the rooftop terrace point straight at them.
phrases.clear_night: After midnight, the lights along Gran Vía glow below the room balcony under a clear night sky.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over Madrid this morning, so the light on the skyline outside the 8th-floor pool windows changes every few minutes.
phrases.partly_afternoon: This afternoon the sun comes and goes over Plaza España, and guests on the balconies see it in short bright patches.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, some red-tiled rooftops below the terrace are lit and others are in cloud shadow.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers Madrid today, but the Royal Palace is still clearly visible from the desk in the room.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on Gran Vía today, and the drops run down the skylights above the indoor lap pool on the 8th floor.
phrases.thunderstorm: If you were in the Somos restaurant right now, you would see the lightning over Gran Vía through full-height glass.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog sits over Madrid, and from the rooftop terrace only the nearest red-tiled rooftops can be made out.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on Madrid, a rare sight, and from the balconies the Metrópolis dome is slowly turning white.
phrases.very_cold: From a front window now, you would see Gran Vía below in hard winter light, the terrace chairs empty.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot air hangs over the red-tiled rooftops this afternoon, and the rooftop terrace chairs stand in direct sun.
phrases.mild_night: Under a mild cloudy night sky, the lit Gran Vía runs below the balconies toward the gilded dome of the Metrópolis Building.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so Plaza España below the rooms is clear but the far end of the Madrid skyline is not.
phrases.late_night: In a room facing Gran Vía, the curtain stays open on purpose, and the avenue's lights reach the bed until sleep comes.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner at Somos, the room window shows Gran Vía wet in the rain, the avenue lights blurred on the glass.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight, long after dinner at Somos, the rooms look down on Gran Vía lit under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the water of Puget Sound shows as a dark flat shape from the corner Elliot Bay suites.
phrases.clear_morning: From the fitness center treadmills, the first ferries cross Elliott Bay under a clear sky this morning.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday under a clear sky, the Olympic Mountains stand sharp beyond Elliott Bay from the fourth-floor infinity pool.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: From the fourth-floor infinity pool, the Olympic Mountains stand in low afternoon sun under a clear sky across Elliott Bay.
phrases.clear_night: The pool terrace firepit is lit, and guests with cocktails can see the Great Wheel turning over Elliott Bay.
phrases.partly_morning: From the fourth-floor pool terrace, Elliott Bay lies under patches of morning cloud, with the Great Wheel on the horizon.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Some cloud, some sun over Elliott Bay this afternoon, and the lounge chairs by the infinity pool are mostly taken.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, clouds break up the light on Elliott Bay, seen from the pool terrace.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky, Elliott Bay lies flat and pale beyond the fourth-floor infinity pool and the Great Wheel.
phrases.rain: Rain runs down the floor-to-ceiling windows of the corner Elliot Bay suites, and the ferry crosses Elliott Bay anyway.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm over Elliott Bay has emptied the pool terrace, and guests watch the lightning from the corner Elliot Bay suites.
phrases.fog_haze: If you were at the fourth-floor pool terrace now, you would see midday fog over Elliott Bay and no Great Wheel.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on the pool terrace umbrellas, and Elliott Bay is grey behind them, a rare sight for Seattle.
phrases.very_cold: From the fourth-floor pool terrace, frost edges the empty lounge chairs above Elliott Bay in hard winter light.
phrases.very_hot: A very hot afternoon in Seattle, which is unusual, and the fourth-floor infinity pool is the busiest place in the hotel.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night, and guests at the pool terrace firepit watch the lit Great Wheel over Elliott Bay.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the Olympic Mountains are not visible from the infinity pool, only the near water of Elliott Bay.
phrases.late_night: The only light left in an Elliott Bay suite after midnight comes from ferry lights moving across the water.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the Elliott Bay suite windows after midnight, and the waterfront lights along Puget Sound blur behind it.
phrases.grey_evening: Haze drifts over Elliott Bay in the small hours, and the waterfront lights look soft from the Elliot Bay suites.

phrases.clear_predawn: Dark water fills Victoria Harbour before sunrise, and Kowloon lights are still on when seen from a 30th-floor suite window.

phrases.clear_midday: At midday the outdoor deck of Sugar on the 32nd floor is in full sun, with Lion Rock clearly visible beyond Kowloon.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were on the Sugar deck now, you would see low sun on the Kowloon skyline and the hills behind it.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the high-floor rooms look out on a lit Kowloon skyline across Victoria Harbour, with no cloud over the hills.
phrases.partly_morning: Scattered clouds pass over Victoria Harbour this morning, and from the 30th-floor suites the Kowloon side is visible under them.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Guests on the outdoor deck at Sugar get sun and shade in turns this afternoon as clouds cross Lion Rock.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun turns the broken cloud over Kowloon pink, seen through the glass railings of the rooftop bar.
phrases.overcast: A flat grey cloud layer sits over Victoria Harbour today, so the 32nd-floor deck gets the view but no sun.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on Victoria Harbour, so the tapas at Sugar are being eaten indoors rather than on the outdoor deck.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over Kowloon can be watched from the 30th-floor harbour-view suites, behind glass, while the outdoor deck stays empty.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over Victoria Harbour today makes the Kowloon skyline a faint outline from the rooftop bar, and Lion Rock is hidden.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare in Hong Kong, but a few flakes over Victoria Harbour would be seen best from the 32nd-floor deck.
phrases.very_cold: Guests in the 30th-floor suites look across Victoria Harbour to Kowloon this morning, the deck at Sugar empty in the cold.
phrases.very_hot: From the 32nd-floor deck at Sugar, the Kowloon skyline across Victoria Harbour looks blurred in the midday heat-haze.
phrases.mild_night: It is a mild cloudy night in Quarry Bay, and guests with cocktails at Sugar see Kowloon lights but no stars.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low, so from the 30th-floor suites the near harbour water is clear but Lion Rock and far Kowloon are not.
phrases.late_night: Near midnight in a 30th-floor harbour suite, a glass of water comes with the Kowloon lights across Victoria Harbour.
phrases.wet_evening: After midnight, rain runs down the harbour-view suite windows, and the Kowloon lights blur across Victoria Harbour.
phrases.grey_evening: Up in the 30th-floor harbour suites after dinner, the Kowloon lights come through low cloud across Victoria Harbour.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Writers Room terrace is empty and the CN Tower lights still show over the dark financial district.
phrases.clear_morning: From a king room, the green tree canopy below is lit by low sun, with the downtown towers sharp beyond it.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the floor-to-ceiling glass on the 17th floor shows the CN Tower in full daylight, no haze anywhere.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun now hits the west side of the CN Tower, seen from the south-facing suites above Avenue Road.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would see the CN Tower fully lit from a lounge chair on the Writers Room terrace.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds pass over the financial district this morning, and the king room windows show the tree canopy in changing light.
phrases.partly_afternoon: This afternoon the CN Tower moves between sun and cloud shadow, which is easy to follow from the Writers Room bar.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud turns pink behind the CN Tower, seen through the Writers Room windows.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the downtown towers look flat from the 17th floor, and the CN Tower is still clear to see.
phrases.rain: Rain runs down the floor-to-ceiling glass of the Writers Room, and the terrace lounge chairs sit wet and empty.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a storm, guests inside the Writers Room can watch lightning over the financial district, with nobody out on the terrace.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides the top of the CN Tower today, so the 17th floor view stops at the nearer downtown towers.
phrases.snow: Snow falls on the Writers Room terrace, and from inside the bar the CN Tower appears grey behind the flakes.
phrases.very_cold: On a very cold clear day, the air over Toronto is sharp and the CN Tower stands out from south-facing suites.
phrases.very_hot: Toronto is very hot this afternoon, and the lounge chairs on the Writers Room terrace sit in full sun.
phrases.mild_night: On a mild cloudy night the Writers Room terrace lanterns are lit, and the CN Tower lights show under the low cloud.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the 17th floor the CN Tower is a faint outline and the far towers are missing.
phrases.late_night: After midnight, the CN Tower's outline above the lit downtown is reason enough to stay up.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner at Joni, a south-facing suite shows the CN Tower through rain on the glass, over the lit downtown.
phrases.grey_evening: After a late dinner at Joni, the south-facing suites face the CN Tower's spire under low cloud, the downtown lit beneath it.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the White House façade is still floodlit, and the balconies facing the North Lawn are empty and quiet.
phrases.clear_morning: Breakfast at the Lafayette is under way, and from the balconies the Washington Monument stands clear behind the North Lawn.
phrases.clear_midday: Under a clear midday sky, the rooftop terrace gives a direct look at the White House and the Monument above the trees.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were on the rooftop terrace now, you would see low sun on the Washington Monument above the treeline.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the White House façade is floodlit, and rooms facing Lafayette Square have the clearest look at it.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds pass over the Monument this morning, while guests in the Lafayette restaurant finish their power breakfast.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds come and go over Washington this afternoon, so the North Lawn below the balconies is sometimes sunny, sometimes shaded.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud sits above the Washington Monument, and the rooftop terrace has guests with drinks.
phrases.overcast: The sky over Washington is fully grey today, and from the guestroom window the Monument shows against flat cloud.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on Lafayette Square, and the private balconies are wet, so guests watch the White House from inside.
phrases.thunderstorm: During the storm, nobody is out on the balconies; the Off the Record bar is the busier place to be.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog over the city today means the White House is visible from the balconies but the Monument behind it is not.
phrases.snow: Snow is settling on the North Lawn, and from the guestroom window the Washington Monument is hard to tell from the sky.
phrases.very_cold: It is very cold outside, so the balconies facing the White House are empty and the view is enjoyed through glass.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot Washington day, few guests stay long on the rooftop terrace, though the Monument view is unchanged.
phrases.mild_night: It is a mild, cloudy night in Washington, and the floodlit White House is clear from the Lafayette Square rooms.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low over Washington today; the White House is clear from the balconies, but the Monument behind is a faint shape.
phrases.late_night: If you turned off every light in a White House-facing room after midnight, the only glow left would come from Lafayette Square.
phrases.wet_evening: With the last drink from Off the Record, you would see the White House through rain on the glass tonight.
phrases.grey_evening: With a last glass from Off the Record, you would see the White House across Lafayette Square under low cloud tonight.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the bay windows of the residences frame Alcatraz as a dark shape on the dark water.
phrases.clear_morning: From the dining room windows, Alcatraz is clearly visible straight ahead, with the Golden Gate Bridge to the left.
phrases.clear_midday: Clear skies over San Francisco Bay this midday, so guests in the residences can see both bridge and island sharply.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon sun lights the Golden Gate Bridge on the left, seen from the bay windows of the Three-Bedroom Residence.
phrases.clear_night: On the rooftop terrace tonight, the fire pit is lit and the city lights show clearly beyond the brick buildings.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds move over the bay this morning, and Alcatraz stays in view from the dining room windows.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Patches of cloud pass over the Golden Gate Bridge this afternoon, while the pier outside the dining room gets some sun.
phrases.partly_golden: Broken clouds let some low sun reach the Golden Gate Bridge, seen from the rooftop terrace as the day ends.
phrases.overcast: Grey cloud covers the whole bay today, so the Golden Gate Bridge looks dull red rather than bright from the residence windows.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on San Francisco Bay, and guests in the residences have the fireplaces lit while watching the rain over Alcatraz.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder over the bay this hour, and the rooftop terrace is empty while guests watch the lightning from the dining room windows.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog covers the bay today, hiding Alcatraz and the bridge, so only the moored sailboats are visible from the dining room.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare in San Francisco, but today a few flakes fall past the residence bay windows toward the water.
phrases.very_cold: A cold day by San Francisco standards, and the rooftop fire bowl is lit in daylight, Alcatraz sharp across the bay.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot for this city, so the rooftop terrace is quiet and guests watch the bay from inside the residences instead.
phrases.mild_night: Mild and cloudy tonight, with people around the rooftop fire pit looking at the city lights beyond the brick buildings.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low over the bay today: the pier and moored sailboats are visible from the dining room, Alcatraz is not.
phrases.late_night: Past one in the morning, the bay water shows the city lights, and there is no hurry to leave the bay windows.
phrases.wet_evening: With the curtain open past midnight, rain on the Bay View Residence windows blurs the lights across San Francisco Bay.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight, curtains in the Bay View Residence are open, and waterfront lights show under low cloud toward the Golden Gate.

phrases.clear_predawn: From the Flag Suite tower in the hour before dawn, the palace opposite is still unlit under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_morning: Morning sun lights the palace facade, and breakfast guests at the Veranda see Gamla Stan clearly across the water.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sky over Stockholm is fully clear, and from the balcony the City Hall tower is sharp on the horizon.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Golden hour puts direct sun on the palace facade, and from the Veranda tables Gamla Stan appears twice, once on the water.
phrases.clear_night: If you were on the balcony tonight, you would see the palace lit up across Stockholms ström under a clear sky.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds move over Gamla Stan this morning, but the palace facade stays in plain view from the Veranda tables.
phrases.partly_afternoon: This afternoon the Flag Suite tower shows a sky that changes every few minutes, half cloud, half blue, all round.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, cloud edges go orange above Parliament, seen from the balcony with a drink in hand.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the palace looks flat and grey too, which is honest Stockholm weather as seen from the Veranda.
phrases.rain: Rain marks the water of Stockholms ström, and the indoor pool with its two fireplaces is the busier place today.
phrases.thunderstorm: If you were on the balcony now, you would see lightning flash over the Royal Palace across Stockholms ström.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides most of Gamla Stan today; from the Veranda only the nearest part of the palace facade can be seen.
phrases.snow: Snow falls on the palace roof opposite, and guests in the Flag Suite watch it come down from the top floor.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold and clear today, so the palace facade and Parliament are sharp from the balcony, best seen through glass.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot days are rare in Stockholm; the Veranda's waterfront tables face Gamla Stan while the sun stays strong.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night, and the balcony tables have cocktails on them, with the palace and Parliament across the water.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today: the City Hall tower on the horizon cannot be seen, but the palace opposite still can.
phrases.late_night: The curtain is left open on purpose; the Gamla Stan lights beside the Royal Palace are the last thing seen before sleep.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the Veranda windows tonight, and the lights of Gamla Stan look blurred across the water beside the palace.
phrases.grey_evening: Cloud hangs low over the palace after midnight, and the lights of Gamla Stan reflect in the water opposite the Flag Suite.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the 19th-floor windows of Top of the Mark show the bay still dark and Alcatraz as a shape.
phrases.clear_morning: Clear sky over San Francisco Bay this morning, so an in-room breakfast comes with Alcatraz and the hills in full view.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the western windows of Top of the Mark give a clear, if partial, view of the Golden Gate Bridge.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun from the west lights the Transamerica Pyramid, seen from the sitting area with the wicker chairs.
phrases.clear_night: If you were at Top of the Mark tonight, you would see the city skyline lit under a clear sky, martini optional.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds over downtown this morning, which is roughly what the king rooms' windows frame on most days.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Broken cloud over the bay this afternoon puts Alcatraz in sun one minute and shadow the next from Top of the Mark.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, clouds above the Golden Gate Bridge turn orange when seen from the lounge's west windows.
phrases.overcast: Full grey sky over San Francisco today, yet Alcatraz and the bay are still plainly visible from the 19th floor.
phrases.rain: Rain on Nob Hill right now, and a wood-paneled suite with a fireplace is a sensible place to be.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder over the bay, and from Top of the Mark guests can watch lightning behind Alcatraz without leaving their seats.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog over the bay today, so the Golden Gate Bridge is hidden from the lounge while the 100 Martinis menu is not.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare in San Francisco, but if it fell today the upper-floor rooms would show the city hills turning white.
phrases.very_cold: Near freezing outside, unusual here, and the air is clear enough that the Marin Headlands look close from the lounge.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot for San Francisco today, and from the north windows of the lounge the bay at least looks cool.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night on Nob Hill, and the lights of downtown are the main view from the king rooms.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today, so the Golden Gate Bridge and the Marin Headlands are not visible from the lounge, though downtown is.
phrases.late_night: After midnight the upper-floor bay rooms are dark, and the only light comes from the city between Nob Hill and the bay.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the Top of the Mark windows after midnight, and the lights across the bay blur and clear in turns.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight, cloud hangs over the bay, and from the upper-floor rooms the city lights show under it toward the Golden Gate.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the west-facing windows show a dark Atlantic, and the WET Deck infinity pool is still empty.
phrases.clear_morning: From the Paper Moon terrace this morning, the Atlantic is bright blue and the golden cliffs are already in full sun.
phrases.clear_midday: Under a clear midday sky, the Atlantic lies flat and blue beyond the glass balustrade of the rooftop lap pool.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were in a west-facing room now, you would watch the sun go down directly into the Atlantic.
phrases.clear_night: Clear night over the WET Deck, with stars above the Atlantic and the lawn below the terrace fully dark.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds are moving over the sea this morning, visible from every room since all 134 face west.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Patches of shade cross the lawn and the pine trees this afternoon, while the Atlantic stays mostly blue.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun lights the clouds orange over the Atlantic, best seen from a WOW suite rooftop pool.
phrases.overcast: Grey sky from the Paper Moon terrace today, the Atlantic a flat grey too, the golden cliffs looking paler than usual.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the WET Deck today, and the lounge chairs on the rooftop terrace are wet and unused.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunderstorm over the Atlantic right now, lightning visible from the west-facing windows, and the indoor fitness centre is the dry option.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over the sea today, so from the rooftop terrace the horizon is blurred and the cliffs look pale and grey.
phrases.snow: Snow in the Algarve is extremely rare, yet today flakes are falling on the rooftop lap pool and its white stone surround.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold today, so the lounge chairs by the WET Deck are empty, though the Atlantic is bright and clear.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot this afternoon, and guests are mostly in the WET Deck infinity pool or under the pine trees on the lawn.
phrases.mild_night: On a mild cloudy night, the lit WET Deck infinity pool faces the dark Atlantic below a sky with no stars.
phrases.reduced_visibility: If you stood on a west-facing balcony now, you would see the nearby Atlantic but not the horizon or the far cliffs.
phrases.late_night: Guests in the WOW suites have switched everything off, and moonlight on the Atlantic is the only glow inside now.
phrases.wet_evening: Anyone awake in a WOW suite after midnight is watching rain run down the glass, the Atlantic grey behind it.
phrases.grey_evening: Anyone awake in a WOW suite after midnight can watch low cloud move slowly over the Atlantic and dim the coast lights.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Times Square billboards are still lit, and from the king rooms the screens look brighter than the sky.
phrases.clear_morning: Clear morning over Midtown, and the fitness center window shows Times Square traffic starting while guests pedal on the stationary bikes.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the Midtown skyscrapers stand sharp in the sun from the two-queen rooms, and the billboards look paler in daylight.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Low afternoon sun lights the Midtown towers seen from the rooftop terrace, and the coin binoculars are getting some use.
phrases.clear_night: Clear night, and the Times Square neon fills the windows of Beast & Butterflies while diners finish their plates.
phrases.partly_morning: Scattered clouds pass over the Midtown skyscrapers this morning, and from the king rooms the billboards are already switched on.
phrases.partly_afternoon: If you were on the rooftop terrace this afternoon, you would see patches of sun moving across the Times Square crowds.
phrases.partly_golden: The last sun colors the clouds orange above Midtown, and the Times Square screens get brighter as guests watch from their windows.
phrases.overcast: Grey sky over Manhattan today, so the Times Square billboards do most of the lighting outside the fitness center window.
phrases.rain: Rain on Times Square, and from Beast & Butterflies guests watch umbrellas open under the billboards while they eat.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm is over Midtown, and lightning shows above the skyscrapers from the king rooms while guests leave the rooftop terrace.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over Manhattan today, and from the rooftop terrace the tops of the Midtown skyscrapers are hard to see.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on Times Square, and from the king rooms the billboard light turns the falling flakes red and blue.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold outside today, and the rooftop terrace stools are empty while guests watch Times Square through the fitness center window instead.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot in Midtown today, and the red stools on the rooftop terrace stand in full sun with nobody on them.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night, and guests on the rooftop terrace sit on the blue bar chairs looking at the Times Square crowds.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the Hudson River-facing rooms the water is hard to make out, and Midtown towers look faded.
phrases.late_night: Toward three in the morning, with every bedside light switched off, the Times Square billboards give the only glow inside.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the King room window after midnight, and the Times Square billboards blur into colour on the wet pavement.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight the haze over Midtown glows with Times Square neon, seen from the King room window.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the two arched windows of a bay-view room show Saltsjö Bay still dark and Djurgården as a flat shoreline.
phrases.clear_morning: Clear sky this morning, and the first ferries leave the quay beside the mill for Djurgården across flat, bright water.
phrases.clear_midday: Lunch on the waterfront terrace comes with full sun on the table and a clear look at passing ferries.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun comes straight through the arched windows, and Djurgården's shoreline across the water turns a warmer colour.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would see Gröna Lund and the city skyline across the water from an open window.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over Saltsjö Bay this morning, and the colourful waterfront buildings beyond the arched window brighten and dim in turns.
phrases.partly_afternoon: On the waterfront terrace, the afternoon is half sun, half cloud, with ferries crossing the bay on schedule.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun lights the clouds over Djurgården, and the bay-view rooms face it directly through two arched windows.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky, Gröna Lund and the city skyline are still clear from an open window, just without any shadows.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on Saltsjö Bay, while in the spa's indoor pool the light comes from warm wall sconces, not the sky.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm over the bay means the terrace tables stand empty, and the ferry to Djurgården looks less inviting from indoors.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog sits on Saltsjö Bay, and from the bay-view room the Djurgården shoreline is a faint line or not there at all.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on the park and the inlet below the old mill, and the terrace dining tables are white on top.
phrases.very_cold: From the arched window, frost edges the glass over Saltsjö Bay while the ferry leaves the quay for Djurgården.
phrases.very_hot: A very hot day for Stockholm, and guests on the waterfront terrace sit close to the water, watching the ferries pass.
phrases.mild_night: Mild and cloudy tonight, and guests with an open window hear the water of Saltsjö Bay without needing an extra blanket.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low over the bay, so the Djurgården shoreline is unclear from the rooms and the city skyline cannot be seen.
phrases.late_night: Back in a bay-view room after a late dinner, you would see Djurgården's shore lights on the bay through both arched windows.
phrases.wet_evening: If you were having a last drink in a bay-view room now, rain on the windows would blur the Djurgården shore lights.
phrases.grey_evening: With a last drink at the arched window tonight, you would see Djurgården's shore lights across the bay under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Pacific is still dark from the Skyline Ocean Residences, and the balcony doors are already open.
phrases.clear_morning: From the ocean-facing fitness centre, early runners on the treadmills watch the sun already high over a flat blue Pacific.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sun is straight above the beach, and most guests are in the outdoor pool near the swim-up bar.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon light falls on the sand below the towers, and the surf is easy to see from every high balcony.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the sky over the Pacific is clear, and from the upper rooms the Surfers Paradise skyline shows its lights.
phrases.partly_morning: Guests in the Skyline Ocean Residences above the 36th floor look out this morning at the Pacific under a few clouds.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over the water this afternoon, moving their shadows across the surf seen from the floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud turns orange above the beach while the lights of Akoya come on inside.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the Pacific looks grey too, so the indoor pool under its slanted skylights is busier than usual.
phrases.rain: Rain is running down the floor-to-ceiling glass of the suites, and the beach below is almost empty.
phrases.thunderstorm: If you were in a Skyline Ocean Residence right now, you would watch lightning over the Pacific from behind the glass.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hides the far end of the beach today, and rooms on the hinterland side get even less to look at.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on the Gold Coast, which almost never happens, and guests at the balcony windows are mostly taking photos.
phrases.very_cold: A very cold day for the Gold Coast, and from the balconies the beach below looks wide and nearly empty.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot outside today, and most guests have chosen the water at the swim-up pool bar over the beach.
phrases.mild_night: Warm air and cloud tonight, so the balcony doors of the twin rooms stay open to the sound of the surf.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the Surfers Paradise skyline is a faint outline and the horizon over the ocean is missing.
phrases.late_night: Were you in a Skyline Ocean Residence tonight, you would sleep well and wake to the Pacific across the window at dawn.
phrases.wet_evening: If you were having a last drink in a Skyline Ocean Residence, rain would run down the glass over the lit beachfront.
phrases.grey_evening: If you took a last drink up in a Skyline Ocean Residence now, you would see the Surfers Paradise lights under cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, Table Mountain is already a dark shape in the Mountain View room windows, with the city bowl still lit below.
phrases.clear_morning: From a balcony, early sun lights Table Mountain while the Gardens rooftops and palm trees below stay in shade.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the floor-to-ceiling windows of the suites show Table Mountain in full detail, with no cloud on its flat top.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun turns the rock of Table Mountain orange, and guests on the balconies sit in the woven chairs to watch it.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would see the Gardens rooftops lit below and Table Mountain as a dark outline above.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds this morning sit high above Table Mountain and Lion's Head, but both peaks stay clear in the Mountain View room windows.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Seen from the balcony, patches of cloud put Lion's Head in sun one minute and in shade the next this afternoon.
phrases.partly_golden: Clouds above the De Waterkant rooftops turn pink in the last sun, while Table Mountain goes grey.
phrases.overcast: A flat grey sky covers Cape Town today, and from the suites Table Mountain looks dark grey against the cloud.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the Gardens rooftops, and guests watch it from the floor-to-ceiling windows rather than from the balconies.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder over Table Mountain keeps the balconies empty, and a table at Ongetem is the sensible place to sit it out.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides the upper part of Table Mountain today, so the Mountain View rooms show only its lower slopes and the rooftops.
phrases.snow: Snow is unusual here, but today the floor-to-ceiling windows of the suites show a white layer on the top of Table Mountain.
phrases.very_cold: On a day this cold for Cape Town, the balcony chairs stay empty and guests look at Lion's Head through the glass.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot air sits over the city bowl today, and the palm trees below the balconies do not move at all.
phrases.mild_night: The night is warm and cloudy, so guests stay out on the balconies above the lit rooftops of De Waterkant.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is poor today, so from the balcony Table Mountain is a faint shape and Lion's Head is hard to make out.
phrases.late_night: In a Mountain View suite tonight, you could fall asleep with the curtain open, the mountain's flat outline above the rooftops.
phrases.wet_evening: Were you having a last drink in a Mountain View suite, rain would blur the city lights under Table Mountain.
phrases.grey_evening: Were you having a last drink in a Mountain View suite now, Table Mountain's flat top would show against city-lit cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the balconies above Shelter Cove face a dark Pacific, and early risers watch for dolphins from their rooms.
phrases.clear_morning: From the clifftop balconies, the morning Pacific lies flat and bright below Shelter Cove under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sun is straight over the oceanfront pool, and the blue lounge chairs by the hot tub are mostly taken.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon sun comes straight through the open French doors of the king rooms and lights the Pacific beyond.
phrases.clear_night: On a clear night the lobby and stone tower are lit, and from the balconies the Pacific is dark under stars.
phrases.partly_morning: Broken cloud sits over Shelter Cove this morning, and the Pacific in front of the balconies shows blue and grey patches.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the hot tub this afternoon, cloud shadows can be seen moving over the coastal rocks and the open Pacific.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun turns the clouds pink above the Pacific, and the palm trees by the pool stand against it.
phrases.overcast: From a clifftop balcony now, you would see the Pacific grey and flat under a low overcast sky above Shelter Cove.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the balconies above Shelter Cove, and guests watch the wet Pacific from behind closed French doors.
phrases.thunderstorm: From the clifftop balconies, lightning flashes over the Pacific Ocean during the thunderstorm, lighting the rocks of Shelter Cove below.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog has come in over Shelter Cove, and from most balconies the Pacific is hidden a short distance past the coastal rocks.
phrases.snow: Snow is almost unknown in Pismo Beach, but a few flakes would land on the balcony rails above the Pacific.
phrases.very_cold: Rare very cold air over Pismo Beach today, and the heated hot tub above the ocean is the only comfortable spot outside.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot days are unusual on this coast, and guests move between the ocean breeze on the balconies and the pool.
phrases.mild_night: Mild and cloudy over Shelter Cove tonight, the lobby lit under the palm trees and a few guests in the hot tub.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the clifftop rooms the ocean fades out before the horizon and dolphins cannot be spotted.
phrases.late_night: Well past midnight, white lines of surf show under the king room windows, and the waves can be heard through the glass.
phrases.wet_evening: Curtains open after midnight, rain runs down the king rooms' French doors and the Pacific surf below sounds through the glass.
phrases.grey_evening: Curtains stay drawn back after midnight, and low cloud covers the Pacific above Shelter Cove.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Giralda tower is a dark shape above the terracotta roofs seen from Terrace 1912.
phrases.clear_morning: Guests in the Premium Views rooms open the curtains to full sun on the Ayuntamiento façade across the plaza.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the plunge pool on the rooftop is the sensible place to be, with the Cathedral in plain view.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun turns the stone balustrade of Terrace 1912 orange, and the Giralda stands sharp against a clear sky.
phrases.clear_night: If you were at the cocktail bar tonight, you would see the Giralda tower under a clear sky full of stars.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds pass over the spires this morning, visible from the upper level of Terrace 1912.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the balcony rooms, the afternoon light comes and goes on the green foliage as clouds move across Seville.
phrases.partly_golden: Broken cloud over the Cathedral gives the last hour of sun some colour, best watched from the rooftop loungers.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the terracotta rooflines look flat, but the Giralda is still clear from the plunge pool.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on Plaza San Francisco, and the Ayuntamiento façade is wet and shiny from the Premium Views windows.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder over Seville means the rooftop is empty, and guests watch the lightning from their rooms instead.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze today softens the Giralda tower from Terrace 1912, while the Ayuntamiento across the square stays easy to see.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare in Seville, but today a few flakes land on the sun loungers beside the plunge pool.
phrases.very_cold: Close to freezing is unusual here, and the plunge pool has no takers, though the view of the Cathedral is sharp.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot afternoon in Seville: the plunge pool is the busiest part of the hotel, and nobody sits on the street terrace.
phrases.mild_night: A mild night with cloud over Seville, and guests at the rooftop cocktail bar still have the Giralda in view.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the Ayuntamiento opposite is clear but the Cathedral and Giralda look faint from the rooftop.
phrases.late_night: If you switched off the lights in a Premium Views room after midnight, Plaza San Francisco would be the only light left.
phrases.wet_evening: If you carried a last drink up to Terrace 1912 after midnight, you would see the Giralda through the rain.
phrases.grey_evening: Were you on Terrace 1912 for a last drink, you would see the Giralda's spire under low cloud and lit rooflines.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Arno is still dark below the Deluxe balconies, and San Miniato al Monte is only an outline.
phrases.clear_morning: Breakfast trays go out on the balconies, with a clear view down the Arno to Ponte alle Grazie.
phrases.clear_midday: At the Empireo rooftop pool, the sun is directly overhead and the Duomo stands sharp across the rooftops.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were on a Deluxe balcony, you would see the late sun on San Miniato al Monte and the replica David.
phrases.clear_night: From the rooftop terrace tonight, the Duomo dome and the hills toward Piazzale Michelangelo are dark shapes under a clear sky.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit over the Tuscan hills this morning, while guests in Superior rooms look down at the Arno.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over the Arno in the afternoon, and the heated rooftop pool stays in use at Empireo.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, clouds break up the light over San Miniato al Monte, seen from the Deluxe balconies.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky today, the Gothic tower of Santa Croce is still clear from the room windows that face it.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the Arno and on the Empireo terrace, so the Deluxe room windows are the dry place to watch it.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the Tuscan hills shows up well from the panoramic windows of the Deluxe rooms, with the rooftop empty.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog on the river hides San Miniato al Monte today, and Ponte alle Grazie is only partly visible from the balconies.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare in Florence, but today the rooftops and cypress trees outside the windows have a thin white layer.
phrases.very_cold: From the Empireo rooftop, hard winter light falls on the Arno below Ponte alle Grazie and San Miniato al Monte.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot afternoon, the Empireo pool is the busiest spot in the hotel, with the Duomo visible across the roofs.
phrases.mild_night: Guests on the Deluxe balconies sit out late under a cloudy, warm sky, with the Arno moving quietly below.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today, so the Arno and Ponte alle Grazie are clear from the balconies but the Tuscan hills are not.
phrases.late_night: Sleep comes easily in the Arno-facing Deluxe rooms, where the Lungarno lights reflect in the water until dawn shows San Miniato again.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner, rain runs down the Deluxe room windows, and the Lungarno lights show as long lines in the wet Arno.
phrases.grey_evening: After dinner, the Deluxe rooms' panoramic windows show the Arno under low cloud, the Lungarno lights reflected in the water.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise under a clear sky, pale light shows the limestone mountains and the water of Lake Garda below the infinity pool.
phrases.clear_morning: Sunlight now reaches the wooded peaks, and from the infinity pool the still water mirrors them almost exactly.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the lake is bright blue through the large restaurant windows, and the distant hills stand out sharply.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun lights the Riviera dei Limoni below the resort, and guests on the Gramen terrace watch the lake change colour.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in a Sky Suite tonight, you would sit in the outdoor Jacuzzi under a clear sky full of stars.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds sit above the limestone mountains this morning, while the lake beneath the infinity pool stays mostly in sunshine.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over Lake Garda this afternoon, so the water seen from the room window shifts between blue and grey.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, cloud edges above the mountains catch light, and the outdoor heated pool is still in use.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the lake looks flat and pale from the restaurant windows, and the hills across the water are dull.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the lawn and the lake, and most guests move between the six saunas and the steam room.
phrases.thunderstorm: A storm is over the lake, and from a canopy-bed room you can watch lightning above the mountains through the large window.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hides the distant hills today, and from the Gramen terrace only the nearest part of the lake is clear.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare here, but today it lands on the lawn and the trees while the indoor heated pool stays warm.
phrases.very_cold: The air is close to freezing on the Sky Suite terraces, yet the view of the mountains is unusually sharp.
phrases.very_hot: It is a very hot day above the Riviera dei Limoni, and guests stand waist-deep in the infinity pool.
phrases.mild_night: Clouds cover the sky on a mild night, and the outdoor Jacuzzi on a Sky Suite terrace faces a dark lake.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the hills on the far side of the lake cannot be seen from the restaurant windows.
phrases.late_night: After a late dinner at Gramen, the Sky Suite windows show the shore lights of the Riviera dei Limoni along the lake.
phrases.wet_evening: With the curtain left open after midnight, rain blurs the window and the shore lights of the Riviera dei Limoni below.
phrases.grey_evening: The curtain is open before bed in a lake-view room, and the Riviera dei Limoni lights show below under the cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, Reunion Tower stands dark against a clear sky in the colossal windows of Monduel's atrium bar.
phrases.clear_morning: From the third-floor studio junior suites, the downtown Dallas skyline is sharp under a blue sky this morning.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday, the treadmills in the fitness centre face floor-to-ceiling windows full of downtown buildings under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun hits the lattice of Reunion Tower, seen straight up through the colossal windows at Monduel's.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight, from the atrium bar, Reunion Tower is lit against a clear sky with Fountain Place and city lights beyond.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass between patches of blue over the Dallas skyline this morning, visible from the guest room windows.
phrases.partly_afternoon: This afternoon, shadows from scattered clouds move across the downtown buildings outside the fitness centre windows.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, a few clouds turn orange above Reunion Tower, framed by the windows of Monduel's.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers downtown Dallas today, so Reunion Tower looks flat and grey from the atrium bar.
phrases.rain: Rain runs down the colossal windows of Monduel's, and Reunion Tower is wet and grey above the atrium.
phrases.thunderstorm: If you were at Monduel's right now, you would watch lightning over the skyline through the colossal windows.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides the upper part of Reunion Tower today, so the windows of Monduel's show mostly white sky.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare in Dallas, but today flakes fall past the guest room windows while the skyline turns white.
phrases.very_cold: On a very cold, clear day like this, the downtown skyline looks sharp from the third-floor studio junior suites.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot today, so guests at the rooftop pool stay in the water, with the highway overpass beyond the terrace wall.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night in Dallas, and the lights of Reunion Tower show clearly through the windows of Monduel's.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so Reunion Tower is clear from Monduel's but the farther downtown buildings are hard to make out.
phrases.late_night: After midnight, the third-floor studio junior suites face Reunion Tower's round top, and the skyline lights show around it until dawn.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner, the lattice ball of Reunion Tower shows through rain on the third-floor junior suite windows, downtown lights behind it.
phrases.grey_evening: After dinner, the third-floor studio junior suites look toward the round lattice of Reunion Tower under low cloud, downtown lit below.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the corner rooms show the Yodo River as a dark line beside a city still full of lights.
phrases.clear_morning: From the indoor pool, the distant mountains stand out clearly behind the Osaka skyline this morning.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sun is high over Kita Ward, and the gym treadmills face a sharp, bright high-rise cityscape.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: In the high-floor lounge, the late sun lights the Osaka skyline from the side while guests sit by the windows.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would see the whole Osaka skyline lit up from a 28th-floor GENSUI suite window.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds drift over the skyline this morning, and the marble soaking tub by the window is a good place to watch them.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Shadows from scattered clouds move across the city below the upper six floors, visible from every room this afternoon.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun reaches the spa treatment room windows between the clouds, with the skyline in warm colours outside.
phrases.overcast: Under a flat grey sky the distant mountains are harder to see, but the dense cityscape fills the twin room windows.
phrases.rain: Rain runs down the floor-to-ceiling windows of the indoor pool, and the skyline behind the glass looks blurred and softer today.
phrases.thunderstorm: A storm sits over Osaka right now; from a corner room, lightning shows up above both the river and the city.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hides the distant mountains today, so the gym windows frame only the nearest Osaka high-rises in pale grey.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling over Kita Ward, a rare sight, and the GENSUI suites' shoji screens open onto a whitened skyline.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold and clear over Osaka today, which makes the distant mountains unusually sharp from the high-floor lounge windows.
phrases.very_hot: A very hot day in Osaka; the city looks pale in strong light through the shoji screens of a GENSUI suite.
phrases.mild_night: Tonight is mild under low cloud, and the long chair at the suite window faces the dark bay.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today: the distant mountains cannot be seen, and only the closer towers show from the pool windows.
phrases.late_night: Whoever wakes for water in a corner room sees city lights along the Yodo River.
phrases.wet_evening: Guests in the GENSUI suites may slide the shoji open before bed and see Osaka's lights blurred by rain on the glass.
phrases.grey_evening: Whoever has a GENSUI suite tonight sees the Osaka skyline lights through the shoji screens, low cloud resting over the towers.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the suite terraces face a dark Andaman Sea, and the garden pools below are still and empty.
phrases.clear_morning: From the room's window seat, the morning sun lights the palm trees and a strip of blue sea behind them.
phrases.clear_midday: Under a clear midday sky, the red umbrellas by the garden pools are taken, and most guests are in the water.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were on a suite terrace now, you would see the sun dropping toward the Andaman Sea beyond Mai Khao Beach.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the sky over the Andaman Sea is clear, and from a villa deck the beach is dark but waves are audible.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit over the garden pools this morning, and the palm trees cast patchy shade on the beach side.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Cloud shadows move across the turquoise water this afternoon, and from a villa deck the sea changes colour with them.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken clouds over the sea turn orange, best seen from the adults-only pool at low tide.
phrases.overcast: Grey cloud covers Phuket's northern tip today, so the garden pools look grey too and the sea is less turquoise than usual.
phrases.rain: Heavy rain is falling on the garden pools and the red umbrellas, and the suite terraces are empty for now.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder over the Andaman Sea right now, and lightning is visible from the suite terraces between heavy showers.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze sits over the water today, so from the balconies the distant hills are missing and the sea looks pale.
phrases.snow: Snow at Mai Khao Beach would be a first, and the pool villa decks would be the place to watch it.
phrases.very_cold: Near-freezing air at Mai Khao Beach is almost unknown, and the three outdoor pools and villa decks would likely stay empty.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot today, so the pergola shade on the villa decks matters, and the adults-only pool has fewer swimmers.
phrases.mild_night: A warm cloudy night at the resort, and from the suite terraces there are no stars over the Andaman Sea.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the suite terraces the distant hills cannot be seen, only the beach and nearby sea.
phrases.late_night: A glass of water near midnight, and the pool shows pale from the villa bedroom, the Andaman Sea heard past the palms.
phrases.wet_evening: After midnight rain runs down the villa bedroom window, and the private pool outside catches every drop in the room's light.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight, low cloud passes over Mai Khao Beach, and the private pool shows pale outside the villa bedroom window.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Literary Terrace is empty and Mount Etna is already a dark shape against a clear sky.
phrases.clear_morning: Morning sun on the Restaurant Timeo terrace lights the ancient theatre columns, and the whole of Etna is clear behind them.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the pool is the coolest place on the terrace, with Taormina's hillside town and Etna in view from the water.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun turns the stone terrace gold, and the Bay of Giardini Naxos is bright under a cloudless sky.
phrases.clear_night: On a clear night, guests at the Literary Terrace & Bar can see stars above Mount Etna and the dark bay below.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit over Etna this morning, while a waiter sets breakfast tables on the terrace facing the sea.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over the bay this afternoon, so swimmers at the pool get sun one minute and shade the next.
phrases.partly_golden: If you were on the stone terrace now, you would see the last sun colouring the clouds above Mount Etna.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky, Etna's top is hidden, but the Greek Theatre columns opposite Restaurant Timeo are clear to see.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the iron chairs outside, so guests have moved into the bar with its wood-panelled counter.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder rolls over the Bay of Giardini Naxos, and lightning shows the garden terrace through the bar's tall windows.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over the sea today means the bay is pale, and Mount Etna is only a faint outline from the terrace.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare down in Taormina, but today it reaches the hotel terrace, with Etna already white far above.
phrases.very_cold: The air is close to freezing on the terrace, so the pool is empty and the snow on Etna shows very clearly.
phrases.very_hot: In this heat, the pool umbrellas are all taken and the open-air restaurant under the pergola gives welcome shade.
phrases.mild_night: A warm cloudy night, and tables on the Restaurant Timeo terrace are set with the dark theatre ruins just opposite.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short, so Mount Etna cannot be seen from the terrace and only the near part of the bay is visible.
phrases.late_night: Back from a late dinner, you would see Giardini Naxos lit along the bay.
phrases.wet_evening: If you took a last drink at the Literary Bar tonight, rain would blur the Giardini Naxos lights across the bay.
phrases.grey_evening: A last drink at the Literary Terrace and Bar tonight would show you cloud over Etna and Taormina's lights along the bay.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Parthenon is already a dark shape against the sky from the King Deluxe Acropolis View Room windows.
phrases.clear_morning: From the rooftop Première, the Parthenon stands in full sun this morning, with no cloud anywhere behind it.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the Acropolis sits in strong sun, and the floor-to-ceiling suite windows show every column clearly.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon sun turns the Parthenon stone a warmer colour, seen straight from the rooftop restaurant tables.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would see the Acropolis lit up above Athens from a rooftop Première table.
