phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm over Edinburgh puts the castle rock against a dark sky, better watched from a room window than the rooftop hydropool.
phrases.fog_haze: Guests in the Club Castle View rooms this morning see only a faint outline of Edinburgh Castle through the fog.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on Edinburgh, settling on the castle walls, while the rooftop hydropool stays warm for those already in it.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air over Edinburgh gives a sharp view of the castle, and the rock sauna and Himalayan salt room are busy.
phrases.very_hot: A rare very hot day in Edinburgh, and the 19-metre indoor pool is busier than the sunny rooftop hydropool.
phrases.mild_night: On a mild cloudy night the castle stays lit above the rooftops, and One Square is serving its hundred-plus gins downstairs.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low over Edinburgh today, so the castle rock is faint from the rooms and the far rooftops are not visible.
phrases.late_night: Guests in the Club Castle View rooms sleep facing the city lights; the castle on its rock fills their window at dawn.
phrases.wet_evening: Guests in the Club Castle View rooms watch rain run down the glass, the castle's shape above the wet, lit rooftops.
phrases.grey_evening: Whoever has a Club Castle View room tonight can see the castle above the rooftops, the city lights spread under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the balconies face a dark Andaman Sea, and Ko Man is only a flat shape against the sky.
phrases.clear_morning: From a suite balcony this morning, Nai Harn Beach is bright and the green hills around the bay are sharp.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday from the private balconies, clear sky sits over Nai Harn Bay and Ko Man shows plainly across the water.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: The rooftop pool faces west, so guests up there watch the sun drop toward Ko Man island this afternoon.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would see stars over the Andaman Sea from your balcony and very little else.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit over the hills behind the hotel this morning, while the beach below the balconies stays sunny.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds come and go over Nai Harn Bay this afternoon, so the view from The Cosmo changes every few minutes.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud to the west gives the rooftop pool a sunset with gaps in it.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the Andaman Sea looks flat and pale from the balconies, and Ko Man is a dull green.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on Nai Harn Beach, and guests watch it from the balcony table rather than from the sand.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm is crossing the Andaman Sea, and the balconies give a dry seat for watching lightning beyond Ko Man.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over the water today means Ko Man is a faint outline from the balconies, and the hills look softer.
phrases.snow: If snow really fell here, guests on the balconies would watch flakes land on Nai Harn Beach in complete disbelief.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air is rare on this bay, but the balconies still face Nai Harn Beach and a clear Andaman Sea.
phrases.very_hot: It is very hot this afternoon, and the rooftop pool is the only place at the hotel where that feels fine.
phrases.mild_night: A warm night with cloud over the bay, and Rock Salt is lit up beside the dark water of Nai Harn Bay.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so Ko Man is missing from the balcony view, though Nai Harn Beach below is still clear.
phrases.late_night: Near midnight, a glass of water, and the sea of Nai Harn Bay shows through the suite window, white at the shore.
phrases.wet_evening: After a late dinner at The Cosmo, rain runs down the room windows and a few anchored boat lights mark Nai Harn Bay.
phrases.grey_evening: Late after dinner at The Cosmo, cloud covers the moon over Nai Harn Bay and the sea is heard from the room.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the east-facing balconies on the upper floors look straight at a Caribbean that is still dark.
phrases.clear_morning: The sun comes up over the sea directly in front of the ocean-view suites, so breakfast on the balcony starts bright.
phrases.clear_midday: If you were on a balcony now, you would see the Caribbean bright blue under a clear midday sky off Mamitas Beach.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon light comes through the slatted pergola on the open-air terrace, while the sea in front stays calm and blue.
phrases.clear_night: If you were on a balcony tonight, you would see stars over the Caribbean and the dark outline of the distant pier.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds pass over the Caribbean this morning, so the balcony daybeds get sun one minute and shade the next.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the pool deck, clouds drift over the sea while the Sushi 'n' Raw Bar serves the afternoon crowd.
phrases.partly_golden: Clouds break up the last hour of sun on the open-air terrace, with warm light coming and going through the pergola slats.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the Caribbean looks flat and pale from the upper balconies, and the sand has no shadows.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on Mamitas Beach, and the covered balconies keep the daybeds dry while the sea turns a darker green.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the Caribbean is easy to watch from behind the sliding glass doors of an ocean-view room.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hides the distant pier from the balconies today, and the line between sea and sky is hard to find.
phrases.snow: From the upper-floor balconies, snow drifts down over Mamitas Beach and the flat Caribbean toward the pier.
phrases.very_cold: A freezing day would be unheard of on Mamitas Beach; the Caribbean from the balconies would look the same as always.
phrases.very_hot: From the upper-floor balconies, heat-haze shimmers over Mamitas Beach and the distant pier in the Caribbean.
phrases.mild_night: Clouds cover the stars tonight, but the air on the open-air terrace is warm and the sea is audible below.
phrases.reduced_visibility: The distant pier is hidden from the balconies today, and the horizon over the Caribbean is blurred rather than sharp.
phrases.late_night: An ocean-view suite's curtain is left open tonight, so the white wave lines on Mamitas Beach show after midnight.
phrases.wet_evening: After midnight rain runs down the sliding glass doors of the ocean-view suites, and the Caribbean breaks white on the sand below.
phrases.grey_evening: Cloud hides the moon tonight, and the only light on the Caribbean comes from the pool deck below the ocean-view suites.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the southern reach of Windermere is still dark below the twelve hot tub balconies, and the fells are only outlines.
phrases.clear_morning: From a hot tub balcony, the whole southern reach of the lake is clear in the morning sun, right at water level.
phrases.clear_midday: Midday sun on Windermere, and guests in the water-level hot tubs have the length of the southern reach in front of them.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon light turns the fells behind the gardens orange, seen from the covered balconies through the glass balustrades.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the three floors of balconies are lit, the hot tubs glow purple, and the lake beyond them is black and still.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds move over the southern reach this morning, so the water changes from grey to bright blue every few minutes.
phrases.partly_afternoon: If you were in a hot tub this afternoon, you would see cloud shadows crossing the fells on the far side.
phrases.partly_golden: Last sun of the day catches the cloud edges above Windermere, and the balcony hot tubs steam in cooler air.
phrases.overcast: A flat grey sky sits over the southern reach today, and the wooded hills seen from the dining room look dark green.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on Windermere; the balconies are covered, so the hot tubs stay in use with the lake directly below.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a thunderstorm the hot tub balconies are the wrong place to be, and guests move to the lounge's velvet wingback chairs.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog on the lake today: from the balconies the southern reach disappears after a short distance and the fells are gone.
phrases.snow: Snow is settling on the fells above the gardens, while steam rises from the balcony hot tubs over the lake.
phrases.very_cold: It is a freezing day outside, so the hot tubs on the balconies are the only comfortable way to look at Windermere.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot day, which is rare here, the spa's cold plunge gets more use than the twelve hot tubs.
phrases.mild_night: A mild, cloudy night over Windermere, and the purple glow of the hot tubs is the brightest thing on the balconies.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Low visibility today: from the hot tub balconies the near water is clear, but the end of the southern reach is not.
phrases.late_night: After a late Bowness dinner, Windermere's southern reach shows faint from the hot tub rooms.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the windows of the lake-level rooms after midnight, and Windermere's surface shows where the hot tub light reaches it.
phrases.grey_evening: Haze covers the southern reach of Windermere after midnight, and from the lake-level rooms a few far-shore lights show through it.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the sea-view rooms face a dark Arabian Gulf under a clear sky, with the Corniche still quiet below.
phrases.clear_morning: From the upper floors this morning, the Arabian Gulf is turquoise under a clear sky and the Corniche is easy to follow.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the rooftop pool is in full sun, and the glass towers around it stand out sharply against the blue.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon sun reaches the suite living rooms, and the sea beyond the floor-to-ceiling windows turns a deeper blue.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the enclosed terrace at Mr. & Mrs. Hawker gives a clear view of the city lights and the dark Gulf.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit over Doha Bay this morning, seen from the suite windows, but the sea is still calm and bright.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over the rooftop pool this afternoon, so the magenta loungers get sun one minute and shade the next.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken clouds over the Gulf catch some orange, visible from the sea-view rooms.
phrases.overcast: Full cloud over West Bay today, and from the floor-to-ceiling windows the Arabian Gulf shows more grey than blue.
phrases.rain: Rain is rare in Doha, but today it falls on the rooftop pool while the third-floor enclosed terrace stays dry.
phrases.thunderstorm: If you were in a suite right now, you would watch lightning over the Arabian Gulf through the floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over the Gulf today blurs the horizon, and from the upper floors the Corniche is clearer than the open sea.
phrases.snow: Snow in Doha would be a first, but if it fell you would see it from the sea-view rooms over the Gulf.
phrases.very_cold: On this unusually cold Doha day, the view of the Gulf is sharp, and the rooftop pool has very few swimmers.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot in Doha today, and the rooftop pool is the only outdoor space that makes sense before sunset.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night in West Bay, and the lights along the Corniche are visible from the sea-view rooms.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the sea-view rooms the Corniche is clear but the far side of the Gulf is not.
phrases.late_night: A midnight glass of water stands by the bed; the Corniche lights reflect in the Gulf.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the glass of the sea-view rooms, and the Corniche lights blur over the Gulf after midnight.
phrases.grey_evening: Haze sits low over West Bay after midnight, and the sea-view rooms look out on the Corniche lights along the Gulf.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the sea-facing rooms look out at a dark Atlantic, with the Twelve Apostles still only an outline behind the beach.
phrases.clear_morning: The sun has climbed over the Twelve Apostles, and the heated pool is the first stop for most guests before the sand.
phrases.clear_midday: From the pool deck, the Atlantic is bright blue under a clear sky and the grey loungers are mostly taken.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: The afternoon sun lights the Camps Bay suburb below the balconies, and the Twelve Apostles turn orange behind it.
phrases.clear_night: From a balcony tonight, the sky over the Atlantic is clear and the lights of Camps Bay are on below.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit on the Twelve Apostles this morning, but the beach in front of the pool is in sunshine.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds move across the sky above Camps Bay, and the hanging chair under the pergola is the shadiest seat on the terrace.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, the clouds over the Atlantic turn pink while guests watch from the infinity pool.
phrases.overcast: Grey sky from the balconies today, but the Twelve Apostles are still clear behind the beach and the pool stays heated.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on Camps Bay beach, and the cocktail bar is busier than the pool deck this hour.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder over the Atlantic keeps guests off the terrace, so the storm is watched through the glass of the sea-facing rooms.
phrases.fog_haze: Sea fog hides the Twelve Apostles today, so the balcony view stops at the beach and the water's edge.
phrases.snow: Snow is almost unknown in Camps Bay, and the heated pool is the warmest place to look at the white Twelve Apostles.
phrases.very_cold: A very cold day for Cape Town, with clear air showing every ridge of the Twelve Apostles from the balconies.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot in Camps Bay, so the pool and the shade of the pergola are the two busiest places at the hotel.
phrases.mild_night: Clouds cover the stars tonight, but the air is mild and the terrace loungers are still in use after dark.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today, so from the sea-facing rooms the beach is clear but the Twelve Apostles are only a faint shape.
phrases.late_night: If you were awake late in a sea-facing room, the Camps Bay lights would hold your eye below Lion's Head.
phrases.wet_evening: If you had a last drink in a sea-facing room tonight, rain on the glass would blur the Camps Bay lights.
phrases.grey_evening: If you were finishing a last drink in a sea-facing room now, you would see Camps Bay lit under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the canal-facing rooms look onto a dark, still Nyhavn, with the painted facades opposite not yet lit.
phrases.clear_morning: Morning sun falls on the canal water right now, and the painted townhouse facades opposite show every colour from the arched windows.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday under a clear sky, the canal-facing rooms look across Nyhavn to the painted townhouse facades and moored boats.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon sun reaches the painted facades across the canal, and the water below the arched windows reflects them.
phrases.clear_night: Guests in the canal-facing rooms tonight look out through arched windows at facade lights on the clear water of Nyhavn.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over Copenhagen, so the sun on the canal comes and goes while guests eat breakfast in the main hall.
phrases.partly_afternoon: With broken cloud this afternoon, the inner harbour beyond the arched windows changes between grey and blue every few minutes.
phrases.partly_golden: If you were there now, you would see the painted facades lit between the clouds across the canal.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky, the church spire seen from one guest room looks flat, and the canal below stays busy with boats.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on Nyhavn right now, and the canal boats keep moving while guests watch from behind the arched windows.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm sits over the harbour, and from canal-facing rooms lightning shows the painted facades for a second.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hangs over the canal today, so the facades opposite are only outlines from the rooms, and boats appear suddenly.
phrases.snow: From the canal-facing rooms, snow falls on the moored boats of Nyhavn and the painted facades across the water.
phrases.very_cold: Outside it is close to freezing, yet the clear sun still lights the painted facades seen from the canal-facing rooms.
phrases.very_hot: Guests in the canal rooms look out through arched windows at heat-haze above the painted facades across the water.
phrases.mild_night: It is a mild, cloudy night, and the canal outside the rooms is quiet, with the facades reflected on the water.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the church spire seen from one room is faint, though the facades across the canal are clear.
phrases.late_night: In the small hours, lights from the townhouses opposite show on the water of Nyhavn.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner, rain runs down the arched windows of the canal rooms, and the lit facades opposite reflect in Nyhavn's water.
phrases.grey_evening: Back in a canal-facing room after dinner, low cloud covers Nyhavn and the townhouse lights opposite reflect in the water.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Dallas skyline is still lit from the private balconies, and the rooftop pool deck is empty.
phrases.clear_morning: Early guests on the treadmills look straight out at Dallas high-rises and treetops through the fitness centre's tall windows.
phrases.clear_midday: Under a clear midday sky, the loungers around the rooftop pool get full sun, and the draped cabanas offer the only shade.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were on a private balcony this afternoon, you would see low sun on the Dallas skyline towers.
phrases.clear_night: From the rooftop terrace tonight, the lit Dallas skyline stands under a dark clear sky beyond the glass railing.
phrases.partly_morning: Scattered morning clouds pass over the skyline while guests in the corner suites watch from behind floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.partly_afternoon: The gray cabana seats on the rooftop terrace sit in soft, changing light as clouds move over Uptown this afternoon.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken clouds colour the sky above the skyline seen from the hot tub.
phrases.overcast: A flat grey sky covers Dallas today, and the rooftop pool is quiet, with the skyline towers clearly visible.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the rooftop pool deck and the pergola, so guests watch the wet skyline from inside their rooms.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the Dallas skyline is best seen from the corner suite windows, while the rooftop terrace stays empty.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze thins the view today, and from the fitness centre treadmills the Dallas high-rises look pale and soft-edged.
phrases.snow: A rare Dallas snowfall leaves a thin white layer on the rooftop pool deck and pergola, with the skyline behind.
phrases.very_cold: On a freezing cold day, the outdoor hot tub is the warmest place to look at the Dallas skyline.
phrases.very_hot: Extreme heat keeps most guests in the shaded cabanas or in the water of the rooftop pool, skyline in full view.
phrases.mild_night: On this mild cloudy night, the lantern-lit bar tables on the terrace face the lit Dallas skyline towers.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the balconies the nearer Uptown buildings are clear but the far skyline towers are faint.
phrases.late_night: Around two the corner suite's lights are off, and the only light left in the room comes from the Dallas skyline.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the floor-to-ceiling windows of the corner suite, and the Dallas skyline lights show blurred behind it.
phrases.grey_evening: Low cloud hangs over Dallas after midnight, and the corner suite windows show the skyline lights blur and sharpen as it passes.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the North Shore peaks are a dark outline from Mountain View rooms, with the downtown grid still lit below.
phrases.clear_morning: Clear morning over Vancouver, and from the Regency Club lounge the North Shore Mountains stand sharp beyond the downtown towers.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sun is on the fourth-floor outdoor pool, and swimmers look up at downtown towers under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun reaches the Mountain View rooms, and the North Shore peaks show their full shape in warm afternoon light.
phrases.clear_night: If you were on the balcony tonight, you would see the lit downtown towers and the dark mountain silhouette behind them.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds sit over the North Shore Mountains this morning, but the peaks are mostly visible from the upper floors.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the Mountain View rooms on Burrard Street, the North Shore peaks stand under a few afternoon clouds beyond the downtown towers.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken clouds above the North Shore peaks turn orange, seen from the Regency Club lounge.
phrases.overcast: Grey cloud covers Vancouver today, and from the Mountain View rooms the peaks look flat and pale beneath it.
phrases.rain: Rain runs down the floor-to-ceiling windows, and the outdoor pool on the fourth floor is heated, so a few swimmers stay in.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder over the North Shore Mountains, and guests in the restaurant watch lightning through the tall windows between courses.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides the North Shore Mountains today, so Mountain View rooms show only the nearest downtown towers and grey air.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on the downtown grid, and the fourth-floor heated pool has steam rising while flakes land around it.
phrases.very_cold: On a day this cold, the North Shore peaks look clear from the Regency Club lounge, and the balcony chairs stay empty.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot afternoon in Vancouver, and the outdoor pool on the fourth floor is the busiest spot in the building.
phrases.mild_night: A mild, cloudy night, and both balcony chairs face the lit downtown towers while the mountains stay hidden in the dark.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today, so the North Shore Mountains are not showing from the Mountain View rooms, only the nearby downtown blocks.
phrases.late_night: Lights off in the Mountain View rooms, guests see only the lit towers in front of the North Shore peaks.
phrases.wet_evening: Guests in Mountain View rooms watch rain on the glass tonight, low cloud covering the North Shore peaks beyond the lit towers.
phrases.grey_evening: Anyone awake in a Mountain View room tonight sees the downtown towers lit under low cloud over the North Shore peaks.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Empire State Building stands dark and sharp in the glass of the Empire View rooms.
phrases.clear_morning: From the Spyglass rooftop this morning, the coin binoculars give a clear, close look at the Empire State Building.
phrases.clear_midday: Midday sun on Manhattan, and the floor-to-ceiling windows show the Empire State Building without a single cloud behind it.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon light gives the Empire State Building a gold colour, and guests on the Spyglass terrace are ordering cocktails.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in an Empire View room tonight, the lit Empire State Building would fill the window from the pillow.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit over Midtown this morning, but the Empire State Building is fully visible from the rooftop terrace.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds come and go over the Midtown skyline, and the Spyglass viewfinders still point at the Empire State Building.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, guests at the 22nd-floor Spyglass bar see the Chrysler Building under broken clouds.
phrases.overcast: Grey sky over New York today; the Empire State Building is still clear through the black-framed window beside the brick wall.
phrases.rain: Rain runs down the floor-to-ceiling glass of the Empire View rooms, and the Empire State Building looks less sharp behind it.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder over Midtown, and guests watch the storm around the Empire State Building from inside the Empire View rooms.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog in Manhattan today, and only the lower floors of the Empire State Building show from the rooftop terrace.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling past the 22nd-floor Spyglass windows, and the Empire State Building is partly hidden behind the flakes.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air on the rooftop terrace today, and the Empire State Building stands sharp in a clear winter sky.
phrases.very_hot: A very hot day in New York, and the Empire State Building sits in strong sunlight seen from the Spyglass terrace.
phrases.mild_night: Mild night, cloudy sky, and from the rooftop bar the lit Empire State Building shows clearly below the cloud.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the Empire State Building looks pale from the rooftop and the Chrysler Building is hard to see.
phrases.late_night: Guests in Empire View rooms have turned everything off, and Midtown's glow is the only light left around the Empire State Building.
phrases.wet_evening: Whoever has an Empire View room tonight is probably watching the Empire State Building through rain on the glass before bed.
phrases.grey_evening: Whoever has an Empire View room tonight can watch the Empire State Building's spire against low cloud as Midtown's windows light up.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Chicago River is dark below the suite windows and the skyscrapers still show only a few lit offices.
phrases.clear_morning: Early sun reaches Lake Michigan before the city, and from a Lake View Suite the water looks pale blue past the towers.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the Chicago River is bright and busy under the guest room windows, with Marina City standing right beside the hotel.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Low afternoon sun lights the downtown skyscrapers from the west, and the corner Travelle Bar gets it through windows on both sides.
phrases.clear_night: On a clear night, the Trump Tower and the lit bridge on the river fill the floor-to-ceiling windows of the suites.
phrases.partly_morning: If you were having breakfast on the 12th-floor Club Level now, you would see clouds moving over the river and lake.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over Lake Michigan, so the water changes from grey to blue every few minutes from the Lake View Suite.
phrases.partly_golden: Late sun between clouds colors the Marina City towers next door while guests order drinks at Travelle Bar.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the Chicago River looks grey too, and the heated indoor pool with its star ceiling gets more visitors.
phrases.rain: Rain runs down the floor-to-ceiling windows of the guest rooms, and the bridge over the river looks blurred through the glass.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm over downtown Chicago means lightning above the Trump Tower, seen from the corner windows of Travelle Bar.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides Lake Michigan completely today, and from the suites only the nearest buildings along the Chicago River can be seen.
phrases.snow: Snow falls on the Chicago River outside, while inside the indoor pool stays warm under its fiber-optic star ceiling.
phrases.very_cold: In very cold clear air, Lake Michigan shows sharply from the One Bedroom Lake View Suite, far past the downtown towers.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot day, the Chicago River below the guest rooms looks cooler than it is, and the pool is indoors.
phrases.mild_night: Clouds cover the stars tonight, but the lit downtown towers along the river still show clearly from Travelle Bar on two sides.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Low visibility today means Lake Michigan cannot be seen from the Lake View Suite, though the river and Marina City still can.
phrases.late_night: Whoever wakes for water after twelve sees bridge lights shining on the Chicago River.
phrases.wet_evening: Whoever has the One Bedroom Lake View Suite can watch rain streak the glass while the river lights blur beyond the bridge.
phrases.grey_evening: Whoever has the One Bedroom Lake View Suite tonight can watch the river lights under low cloud before sleep.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Pacific is still dark from a Deluxe Ocean View balcony, but the waves can already be heard below.
phrases.clear_morning: If you were on your balcony this morning, you would see the sun on calm water and the empty beach below.
phrases.clear_midday: Under a clear sky, the pool deck cabanas give shade while the ocean behind them looks flat and bright blue.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: The terrace with the glass railing faces west, so guests on the white lounge chairs watch the sun drop into the Pacific.
phrases.clear_night: At night the fire bowl on the oceanfront terrace is lit, and the sound of waves replaces any view of the water.
phrases.partly_morning: Breakfast at Splashes comes with a few clouds over the Pacific and patches of sunlight moving across the water.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the pool deck lounge chairs, the afternoon light on the Pacific changes each time a cloud crosses the sun.
phrases.partly_golden: With broken cloud in the west, tonight's sunset from the terrace turns orange and pink between the gaps.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers Laguna Beach today, and from the balconies the Pacific looks grey too, but the waves still arrive.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the beach, and guests keep the pocket doors closed, watching the wet sand from inside their rooms.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the Pacific is easiest to watch from a Deluxe Ocean View room, with the glass door shut.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog has moved onto the shore, so from the balcony the sand is visible but the ocean fades a short way out.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare in Laguna Beach, but if it fell today, guests would watch it from behind closed pocket doors.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air for Laguna Beach today, so the balcony chairs stay empty and guests look at the ocean through closed glass.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot day the arched cabanas by the pool are the useful spot, with the Pacific just beyond.
phrases.mild_night: A mild, cloudy night on the oceanfront terrace, where the fire bowl is more for looks than for warmth.
phrases.reduced_visibility: If you were on a balcony now, you would see the beach and the nearest waves, but haze would hide the far horizon.
phrases.late_night: Up for a glass of water near midnight in a Deluxe Ocean View, you would see white surf breaking below.
phrases.wet_evening: If you were having a last drink in a Deluxe Ocean View now, you would see the white surf through the rain.
phrases.grey_evening: With a last drink in a Deluxe Ocean View room now, you could watch the waves break white under the cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the upper-floor windows show Lumpini Park as a dark block under a clear sky, with the city lit beyond.
phrases.clear_morning: Clear morning light reaches the tree canopy of Lumpini Park, and all 257 rooms look straight onto it.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the infinity pool is in full sun, and the park below looks bright green from the daybeds.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: From the rooftop lounge, the late sun turns the skyline towers orange while the park below slowly darkens.
phrases.clear_night: If you were at the bar tonight, you would see the illuminated towers of Bangkok with no cloud above them.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds pass over Lumpini Park this morning, and their shadows move across the tree canopy below the windows.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Guests in the 39th-floor Club lounge see sun on some parts of the city and cloud shadow on others.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, the clouds above the infinity pool catch colour while Lumpini Park below turns grey.
phrases.overcast: Under a flat grey sky, Lumpini Park still fills the six-metre windows, just with less colour than usual.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on Lumpini Park, and from the rooms the tree canopy looks darker and the skyline less sharp.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over Bangkok shows clearly from the 39th-floor Club lounge, where guests watch the storm from behind glass.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze sits over Bangkok today, so the far towers fade from the infinity pool, but Lumpini Park just below stays clear.
phrases.snow: Snow in Bangkok would be a historic event, and the six-metre windows would give every room a view of it.
phrases.very_cold: Today is unusually cold for Bangkok, so the infinity pool is empty and guests watch the park from inside.
phrases.very_hot: With very hot air outside, the poolside daybeds and the water are where guests spend the day above Lumpini Park.
phrases.mild_night: On a warm cloudy night, the rooftop terrace seating faces the city lights, with no stars above them.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the Club lounge the distant skyline is missing, though Lumpini Park below is still visible.
phrases.late_night: In a Club Corner room the curtain is left open on purpose, the city lights beyond Lumpini Park in view until sleep.
phrases.wet_evening: Behind an open curtain in a Club Corner room, rain streaks the tall window and the city lights blur beyond Lumpini Park.
phrases.grey_evening: With the curtains open in a Club Corner room, the city lights show beyond Lumpini Park under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Porto Cathedral stands dark against a clear sky, seen from the top-floor balconies.
phrases.clear_morning: Morning sun lights the tiled façade of Saint Ildefonso, clearly visible from the selected rooms on the upper floors.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday, the terracotta rooftops outside the bathroom window are bright under a clear sky, with a church tower above them.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun warms the stone of the Porto Cathedral, and the top-floor balconies have the clearest view of it.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would see the Porto Cathedral lit after dark from a top-floor balcony.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds move over Clérigos Tower in the distance this morning, seen from the hotel balconies.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Guests are eating a late lunch in the restaurant while clouds and sun alternate over the tree-lined street outside the arched windows.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud leaves patches of light on the Cathedral and on Saint Ildefonso's tiles.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky, the Porto Cathedral and the tiled church look flat and close from the top-floor balconies.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the terracotta rooftops seen from the bathroom window, and the restaurant is busier than usual.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder rolls over Porto, and guests watch lightning above the Cathedral from inside, behind the top-floor balcony doors.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides Clérigos Tower in the distance today, and only the nearest terracotta rooftops show from the bathroom window.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare in Porto, but if it fell today, the top-floor balconies would show white on the Cathedral roof.
phrases.very_cold: A very cold day for Porto, and guests stay inside the restaurant, where the arched windows still face the tree-lined street.
phrases.very_hot: From the top-floor balconies, heat-haze hangs over the terracotta roofs between the hotel and the Porto Cathedral.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night, and guests are finishing traditional Portuguese dishes in the restaurant with the arched windows open to the street.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Low visibility today, and the distant Clérigos Tower cannot be seen from the balconies, though the nearby Cathedral still shows.
phrases.late_night: After midnight the cathedral-facing rooms are dark inside, and the lit streets of Baixa are the only light left in them.
phrases.wet_evening: After midnight the rain runs down the windows of the cathedral-facing rooms, and the lit rooftops of Baixa show through it.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight a thin haze passes over Baixa, and from the cathedral-view rooms the city lights look soft and blurred.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the river-view rooms look across a dark Douro to the Ribeira and the Dom Luís I Bridge.
phrases.clear_morning: From the floor-to-ceiling windows, morning sun lights the terracotta rooftops of Porto on the far side of the Douro.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the rooftop pool is in full sun, and guests on the orange loungers can see the Porto skyline.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun lights the Ribeira hillside, and wine glasses are already out on the rooftop terrace tables.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the Dom Luís I Bridge is lit, and the Dona Maria restaurant windows face it directly across the Douro.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds move over Porto this morning, so the terracotta rooftops seen from the terrace switch between sun and shade.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Cloud shadows cross the Ribeira hillside this afternoon, while guests by the rooftop pool sit under the blue umbrellas.
phrases.partly_golden: If you were on the rooftop terrace, you would see the last sun on the Dom Luís I Bridge between clouds.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the Douro looks flat and grey too, but the Ribeira is still clear from the river-view rooms.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the Douro today, and the floor-to-ceiling room windows are the dry place to watch the Ribeira.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm sits over Porto, and from the Dona Maria dining room each flash shows the Dom Luís I Bridge briefly.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog sits on the Douro today, and from the river-view rooms the Ribeira is only a faint outline.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare in Porto, but today a few flakes pass the floor-to-ceiling windows on their way to the Douro.
phrases.very_cold: It is close to freezing outside, so the rooftop pool loungers are empty and the sun on the Ribeira does not help.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot air sits over the Douro, and the rooftop pool and its blue umbrellas are the busiest place in the hotel.
phrases.mild_night: Clouds hide the stars tonight, but the air is mild and the rooftop terrace tables face the lit Dom Luís I Bridge.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the rooms the Dom Luís I Bridge is clear but the Arrábida bridge is not.
phrases.late_night: In a river-view room the curtain is left open after midnight, and Ribeira's hillside lights reflect in the Douro.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain streaks the river-view windows tonight, and the Ribeira's house lights come on across the Douro by the Dom Luís I Bridge.
phrases.grey_evening: Low cloud covers Porto after midnight, and from the river-view rooms the Ribeira's lights reflect in the Douro.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the lake below the new suites is flat and grey, and the small island is only a dark shape.
phrases.clear_morning: From a balcony, the mountains across Lake Garda are sharp this morning, and the first loungers on the lawn are already taken.
phrases.clear_midday: Under a clear midday sky, the lakeside lawn and its stone balustrade look out over the bright water of Lake Garda.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun hits the balconies on the lake side, and the historic village along the shore is easy to see from there.
phrases.clear_night: If you were on a balcony tonight, you would see the lights of the lakeside village and a black, calm lake.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds sit over the mountains this morning, but the lake in front of the spa garden is bright and still.
phrases.partly_afternoon: This afternoon, clouds pass over the park and the lawn loungers get sun and shade in turns.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, the headland across the water turns orange while the clouds above it stay grey.
phrases.overcast: Full cloud over Lake Garda today, and from the French doors the little island far out looks flat and dark.
phrases.rain: If you were on an iron balcony now, you would see rain falling on Lake Garda and the lakeside lawn below.
phrases.thunderstorm: From the iron balconies, lightning over Lake Garda shows the small island through heavy rain for a moment.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hides the far shore today, and from the balconies only the palm trees and the nearest water are clear.
phrases.snow: Rare snow on Lake Garda today, and from the balconies it is settling on the palm trees in the park.
phrases.very_cold: From the iron balcony, frost lines the stone balustrade above a lake left empty of boats in hard winter light.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot day like this, the outdoor pool and the shade of the park's big trees are where guests stay.
phrases.mild_night: On this mild late night under cloud, the village lights show along the edge of Lake Garda below the iron balcony.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is poor today, and from the balconies neither the mountains across the lake nor the small island can be seen.
phrases.late_night: Well after dinner at Il Fagiano, a lake-view suite window shows the village lights on the water of Lake Garda.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the French doors of the lake-view suites tonight, and the lights of the lakeside village show through it.
phrases.grey_evening: Low cloud covers Lake Garda tonight, and from the lake-view suites the village lights show along the shore.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Royal Suite balcony already shows the dark outline of Pena Palace against a clear sky.
phrases.clear_morning: From the tall bedroom windows, the lawn and Pena Palace on its hilltop are fully lit this clear morning.
phrases.clear_midday: Midday sun falls on the cypress trees and manicured lawns, and the Serra de Sintra stands sharp behind them.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were on the Royal Suite balcony now, you would see late sun on both the Moorish Castle and Pena Palace.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the neoclassical arch is lit, and from the gardens the hills of Sintra are dark under a clear sky.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over the Serra de Sintra this morning, and Pena Palace sits in shadow one minute and sun the next.
phrases.partly_afternoon: This afternoon some guests sit in the gardens near the spa, watching cloud shadows cross the Sintra hills.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun turns the clouds pink above the lawn, with Pena Palace still clear on its hill.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky, the mountains look flat from the bedroom windows, though Pena Palace is still easy to find.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the manicured lawns, so most guests are indoors in the salon with its botanical murals.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm sits over the Serra de Sintra, and lightning shows now and then through the tall salon windows.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog covers the Sintra hills today, so Pena Palace is hidden and only the cypress trees on the lawn are visible.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare in Sintra, but today a thin white layer covers the lawn in front of the palace.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air sits over the Sintra hills, and the gardens around the spa are almost empty this afternoon.
phrases.very_hot: In very hot weather like today, the shade of the cypress trees on the lawn is the busiest spot at Seteais.
phrases.mild_night: It is a mild cloudy night, the facade lights are on, and dinner continues in the frescoed ballroom.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Low visibility today means Pena Palace is only a faint shape and the Moorish Castle cannot be seen from the balcony.
phrases.late_night: Guests in the mountain-facing rooms have switched everything off, leaving the window toward Pena Palace as the only light in the room.
phrases.wet_evening: Guests in the mountain-facing rooms are probably asleep by now, rain on the tall windows between them and Pena Palace's hill.
phrases.grey_evening: Guests in the Royal Suite are likely asleep by now, low cloud covering the hills around Pena Palace.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the SeaMist terrace is empty and the white deck chairs face a dark, flat Pacific.
phrases.clear_morning: From a balcony, the morning sun lights the pier and the sand while guests eat the continental breakfast.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the Pacific is a bright blue line behind the pool, and the palm trees give little shade.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Guests on the SeaMist terrace have taken the white deck chairs early; the sun is dropping toward the water.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the firepit is lit, the sky over the Pacific is clear, and the water is too dark to see.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds sit in patches over the Pacific this morning, and the pier is clearly visible from the balconies.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Some cloud, some sun this afternoon; shade comes and goes on the blue lounge chairs beside the pool.
phrases.partly_golden: If you were on the SeaMist terrace now, you would see the sun set between clouds over the Pacific.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers the whole 180-degree view from the balconies today, and the ocean looks grey too.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the sand and the pier, and the white deck chairs on the terrace are wet and empty.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the Pacific shows well from inside a room, and nobody is sitting by the firepit right now.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog has moved in from the sea; from the balconies the pier is faint and the horizon is gone.
phrases.snow: Snow in Pismo Beach is very rare, but if it fell today the palm trees by the pool would look very unusual.
phrases.very_cold: From the SeaMist terrace, the white deck chairs sit empty in hard winter light above the Pacific.
phrases.very_hot: If you were on a balcony now, you would see heat-haze above the sand and the Pacific flat beyond the palm trees.
phrases.mild_night: On a mild, cloudy night, guests sit around the firepit in the white deck chairs with no stars to look at.
phrases.reduced_visibility: From the balconies, the sand and the pool are clear today, but the Pacific horizon fades out of sight.
phrases.late_night: If you turned off the room lights after midnight, the only light left would be the Pacific showing through the window.
phrases.wet_evening: If you had a last drink in your room tonight, you would watch rain on the balcony glass and hear the Pacific.
phrases.grey_evening: If you had a last drink in your room tonight, you would see cloud over the Pacific and hear the surf.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the marina basin below the guest-room windows is still dark, with only the lights of the moored yachts showing.
phrases.clear_morning: From the Level 76 pool, Palm Jumeirah shows clearly this morning, with the Gulf flat and blue behind it.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sun is strong on the rooftop pool, and the four sun loungers are the busiest seats in the hotel.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon light reaches the Burj Al Arab and the Palm, both visible from the upper rooms until the sun sets.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in the high-rise bar tonight, you would see the lit skyline through the windows under the painted ceiling.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds sit over the Gulf this morning, and Ain Dubai is still clear from the gym windows.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over the marina basin this afternoon, so the moored yachts move in and out of shadow below the rooms.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun lights the clouds over Palm Jumeirah, seen from the rooftop pool at 310 meters.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers Dubai today, but the Marina, the Palm and the Gulf are all still visible from the guest rooms.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on Dubai, a rare thing here, and guests in the marble bathrooms watch it from their soaking tubs.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a thunderstorm, the 377-meter tower gives a close view of lightning over the Gulf from the upper-floor gym.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hangs over the skyline today, so from the guest rooms the high-rise towers look faded and the Palm is unclear.
phrases.snow: Snow over Dubai Marina would be a first, and the Level 76 pool would be the place to watch it fall.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air for Dubai today, and the Gulf and Palm Jumeirah look unusually sharp from the Level 76 pool.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot outside today, and at 310 meters the rooftop infinity pool is the most popular place with a Gulf view.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night in Dubai, and the lights of the Marina show clearly from the high-rise bar windows.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low, so the Marina below is clear from the rooms but Palm Jumeirah and the Burj Al Arab are not.
phrases.late_night: Were your room lights off in a high-floor suite now, the Marina and Palm Jumeirah would be the only light left.
phrases.wet_evening: If you took a last drink in the high-rise bar tonight, you would see Marina and Palm lights through rain on the glass.
phrases.grey_evening: If you took a last drink to the window now, you would see the Marina lights under low cloud toward Palm Jumeirah.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the London Eye and The Shard already show clearly from the large windows of the city-view rooms.
phrases.clear_morning: From the 8th-floor Sky Bar terrace, the morning sun lights The Shard and The Gherkin without a single cloud.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the whole run from the South Bank to the City is sharp from any upper-floor window.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were on the terrace now, you would see low afternoon sun on the London Eye and The Shard.
phrases.clear_night: Under a clear night sky, the lit London Eye and The Shard appear in the same frame from the suite windows.
phrases.partly_morning: Scattered morning clouds pass over the City, and The Gherkin moves in and out of shade, seen from the Sky Bar terrace.
phrases.partly_afternoon: This afternoon, broken cloud sits above the skyline while guests on the wicker chairs look across at the London Eye.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, a few clouds turn orange behind The Shard, seen from the city-view rooms.
phrases.overcast: A flat grey sky covers London today, but The Shard and The Gherkin remain plain to see from the guest rooms.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the Sky Bar terrace today, and guests watch the London Eye through the large windows of their rooms instead.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm is passing over the City, and from the suite living room lightning shows briefly behind The Shard.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog covers the City this morning, and from the terrace only the nearer London Eye can be made out.
phrases.snow: Snow is settling on the wicker chairs of the rooftop terrace, and the London Eye looks pale grey through the flakes.
phrases.very_cold: It is very cold outside, so the Sky Bar terrace chairs stay empty, though the skyline is clear to The Gherkin.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot in London today, and the rooftop terrace sits in full sun with the London Eye clear beyond the South Bank.
phrases.mild_night: Clouds cover the night sky, but the mild air keeps guests on the Sky Bar terrace, looking at the lit London Eye.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Low visibility today: the London Eye still shows from the terrace, but The Gherkin and the City are hard to make out.
phrases.late_night: After a late dinner at Three O Two, the city-view windows show the wheel of the London Eye against the City's lights.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the windows of a city-view room after midnight, the curtain open on the London Eye and the lit City.
phrases.grey_evening: The curtains are open after midnight in the city-view rooms, and the lit City skyline and the Eye's wheel show under cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: The harbour is still dark in the hour before sunrise, and the lit Hong Kong Island skyline shows through the floor-to-ceiling glass.
phrases.clear_morning: On the Peninsula Suite's landscaped terrace this morning, clear sky over Victoria Harbour makes the Hong Kong Island towers easy to count.
phrases.clear_midday: Midday sun falls straight onto the harbour, so guests in the window seating areas have the brightest view of the day.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were on the Peninsula Suite terrace, you would see low sun lighting the glass of the Hong Kong Island skyline.
phrases.clear_night: Dinner at Felix tonight comes with a clear view of the lit skyscrapers across Victoria Harbour.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit over Hong Kong this morning, and the harbour-view rooms get patches of sun on the water.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds move across the Hong Kong Island skyline this afternoon, seen through the floor-to-ceiling glass of the Peninsula Suite.
phrases.partly_golden: Broken cloud over Victoria Harbour turns orange as the sun goes down, which is what the terrace on the 26th floor faces.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky, Victoria Harbour looks flat from the guest rooms, and the skyline across it has no shine.
phrases.rain: Rain runs down the floor-to-ceiling windows, and the marble soaking tub faces a wet, grey Victoria Harbour.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over Victoria Harbour is the show from the floor-to-ceiling windows, and nobody is on the 26th-floor terrace right now.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hangs over the harbour today, and from the window seating areas the Hong Kong Island skyline is only an outline.
phrases.snow: Hong Kong almost never sees snow, so flakes over Victoria Harbour would bring guests to the floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.very_cold: Freezing days are rare here, and the 26th-floor terrace gives a sharp view of the skyline to anyone who dresses for it.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot air sits over Hong Kong, so guests watch Victoria Harbour from behind the floor-to-ceiling glass rather than from the terrace.
phrases.mild_night: On a mild cloudy night, the lit skyscrapers across the harbour are the view from a table at Felix.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the harbour-view rooms the near water shows but the Hong Kong Island skyline is faint.
phrases.late_night: In the small hours Hong Kong Island's lights shine on Victoria Harbour, water the Peninsula Suite's glass will show again at dawn.
phrases.wet_evening: With the curtains open in a harbour-view room, the Hong Kong Island lights blur through rain across Victoria Harbour.
phrases.grey_evening: With the curtains open in a harbour-view room, the Hong Kong Island lights reflect in the water under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Mekong is a pale grey band beyond the rooftops from the river-facing rooms, the sky clear.
phrases.clear_morning: Sunlight comes straight in from the east this morning, so the river-facing rooms get the Mekong and the full sun together.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the whole width of the Mekong is visible from a corner suite, with no cloud over Phnom Penh.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: The low afternoon sun is behind the tower now, so from Sora's terrace the river and rooftops are lit in warm orange.
