phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over the hills this morning, so the pagoda comes and goes while the restaurant makes its slow turn east.
phrases.partly_afternoon: If you were at a window table this afternoon, you would see cloud shadows moving across the rooftops toward Higashiyama.
phrases.partly_golden: The last sun catches Kyoto Tower between clouds, and guests in the upper rooms watch the hills turn grey.
phrases.overcast: A flat grey sky covers Kyoto today, and from the 14th floor the pagoda is only a dark shape against the hills.
phrases.rain: Rain streaks the floor-to-ceiling windows of the east-facing rooms, and the trains near the station are the clearest thing in the view.
phrases.thunderstorm: During the storm, diners in the revolving restaurant see lightning over the eastern hills while the room keeps turning.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over Kyoto today hides the pagoda completely, though Kyoto Tower still shows faintly when the restaurant turns toward it.
phrases.snow: Snow falls on the Higashiyama rooftops, and from the Japanese-style rooms the pagoda roofs carry a thin white edge.
phrases.very_cold: On this freezing day the air is very clear, and the five storeys of the pagoda stand sharp above the rooftops.
phrases.very_hot: Guests in the 14th-floor restaurant this afternoon look out at the Yasaka Pagoda through heat-haze over the Higashiyama rooftops.
phrases.mild_night: A warm cloudy night covers Kyoto, and from the candlelit tables the tower glows orange with no stars behind it.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today, so the pagoda does not appear during the restaurant's turn, and only Kyoto Tower, close by, remains clear.
phrases.late_night: Near midnight, for the length of a glass of water, an east-facing room shows city lights and the five-story pagoda over Higashiyama.
phrases.wet_evening: Through rain on the east-facing glass, the Yasaka Pagoda blurs among Higashiyama's night lights.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight, haze hangs over Higashiyama, and the east-facing upper rooms look toward the five-story pagoda above the lit city.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the valley below the superior suite balconies is still dark, and the forested hills show only as outlines.
phrases.clear_morning: From an open casement window, the terracotta rooftops and green trees of Sintra sit in clear morning light.
phrases.clear_midday: From the Esplanada Floresta terrace at midday, the terracotta roofs and hills of the Sintra valley stand sharp under a blue sky.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun reaches the pale yellow front of the manor, and the rose pergola on the terrace is lit from the side.
phrases.clear_night: From a superior suite balcony, stars fill the clear night sky above the Sintra valley at Lawrence's Hotel.
phrases.partly_morning: If you were at a suite balcony this morning, you would see broken cloud over the forested Sintra valley.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Guests on the garden terrace sit between sun and shade as broken cloud moves over the valley this afternoon.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, patches of light cross the forested valley seen from the five private balconies.
phrases.overcast: Grey cloud covers Sintra today, so the hills look flat and dull from the restaurant windows, though the trees stay green.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the terrace umbrellas, and guests have moved inside to rooms with period fireplaces and oak floors.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder rolls over the Sintra hills, and the casement windows are closed while lightning shows above the valley.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog sits in the valley today, and from the balconies only the nearest tall trees of the garden are visible.
phrases.snow: Snow is rare in Sintra, but today a thin layer sits on the terracotta stairs and the terrace tables.
phrases.very_cold: On a very cold clear day, the terrace chairs are empty and fires burn in the period fireplaces indoors.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot air sits over Sintra today, and the blue umbrellas on the terrace give the only outdoor shade.
phrases.mild_night: Clouds hide the stars tonight, but it is mild enough to sit on a suite balcony above the dark valley.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the distant valley is not visible from the terrace, only the garden trees and nearby rooftops.
phrases.late_night: In the superior suites, the curtain is left open after midnight, and a few house lights can be seen across the Sintra valley.
phrases.wet_evening: After midnight, rain runs down the superior suites' windows and blurs the few lights left across the Sintra valley.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight, low cloud moves across the Sintra valley, and its scattered lights come and go from the superior suite windows.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Kowloon skyline across Victoria Harbour is still lit, seen from a Grand Premier Harbour View room.
phrases.clear_morning: Morning sun is on the harbour, and from the roof garden fifty-six floors up the Kowloon hills show clearly behind the towers.
phrases.clear_midday: Blue sky covers the outdoor pool right now, and the Bank of China Tower stands directly beyond the red loungers.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon sun comes through the floor-to-ceiling windows of the harbour-view rooms and reaches the marble bathroom.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in the marble bathtub tonight, you would see the lit Kowloon skyline across the harbour through the windows.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds over Kowloon this morning, and the harbour water below the Grand Premier rooms changes colour as they pass.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds and sun alternate over the outdoor pool this afternoon, so the white umbrellas are only needed half the time.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last sunlight, broken cloud puts patches of light and shade on the mountain line seen from the Shangri-La Suite.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky sits over Victoria Harbour today, and the Kowloon towers look flat and colourless from the roof garden.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the harbour, and the red loungers at the outdoor pool are empty and wet for now.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over Kowloon can be watched from the canopy bed in a harbour-view room, with the windows closed and the lights off.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hangs over the harbour, so from the roof garden on floor fifty-six Kowloon is only a faint outline.
phrases.snow: Snow almost never reaches Hong Kong, but if it did, guests on the roof garden would watch it fall over the harbour.
phrases.very_cold: It is an unusually cold day for Hong Kong, and the clear air shows the mountain line sharply from the Shangri-La Suite.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot outside today, and most people at the outdoor pool are either in the water or under the white umbrellas.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night, and the Kowloon skyline lights across the harbour are clear from the floor-to-ceiling windows of the rooms.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the roof garden the Kowloon waterfront shows but the hills behind it do not.
phrases.late_night: Kowloon's lights shine across Victoria Harbour after midnight, framed in the Grand Premier rooms' windows.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the floor-to-ceiling windows of the Grand Premier Harbour View rooms, and the Kowloon lights blur across Victoria Harbour.
phrases.grey_evening: After midnight, haze hangs over Victoria Harbour, and the Kowloon lights look soft from the Grand Premier Harbour View rooms.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the IJ River outside every room is dark and calm, with only a few boat lights moving on the water.
phrases.clear_morning: From the restaurant tables, the city skyline across the river stands sharp under a clear Amsterdam sky this morning.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday, sunlight on the IJ River is bright enough that guests at the work desk in a suite pull the curtain.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon sun lights the Passenger Terminal directly outside, and the river beyond it looks gold from every room.
phrases.clear_night: After dark, boats on the IJ River pass the Passenger Terminal with their lights on, in view from every room.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over the IJ River this morning, so the dining room gets sun for a few minutes at a time.
phrases.partly_afternoon: If you were in a suite this afternoon, you would see cloud shadows crossing the city centre across the river.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun turns the clouds over the IJ orange, a good moment to sit at a restaurant window table.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky, the IJ River looks grey too, but the boats still pass the Passenger Terminal outside the hotel.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the river today, and guests watch it from the dining room instead of walking to the Muziekgebouw.
phrases.thunderstorm: During the storm, lightning over the IJ River shows up clearly from the suites, which all face the water.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog sits on the river today, and from the restaurant the city skyline across the water is barely visible.
phrases.snow: If you were in the dining room now, you would see snow falling on the IJ River and the passing boats.
phrases.very_cold: Today the air over the IJ River is very cold and clear, which gives the restaurant a sharp view of the skyline.
phrases.very_hot: On this very hot day, the water of the IJ is the coolest thing in view from the suite lounge areas.
phrases.mild_night: A mild, cloudy night in Amsterdam, and the boat lights on the IJ River are still moving past every window.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the city skyline across the river is faint from the restaurant, while the Passenger Terminal stays clear.
phrases.late_night: The suite's light stays on past two, as boat lights keep moving on the IJ.
phrases.wet_evening: With the curtains open after midnight, rain streaks the window and a few boat lights cross the IJ.
phrases.grey_evening: With the curtain open in an IJ-facing room, the city centre lights show across the river under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the corner king windows show Chapultepec as a dark mass and Reforma as a line of streetlights.
phrases.clear_morning: A clear morning puts the Mexican flag, the tree-lined streets and the mountains beyond in sharp detail from the high floors.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday under a clear sky, the rooftop pool lounge chairs sit in full sun, with the skyline open all around.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were in a corner king now, you would see late sun on the Auditorio Nacional rooftop and Chapultepec.
phrases.clear_night: On a clear night, Torre BBVA and the Reforma arc appear as lit shapes through the suite's tall glass walls.
phrases.partly_morning: Scattered clouds this morning move over the Chapultepec canopy, and the rooftop pool already has a few guests on the lounge chairs.
phrases.partly_afternoon: This afternoon clouds leave gaps, so the green sports field and the large flag get sun in turns from the high rooms.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun lights the clouds above Polanco, and the corner king windows catch it on two sides at once.
phrases.overcast: Under a flat grey sky, Chapultepec looks darker green and the mountains behind the skyline are only a faint outline today.
phrases.rain: Rain over Polanco today, and from the suite bedroom the tree-lined streets and the Reforma arc look wet and grey.
phrases.thunderstorm: During the storm, guests on floor 15 and above watch lightning over the distant hills while the rooftop pool stays empty.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze sits over the city today; Torre BBVA is still clear from the windows, but the mountains beyond have disappeared.
phrases.snow: Snow almost never reaches Mexico City, but if it fell today you would see it on Chapultepec from the corner rooms.
phrases.very_cold: A very cold, clear day for Mexico City, which means the mountains beyond the skyline are unusually sharp from the suite windows.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot today, and the rooftop pool is the busiest spot in the hotel, with the skyline hazy behind the potted trees.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night in Polanco; from the corner king, the Auditorio Nacional rooftop and Reforma are lit below the clouds.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today: Torre BBVA and Chapultepec are clear from floor 15, but the mountains and distant hills are not.
phrases.late_night: The corner kings on floor fifteen face Reforma's lights after midnight, and at dawn the same window shows the Chapultepec canopy.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner, rain runs down the corner king windows and the Reforma lights show blurred along their wide arc.
phrases.grey_evening: After dinner, the corner king rooms on floor fifteen show the Reforma lights spread under low cloud toward Chapultepec.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Story Bridge lights are still on, seen from the One Bedroom Junior Suite windows over a quiet Brisbane.
phrases.clear_morning: From the rooftop pool, the Story Bridge and the Brisbane River sit in full sunshine while the loungers are still empty.
phrases.clear_midday: Midday sun hits the rooftop lap pool, and the city skyline shows every high-rise and historic building in sharp detail.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon light turns the Story Bridge steel warm orange, best seen from a lounger at the rooftop pool.
phrases.clear_night: At Iris, the mosaic counter is lit and the Story Bridge stands fully illuminated against a clear Brisbane night sky.
phrases.partly_morning: Scattered clouds pass over the city skyline this morning, and the Junior Suite windows catch the sun between them.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Guests at the rooftop pool get sun and shade in turns as clouds move over the Story Bridge this afternoon.
phrases.partly_golden: If you were at Iris now, you would see the last sun light the clouds above the Story Bridge.
phrases.overcast: From the rooftop pool, the Story Bridge and the city skyline stand under a grey overcast sky.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the rooftop loungers, so the Story Bridge view is mostly enjoyed from inside the Junior Suite.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the city skyline is visible from the Junior Suite, while nobody is at the rooftop pool during the storm.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze softens the city skyline today, and the far end of the Story Bridge is harder to see from Iris.
phrases.snow: Snow in Brisbane would be a first, but if it fell, the rooftop pool loungers would hold it briefly.
phrases.very_cold: On a freezing Brisbane day, the rooftop pool is quiet and the Story Bridge view is enjoyed from inside the Junior Suite.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot in Brisbane today, so most guests are in the rooftop lap pool rather than on the white loungers.
phrases.mild_night: Under a cloudy warm night, Iris has its purple lighting on and the Story Bridge lights show across the river.
phrases.reduced_visibility: From the Iris rooftop, the Story Bridge stands clear while the far city skyline fades in the haze today.
phrases.late_night: After midnight city lights fill the One Bedroom Junior Suite window, and the Story Bridge will show over the river at dawn.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner at Iris, rain runs down the One Bedroom Junior Suite window, and the Story Bridge looks soft over the river.
phrases.grey_evening: Dinner at Iris is over, and the One Bedroom Junior Suite frames the Story Bridge and city lights under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, guests on the Atlantic-facing balconies see a dark sea and a sky slowly turning grey in the east.
phrases.clear_morning: The sun is now above the Atlantic, and the club lounge breakfast comes with clear ocean views through the tall windows.
phrases.clear_midday: On the seventh-floor sundeck, the midday sun is strong and the horizon is sharp in every direction.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Intracoastal-facing rooms get the sunset side this afternoon, with low light coming straight through the floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.clear_night: If you were on the sundeck tonight, you would see a clear sky over the Atlantic and a dark, flat sea.
phrases.partly_morning: Scattered clouds sit over the Atlantic this morning, seen from the private balconies of the oceanfront rooms.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds and sun alternate over the Intracoastal Waterway this afternoon, and the west-facing rooms get both in turn.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken clouds over the Intracoastal catch the colour, visible from the west-facing balconies.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers the ocean today, and from the outdoor dining terrace the water looks flat and grey too.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the seventh-floor sundeck right now, and guests are watching the wet Atlantic from behind their room windows.
phrases.thunderstorm: The suites' floor-to-ceiling windows frame each lightning flash over the Atlantic right now, from a dry room.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over the water today, so from the oceanfront rooms the horizon line between sea and sky is hard to find.
phrases.snow: Fort Lauderdale almost never sees snow, but if it fell today the seventh-floor sundeck would be empty and grey.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold for Fort Lauderdale today, and the seventh-floor sundeck is almost empty while the balconies get only short visits.
phrases.very_hot: From the private balcony, midday heat-haze shimmers over the Intracoastal Waterway to the west of the hotel.
phrases.mild_night: Tonight is mild under cloud, and the outdoor dining terrace is still in use, with the ocean dark beyond the palms.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today, so from the Atlantic-facing balconies the sea fades out well before the horizon that the sundeck usually shows.
phrases.late_night: In a west-facing room the curtain is left open after midnight, and the lights along the Intracoastal Waterway show on the water.
phrases.wet_evening: Behind open curtains in the west rooms, shore lights along the Intracoastal Waterway blur through rain on the glass.
phrases.grey_evening: Cloud covers Fort Lauderdale after midnight, and the west rooms' floor-to-ceiling windows show the shore lights along the Intracoastal Waterway.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the breakfast deck is set while the first game drive vehicles leave camp under a dark, clear sky.
phrases.clear_morning: Guests back from the morning game drive eat breakfast on the outdoor deck with the bushveld lit by the low sun.
phrases.clear_midday: Elephants and kudu reach the water below camp at cloudless midday, and guests in the pool have the clearest view.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: The evening game drive is out, and sundowners are served at the outdoor lounge facing the waterhole in golden light.
phrases.clear_night: Dinner moves to the boma tonight, with stars over the camp and the bush audible past the fire.
phrases.partly_morning: If you were on your cottage veranda this morning, you would see cloud shadows crossing the bushveld toward the waterhole.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the rim-flow pool, afternoon cloud shadows cross the waterhole in front of camp and the mopane canopy beyond it.
phrases.partly_golden: Last sun comes through gaps in the cloud onto the thatched cottages, while sundowners are set out at the outdoor lounge.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky sits over the Timbavati bushveld today, which makes the waterhole easier to watch from a lounge chair without glare.
phrases.rain: Rain drips off the thatched roofs today, and guests watch the wet mopane trees from their cottage verandas.
phrases.thunderstorm: From behind the floor-to-ceiling glass of a cottage bedroom, lightning over the Kruger bushveld is what guests are watching this hour.
phrases.fog_haze: Thin haze over the Timbavati today hides the far trees, so the nearby waterhole is the whole view.
phrases.snow: Snow is almost unknown in the Kruger, so flakes over the waterhole would have every veranda at camp occupied.
phrases.very_cold: Bitterly cold air on the morning drive makes the breakfast deck, in full sun, the preferred stop back at camp.
phrases.very_hot: If you were on your veranda now, you would see heat-haze over the waterhole in front of camp.
phrases.mild_night: Clouds cover the stars, but the night is mild, and dinner on the lantern-lit terrace goes ahead with the bush audible.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is down today; from the verandas the waterhole is clear, but the farther bushveld toward the park is not.
phrases.late_night: If you got up for water near midnight, you would see the waterhole through the cottage glass doors, pale in moonlight.
phrases.wet_evening: If you had a last drink in the outdoor lounge now, you would watch rain fall on the waterhole out front.
phrases.grey_evening: If you carried a last drink back to your cottage tonight, you would see the terrace lanterns and cloud over the bush.

phrases.clear_predawn: An hour before the sun comes up, the double room windows frame Tower Bridge, still lit over a dark Thames.
phrases.clear_morning: From the terrace at the water's edge, Tower Bridge and the Shard stand sharp under a clear morning sky.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the Vicinity restaurant looks out on Tower Bridge in full sun, with the Thames bright below it.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were in a double room now, you would see low sun on Tower Bridge and the Shard together.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight Tower Bridge is lit and, from a room window, the Thames shows the reflected lights of the city.
phrases.partly_morning: Patches of cloud sit over London this morning, but Tower Bridge is fully visible from the outdoor terrace.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Guests on the terrace this afternoon are watching sun and cloud take turns on Tower Bridge and the Shard.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud turns orange above Tower Bridge, seen from the fire pit on the terrace.
phrases.overcast: A flat grey sky covers London today, and Tower Bridge looks plain but complete from the Vicinity restaurant.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the Thames right now, so guests watch Tower Bridge from inside the Vicinity restaurant instead of the terrace.
phrases.thunderstorm: With thunder over London, the outdoor terrace is empty and the double rooms give the safer view of Tower Bridge.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hangs over the Thames today, and from the room windows Tower Bridge is only a grey outline.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on Tower Bridge, a rare sight from the terrace at the water's edge, where the fire pit is lit.
phrases.very_cold: It is bitterly cold outside, so most guests take their Tower Bridge view from the Vicinity restaurant rather than the terrace.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot London day, the orange seats on the terrace sit in full sun with Tower Bridge straight ahead.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night, and the fire pit on the terrace is lit while Tower Bridge shines across the water.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low over London today: Tower Bridge is still clear from the rooms, but the Shard has disappeared from the frame.
phrases.late_night: Dinner at Vicinity is over, and after midnight the room window frames Tower Bridge's towers above a Thames full of city lights.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain blurs the room windows after midnight, and the Thames shows the city lights under the two towers of Tower Bridge.
phrases.grey_evening: Haze drifts across Tower Bridge's two towers after midnight, and the Thames shows the city's lights in soft blurs.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the outline of Great Gable is already sharp against a clear sky from the bedroom windows.
phrases.clear_morning: Sun lights the striped lawn and the croquet hoops, and all three fells are clear from the seven rooms.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the wooded hillside is in full sun, seen from the sitting room bay window over a cup of tea.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were there this afternoon, you would watch the low sun move across Glaramara from a bedroom window.
phrases.clear_night: Stars over Borrowdale tonight, and the dark shapes of Great Gable and Dale Head are still visible from the rooms.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over the fells this morning, so Great Gable shows and hides while tea is poured in the sitting room.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the lawn in front of the stone facade, patches of sun cross the open fields and the hillside.
phrases.partly_golden: The last sun catches the top of Dale Head between clouds, a view the bedroom windows face directly.
phrases.overcast: Grey sky sits low over Borrowdale today, and the red velvet armchairs in the sitting room are the brighter option.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the croquet lawn, and the wooded hillside beyond the bay window looks darker and wetter than usual.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm is over the fells, and a bedroom window shows lightning above Glaramara between the showers.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides Great Gable and Dale Head today, and only the nearest fields are visible from the rooms.
phrases.snow: Snow lies on the tops of all three fells, and the striped lawn below the windows is white too.
phrases.very_cold: It is bitterly cold outside today, and the oak tree and fells look very sharp from the bedroom windows.
phrases.very_hot: On this unusually hot day for the Lake District, guests sit under the tall oak tree rather than on the open lawn.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night in Borrowdale, with the fells hidden and the bay window showing only the dark hillside.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is poor today, so Great Gable and Dale Head cannot be seen, though the lawn and hedged lane are clear.
phrases.late_night: Rain on the bay windows is a reason to sleep after midnight; Dale Head and Great Gable return to view at dawn.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the sitting room's bay window after midnight, and the open curtain shows only wet glass over Borrowdale.
phrases.grey_evening: Low cloud covers Borrowdale after midnight, and the sitting room's bay window shows the pale lawn before the curtains are drawn for sleep.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the karst formations of Phang Nga Bay are dark shapes seen from the private terraces.
phrases.clear_morning: Early guests at the infinity pool can see Rang Yai and Coconut islands clearly in the morning sun.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the white pool umbrellas are the only shade near the loungers, and the bay is bright turquoise.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon light falls on the limestone karsts, and guests on the balconies watch the islands change colour.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would see stars over Phang Nga Bay from a villa terrace, with no cloud.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds sit over the islands this morning, and the infinity pool already has swimmers.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over Phang Nga Bay this afternoon, so the karsts seen from the terraces move in and out of shadow.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun lights the clouds orange over the bay, and wine on the balconies is a common sight.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the bay looks flat and silver from the pool, but the islands are still easy to see.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the jungle canopy below the villas, and guests watch the bay through the tall glass of their rooms.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over Phang Nga Bay is visible from the villas, and the infinity pool is empty for now.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hides the far karsts today, so from the terraces only the nearest islands and the water are visible.
phrases.snow: Snow is almost impossible in Phuket, but if it fell, the villa terraces above the jungle would show it first.
phrases.very_cold: On a very cold day, which almost never happens in Phuket, the loungers by the pool would stay empty.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot air sits over the bay, and most guests stay in the infinity pool or under the white umbrellas.
phrases.mild_night: Tonight is warm with cloud over the bay, and the island outlines are hard to make out from the balconies.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the distant karsts are not visible from the pool, only the nearer water and trees.
phrases.late_night: A glass of water near midnight, and through the villa's glass doors Phang Nga Bay shows a little moonlight on the water.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the villa glass doors this evening, and Phang Nga Bay shows grey under low cloud.
phrases.grey_evening: If you had a last drink in the villa tonight, you would see low cloud over Phang Nga Bay beyond the pool.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the wooden deck is empty and the Aegean below the pool is still dark and flat.
phrases.clear_morning: From a Junior King Suite balcony this morning, the mountains across the water show every ridge in clean sunlight.
phrases.clear_midday: Midday sun is strong over Torba Bay, and most guests have moved from the wooden jetties into the sea.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sunlight is coming across the water now, and the whitewashed villas near the pool turn pale orange.
phrases.clear_night: On the rooftop terrace, the ring-lit trees are switched on and the distant islands are dark shapes under a clear sky.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds sit over the forested hills behind Bodrum Bay this morning, but the sea by the jetties is bright.
phrases.partly_afternoon: This afternoon, cloud shadows cross the Aegean beyond the infinity pool and the wooden jetties at Torba Bay.
phrases.partly_golden: If you were on the seaside terrace, you would see the last sun light the clouds above the mountains across the water.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers Torba Bay today, so the Aegean beyond the pool looks grey too, and the lounge chairs are free.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the wooden jetties, and from the suite balconies the mountains across the water are hidden.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder sounds over the Aegean, and lightning across the open water is easiest to watch from a bedroom window.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over the water today means the mountains across the bay are soft outlines, though the jetties are clear.
phrases.snow: Snow falling on the wooden deck above the Aegean is a rare sight here, and the cypress trees are turning white.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air for Bodrum today, and the pool lounge chairs stay empty while the sea and mountains look sharp.
phrases.very_hot: Under a very hot sun, the infinity pool and the sea at the end of the jetties are the only comfortable places.
phrases.mild_night: Under a clouded night sky, the lit infinity pool glows above Torba Bay and the dark Aegean water.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Guests by the infinity pool today see the wooden jetties and nearby water, but haze hides the mountains across the bay.
phrases.late_night: Late dinner at Malva over, the suite window shows the pool lights on Torba Bay.
phrases.wet_evening: With the curtain open after midnight, rain runs down the suite window and the lit infinity pool shines through it by the sea.
phrases.grey_evening: Clouds hide the moon over Torba Bay tonight, and the lit pool shows through the open curtain of a Junior King Suite.

phrases.clear_predawn: While Santa Monica is still dark, the ocean-view rooms face a black Pacific with the Pier's shape just visible.
phrases.clear_morning: A suite window this morning frames Santa Monica Beach, the palm trees and the Pacific clear to the horizon.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday, the Pier and the Pacific are under strong sun, and the ocean-view rooms are the brightest in the building.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were there this afternoon, you would see the sun going down over the Pacific from your room window.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the Pier lights are on along the beach, and downstairs the Georgian Room has live jazz Wednesday through Saturday.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over the Pacific this morning, so the ocean-view windows show changing light on the water and the Pier.
phrases.partly_afternoon: The terrace level around Sirena gets sun and cloud in turns this afternoon, a normal Santa Monica mix.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, the clouds over the Pacific take colour, seen from the dining nook in the suites.
phrases.overcast: Grey cloud covers Santa Monica today, and from the room windows the Pacific and the Pier look the same dull colour.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on Ocean Avenue today, so the Georgian Room with its leather booths is a sensible place to sit.
phrases.thunderstorm: A storm is over the Pacific, and from the ocean-facing suites the lightning is visible well past the Pier.
phrases.fog_haze: Marine fog hangs over the beach this morning, and the Pier is a pale outline from the Ocean Avenue rooms.
phrases.snow: Snow in Santa Monica is unheard of, so a few flakes over the Pier would be worth a photo from the window.
phrases.very_cold: Freezing air is rare here, so the beach below the windows is nearly empty and the Pier has very few visitors.
phrases.very_hot: It is very hot today, and from the room windows the beach near the Pier is full of people.
phrases.mild_night: On a mild, cloudy night the Pier lights still show from the suites, and on jazz nights the Georgian Room is busy.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the beach and the Pier are clear from the windows but the far ocean horizon is not.
phrases.late_night: Whoever has a Pier-facing suite has turned off every light, and the window over the Pier and Pacific is the only glow.
phrases.wet_evening: Whoever has an ocean-view room after midnight can watch rain run down the glass, the Pier a long shape over the water.
phrases.grey_evening: Whoever is awake in an ocean-facing suite after midnight can watch the haze move slowly over the Pacific past the Pier.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Fortress Hohensalzburg is only a dark outline above the trees from the seventh-floor Sky Suite balconies.
phrases.clear_morning: Guests at breakfast in Restaurant Mirabell look out at the park trees under a clear morning sky.
phrases.clear_midday: Under a clear midday sky, the Sky Suite balconies give a direct, bright view of the fortress and Mirabell Gardens.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: In the last hours of sun, warm light falls on the cathedral domes and the fortress above them, seen from ETAGE7.
phrases.clear_night: From the ETAGE7 Rooftop Lounge, stars shine in the clear night sky above Hohensalzburg Fortress and the Mirabell Gardens.
phrases.partly_morning: Scattered clouds move over the fortress this morning, and the Mirabell Gardens below the balconies are partly in shade.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From a seventh-floor balcony this afternoon, the Alps show between clouds, and the gardens are green in broken sunlight.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun lights the fortress walls between passing clouds, a view the Sky Suites face directly.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky sits over Salzburg today, but the fortress and the garden treetops remain easy to see from the guest rooms.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on Mirabell Gardens, and guests in Restaurant Mirabell watch the wet trees through the floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.thunderstorm: If you were there during this thunderstorm, you would watch lightning over the fortress hill from inside a Sky Suite.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides the top of the fortress today; from the seventh floor, only the nearest garden trees are plain.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling on the fortress and the garden paths, seen from the private balconies of the ETAGE7 Sky Suites.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air outside; from behind the suite windows, the fortress and the Alps look sharp in the clear daylight.
phrases.very_hot: The Mirabell Gardens look dry and bright below the Sky Suite balconies on this very hot Salzburg afternoon.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night; the Piano Bar has live music, and from the rooftop lounge the fortress is hard to make out.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the seventh floor the Alps are missing and the fortress looks faded above the trees.
phrases.late_night: If you switched off the Sky Suite lights now, only the lit city below the fortress hill would show in the room.
phrases.wet_evening: If you were in the ETAGE7 Lounge for a last drink, rain on the glass would blur the fortress on its hill.
phrases.grey_evening: Over a last drink in the ETAGE7 Rooftop Lounge tonight, you would see Salzburg's lights under low cloud beneath the Fortress.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the upper-floor suites look over a dark Copacabana Beach, with Sugarloaf Mountain a black shape against the sky.
phrases.clear_morning: From the Clarice Restaurant windows, breakfast comes with a clear view of the beach and the Atlantic in full sun.
phrases.clear_midday: From the upper floors at midday, the full curve of Copacabana Beach runs toward Sugarloaf Mountain under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Seen from the Isabel Lounge terrace, the late sun lights Sugarloaf Mountain and the rocky islands in the Atlantic.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in the rooftop Isabel Lounge tonight, you would see the curve of Copacabana Beach and the city skyline.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds sit over the green hills this morning, while the guest-room windows still show Copacabana Beach in sun.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over Corcovado this afternoon, and from the rooftop terrace the beach goes from bright to shaded and back.
phrases.partly_golden: Just before sunset, broken cloud above the rocky islands turns orange, seen from the lounge chairs on the rooftop terrace.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky covers Rio today, but from the ocean-facing suites Sugarloaf Mountain and the beach are still clear to see.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on Copacabana Beach, and from the Clarice Restaurant windows the sand looks almost empty.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the Atlantic is visible from the guest-room windows, and nobody is using the rooftop terrace right now.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hides Sugarloaf Mountain today, so the 38th-floor Spa Anna Pegova is a reasonable place to be.
phrases.snow: Snow does not fall in Rio, but if it ever did, the view of Copacabana Beach from the suites would be unusual.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold air over Copacabana is almost unheard of, and the Clarice Restaurant windows give the beach view without the wind.
phrases.very_hot: The rooftop infinity pool fills quickly on a very hot day, and the whole arc of Copacabana Beach shows from the water.
phrases.mild_night: Under a cloudy sky tonight, the air is mild, and the Isabel Lounge terrace has the beach and the sea in view.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so Sugarloaf Mountain and the rocky islands are hard to see, though the beach below is clear.
phrases.late_night: Sleep comes easily in the ocean-facing suites while the beach lights curve along Copacabana below, and Sugarloaf comes back at dawn.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain on the ocean-facing suite windows blurs the beach lights along Copacabana's wet curve toward Sugarloaf after midnight.
phrases.grey_evening: Low cloud passes over Sugarloaf after midnight, and the lamps along Copacabana Beach show the whole curve below the upper-floor suites.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Sand River below the Varty Camp chalets is still a grey strip of sand under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_morning: If you were on the Tree Camp deck this clear morning, you would see elephants crossing the Sand River bed.
phrases.clear_midday: Midday sun on the plunge pool deck, with two elephants feeding in the green bush just past the railing.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Golden hour reaches the open-air lounge under its thatched roof, and the bushveld beyond the big tree turns a warmer colour.
phrases.clear_night: On a clear night the lanterns around the pool show in the water, and the sky over the camp fills with stars.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds over the Sabi Sand this morning, and the Varty Camp chalets look out on a riverbed in patches of shade.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the sun loungers by the plunge pool, the afternoon is a mix of cloud shadow and sun across the green bush.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud sits over the river while guests on the Tree Camp deck watch the bank.
phrases.overcast: Grey sky over the whole reserve today, but game viewing from the Varty Camp chalets continues as usual over the river.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the timber deck around the lap pool, and the thatched roof of the lounge keeps the seating dry.
phrases.thunderstorm: If you were there during this thunderstorm, you would watch lightning over the bushveld from under the thatch of the lounge.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hangs over the Sand River today, so the far bank is only a blurred outline from the Varty Camp chalets.
phrases.snow: Snow is almost unknown in the Sabi Sand, but today the view from the Tree Camp deck includes a few white flakes.
phrases.very_cold: A very cold winter day, the kind when the bush is thin and the elephants show clearly from the deck.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot across the reserve today, and the plunge pool on the suite deck is where most guests spend the midday hours.
phrases.mild_night: Mild and cloudy tonight along the river, and in the warmer months the smell of potato bush reaches the decks at dusk.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the Varty Camp chalets the river sand is clear but the far trees are not sharp.
phrases.late_night: Anyone up for water around midnight in a Varty Camp chalet sees the Sand River pale under the moon.
phrases.wet_evening: Guests in the Varty Camp chalets are likely asleep by now, rain falling on the Sand River in front of their windows.
phrases.grey_evening: Anyone awake in a Varty Camp chalet sees cloud over the Sand River and the pool lanterns reflected in the water.

phrases.clear_predawn: Guests on the oceanfront balconies before sunrise watch the clear sky grow light over the Atlantic beyond the baobab garden.
phrases.clear_morning: From the oceanfront balconies, the sun is already over the Atlantic, and breakfast at Elements Restaurant is underway.
phrases.clear_midday: Clear sky at midday, and the water off the beach looks turquoise from the floor-to-ceiling windows of the king rooms.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun lights the Art Deco buildings along the beach, seen from the teal cabanas on the hotel's sand.
phrases.clear_night: On a clear night after midnight, stars show over the Atlantic beyond the oceanfront balconies at The Palms Hotel.
phrases.partly_morning: From the oceanfront balcony, a few morning clouds hang over the Atlantic beyond the baobab garden and white sand.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds come and go over South Beach this afternoon, so the sea changes colour from the suite windows.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun is partly behind cloud, and the terrace in the baobab garden is filling for dinner.
phrases.overcast: From the oceanfront balconies, grey cloud sits over the whole Atlantic and the white sand below the baobab garden.
phrases.rain: Rain over Miami Beach right now, and the Elements terrace in the baobab garden is wet, so dining moves indoors.
phrases.thunderstorm: Thunder over the Atlantic right now, and guests watch the lightning from behind the floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over the water today, so from the oceanfront balconies the horizon is unclear and the sea looks pale.
phrases.snow: Snow is almost unheard of here, but if it fell today, it would land on the baobab garden and the pool.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold for Miami Beach, so the beach chairs stay folded and the oceanfront pool has nobody in it.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot on the sand this afternoon, so most guests sit under the teal umbrellas or stay in the pool.
phrases.mild_night: A mild, cloudy night, and dinner on the outdoor terrace among the baobab trees needs no jacket.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Low visibility today, and from the suite windows the shoreline is easy to see but the far horizon is not.
phrases.late_night: The oceanfront suite has its lights off at two, and only the glow along South Beach reaches the window.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner at Elements, rain runs down the floor-to-ceiling windows of the oceanfront rooms and the lights along South Beach blur.
phrases.grey_evening: After dinner at Elements, the oceanfront rooms look out on the shoreline lights of South Beach under tonight's low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the tallest CBD towers stand as dark outlines against a clear sky, seen from the rooftop pool.
phrases.clear_morning: From the Valley Suite, the clear morning sky puts sharp edges on every skyscraper across the CBD panorama.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the rooftop pool sits in full Brisbane sun, and the skyscrapers ahead reflect it straight back.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Guests by the rooftop pool this afternoon look out at the tallest CBD towers under a clear late sky.
phrases.clear_night: If you were in the rooftop pool tonight, the pink neon would colour the water under a clear Brisbane sky.
phrases.partly_morning: Scattered clouds sit over the high-rises this morning, seen through the floor-to-ceiling windows of the guest rooms.
phrases.partly_afternoon: This afternoon the sun comes and goes over the rooftop pool as broken cloud moves across the Brisbane skyline.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, a few clouds turn orange above the CBD towers, watched from the rooftop lounge.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the skyscrapers lose their shine, but the Valley Suite still frames the whole CBD panorama.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the rooftop pool, and the skyscrapers across the skyline look blurred through the wet glass balustrade.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm sits over the CBD towers, and the sensible view is through a guest room's floor-to-ceiling windows, not the rooftop.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over Brisbane softens the tallest skyscrapers into pale shapes today, as seen from the rooftop pool.
phrases.snow: Brisbane almost never sees snow, so white flakes over the rooftop pool and CBD towers would be a rare sight.
phrases.very_cold: On a rare very cold Brisbane day, the rooftop pool has few takers, and the skyscrapers look sharp in the dry air.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot air over Fortitude Valley makes the rooftop pool the obvious place, with the CBD skyscrapers straight ahead.
phrases.mild_night: On a mild cloudy night, the rooftop lounge's pink neon is on and the skyscrapers stand under low cloud across the Valley.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the tallest CBD towers are only faint outlines from the Valley Suite windows.
phrases.late_night: If you were back in the Valley Suite after midnight, you would see the CBD towers lit through the windows.
phrases.wet_evening: With a last drink in the Valley Suite now, you would see rain on the glass and the CBD towers lit beyond.
phrases.grey_evening: If you were having a last drink in the Valley Suite now, you would see the CBD towers lit under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the waterhole is already visible from the private suite decks, with nothing yet drinking at it.
phrases.clear_morning: From the villa kitchen, guests with coffee can see whatever has come to drink at the waterhole this morning.
phrases.clear_midday: Midday sun on the dry bushveld, and the heated plunge pool on each suite deck is the easiest place to watch from.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun lights the dry bush around the waterhole, seen from the open-air thatched gazebo.
phrases.clear_night: On a clear night like this, dinner can move down into the riverbed, with the stars overhead instead of a roof.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over the Thornybush this morning, and elephants may be at the waterhole in front of the pool deck.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Patches of shade move across the bushveld this afternoon, watched from the gazebo with a drink from the main bar.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, clouds break the light over the waterhole, seen from the four suites that face it.
phrases.overcast: A grey sky over the reserve today, but the waterhole is still clearly visible from the villa lounge and dining area.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the bushveld, and the thatched roof of the gazebo keeps its seats dry for watching the waterhole.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm over the reserve means dinner stays indoors rather than in the riverbed, with the wine cellar nearby.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over the bushveld today softens the far trees, but the waterhole in front of the decks stays easy to see.
phrases.snow: From the suite's private deck, snow lies on the bushveld around the waterhole, lit by the fire bowl on the main deck.
phrases.very_cold: On a very cold morning in the bush, guests watch the waterhole from the heated plunge pool rather than the deck.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot today, and the elephants at the waterhole and the guests in the main pool are both in the water.
phrases.mild_night: Mild cloudy night, so fewer stars over the riverbed dinner, though the waterhole can still be watched from the suite decks.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Low visibility over the reserve today hides the far bush, though the waterhole below the decks is still clear.
phrases.late_night: After the riverbed dinner, the lodge lights reflect in the waterhole that the four suites face.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the glass walls of the lounge, and the lodge lights show in the waterhole through the drops.
phrases.grey_evening: Cloud covers the moon over the waterhole after midnight, and from the suites the lodge lights show on the water.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Big Ben-facing rooms look onto a dark sky, with the clock face still lit and readable.
phrases.clear_morning: Under a clear morning sky, red buses cross below the floor-to-ceiling windows on the Big Ben side.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the London Eye turns slowly in full sun, easy to follow from the rooftop terrace seats.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun hits the gilded clock face, and guests in upper-floor rooms can read the time without squinting much.
phrases.clear_night: Under a clear night sky, the lit London Eye and Big Ben are both in view from the rooftop terrace.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over Westminster this morning, and the Houses of Parliament go in and out of shadow outside the room windows.
phrases.partly_afternoon: The rooftop terrace has sun between clouds this afternoon, with the wicker seats mostly in use.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud colours the sky behind Big Ben, seen from the terrace champagne tables.
phrases.overcast: Grey cloud covers London today, and the London Eye looks flat and pale from the Eye-facing rooms.
phrases.rain: Rain runs down the floor-to-ceiling windows, and Big Ben is still readable, which is the whole point of that side.
phrases.thunderstorm: During the storm, the indoor pool is the sensible place, while lightning over Westminster shows through the room windows.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog hides most of the London Eye today, and guests in Big Ben rooms see only the lower tower clearly.
phrases.snow: Snow falls on the Westminster rooftops, and the terrace wicker seats are empty while the Executive Lounge is not.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold and clear today, so the rooftop terrace is empty and the London Eye is unusually sharp from the Eye-facing rooms.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot London afternoon, the indoor pool and the Mandara Spa get more use than the sunny rooftop terrace.
phrases.mild_night: Tonight is mild under cloud, guests gather at the Primo Bar, and the London Eye is lit outside the Eye-facing rooms.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is poor today, Big Ben reads from the upper floors but the city rooftops beyond the London Eye do not show.
phrases.late_night: Guests in the London Eye-facing rooms are likely asleep after midnight, and the wheel's circle shows in their windows again at dawn.
phrases.wet_evening: Guests in the London Eye-facing rooms watch the wheel's shape through rain on the floor-to-ceiling glass as the city's lights come on.
phrases.grey_evening: Anyone awake in a London Eye-facing room tonight sees the wheel's round shape against low cloud and the lit rooftops.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, one tower looks onto dark open water while the other faces Lusail's towers, still lit.
phrases.clear_morning: A clear morning over the marina, and from the freestanding tub the geometric windows show calm blue Gulf water.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sun is strong on the cantilevered infinity pool, and the Gulf beyond it is very bright to look at.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Warm afternoon light fills the guest rooms through floor-to-ceiling windows, with the curved tower and waterfront outside.
phrases.clear_night: After dark the city-facing tower looks straight at Lusail's lit skyline, while the Gulf side is simply black water.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds over the Gulf, so the water seen from the infinity pool is blue in patches and grey in others.
phrases.partly_afternoon: If you were there this afternoon, you would see cloud shadows moving across the marina from the rooftop terrace's rattan seats.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun turns the clouds orange above the sea, best seen from under the rooftop's white lattice canopy.
phrases.overcast: Grey sky over Doha today, and the Gulf from the guest room windows is a flat grey too, with no clear horizon.
phrases.rain: Rain is rare in Doha, so wet sun loungers by the infinity pool are a small event, and nobody is using them.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a storm, lightning over the Gulf is best watched from the upper rooms, not from the sea-level beach club.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over the water today, so from the tub's geometric windows the Gulf fades to white not far from the shore.
phrases.snow: Snow in Doha would be a first, and anyone on the rooftop terrace would photograph the lattice canopy, not the sea.
phrases.very_cold: An unusually cold day for Qatar, so the three outdoor pools are quiet and guests watch the Gulf from indoors.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot outside, as usual here, and the infinity pool is the only part of the rooftop anyone stays on for long.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night, and the rattan seats under the lattice canopy are busy, with Lusail's towers lit on the city side.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so from the guest rooms the near marina is clear but the far Gulf horizon is not visible.
phrases.late_night: Well after midnight, the guest-room windows show Lusail's tower lights on the marina water.
phrases.wet_evening: After dinner at Mila, the marina lights look blurred through the rain on the guest-room windows.
phrases.grey_evening: Dinner at Mila is over, and the floor-to-ceiling room windows show Lusail's lit towers under tonight's low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the Premier River Room windows show Charles Bridge as a dark line over the Vltava, with the castle behind.
phrases.clear_morning: Breakfast tables on the terrace are set in direct sun, with Charles Bridge and the Vltava River right in front of them.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday, the river-facing rooms get a clear view of Prague Castle and St. Vitus Cathedral above the bridge.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were in a Premier River Room now, you would see the sun setting behind Prague Castle, as the hotel promises.
phrases.clear_night: Tonight the hotel's lit windows reflect on the Vltava, and Charles Bridge is visible from the river-facing rooms under a clear sky.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over Prague Castle this morning, so the terrace breakfast comes with changing light on the Vltava River.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the floor-to-ceiling windows, patches of sun and shadow move across the red roofs of the Old Town this afternoon.
phrases.partly_golden: The last sun of the day catches St. Vitus Cathedral between clouds, seen from the hotel terrace across the river.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky, Charles Bridge and the Vltava look flat and calm from the river-facing rooms, but fully visible.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on Charles Bridge right now, and guests are watching it from behind the floor-to-ceiling windows.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm is over Prague, and from the guest rooms lightning shows Prague Castle for a second at a time.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog sits on the Vltava today, so from the terrace Charles Bridge is only partly visible and the castle is hidden.
phrases.snow: Snow covers the red roofs of the Old Town and Charles Bridge, seen from the warm guest rooms through the big windows.
phrases.very_cold: It is very cold outside, so the view of Prague Castle is mostly enjoyed from inside, behind the floor-to-ceiling glass.
phrases.very_hot: The terrace is in full sun on this very hot day, and the Vltava River below looks cooler than it is.
phrases.mild_night: Clouds cover the sky on this mild night, and the hotel's lit windows reflect on the dark Vltava River.
phrases.reduced_visibility: From the terrace today, Charles Bridge is sharp, but Prague Castle behind it is only a pale shape in the air.
phrases.late_night: After midnight the city lights reflect in the Vltava outside the Premier River Rooms, and at dawn Charles Bridge will show again.
phrases.wet_evening: Back from dinner after midnight, rain runs down the Premier River Room's tall window and Charles Bridge blurs across the Vltava.
phrases.grey_evening: After a late dinner, the Premier River Room's window shows city lights on the Vltava by Charles Bridge under low cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the street lamps on Avenida dos Aliados are still on, seen from the upper-floor suites.
phrases.clear_morning: Breakfast at La Mezzanine comes with clear morning light through the original glazed brasserie windows.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday, the stone building opposite the room windows stands in full sun under a blue sky.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: From the rooftop, the late sun lights up Porto City Hall and Avenida dos Aliados below.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would look down on Avenida dos Aliados from a suite, then finish at Bar Americain.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds over Porto this morning, and La Mezzanine is serving brunch in its glazed brasserie room.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over Avenida dos Aliados this afternoon, and the suite windows get sun in short periods.
phrases.partly_golden: The rooftop has the last hour of sun on Porto City Hall, with a few clouds in between.
phrases.overcast: Grey sky over the avenue today, so the red-walled suites with their Art Deco mirrors look darker than usual.
phrases.rain: Rain on Avenida dos Aliados, watched from the upper-floor suites, while the indoor spa pool stays an option.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm over Porto is best watched from a suite window, or not at all from the hammam.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog over Porto today hides the far end of Avenida dos Aliados from the rooftop.
phrases.snow: Porto almost never sees snow, so guests in the upper-floor suites are watching the flakes land on Avenida dos Aliados.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold outside for Porto, and the sauna at the Grand Bleu Spa has more visitors than the rooftop.
phrases.very_hot: On a very hot day in Porto, the indoor pool with its green mosaic wall is the cooler choice.
phrases.mild_night: A mild cloudy night in Porto, and guests are sitting late at Bar Americain rather than on the rooftop.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Low visibility today, and from the rooftop Porto City Hall is only a faint shape at the end of the avenue.
phrases.late_night: In the upper-floor suites the curtain is left open tonight, so the lights of Aliados Avenue fill the window until morning.
phrases.wet_evening: After a late dinner at Le Monument, the upper-floor suite windows show Aliados Avenue wet and bright in the rain.

phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky, the Osaka skyline looks flat and even from the king rooms, with no shadows between the buildings.

phrases.grey_evening: The curtains are open late tonight in the Matsu Suite, and the Osaka skyline is lit under low cloud.

phrases.clear_midday: From the terrace balustrade, the midday Atlantic lies flat and blue to a sharp horizon under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun turns the terracotta facade orange, and the outdoor pool shows that colour too for about an hour.
phrases.clear_night: If you were there tonight, you would see the lit pool terrace below and a dark Atlantic beyond from a sea-view room.
phrases.partly_morning: Clouds pass over Cascais Bay this morning, so the sea in front of the hotel changes between grey and blue.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Guests on the pool terrace get sun for a few minutes, then shade, as clouds move across the Atlantic.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun lights the clouds over Cascais Bay from below, a view the penthouse rooftop terraces have in full.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky, the sea-facing restaurants still have plenty of daylight, and the Atlantic is a flat grey.
phrases.rain: Rain falls on the empty terrace tables while guests watch Cascais Bay through the restaurant windows or use the Real Spa.
phrases.thunderstorm: During a storm, lightning over the Atlantic is visible from the balcony doors of the sea-view rooms, kept shut for now.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog sits on Cascais Bay today, and from the terrace only the nearest water past the balustrade can be seen.
phrases.snow: Snow is very rare in Cascais, but if it fell today, the penthouse rooftop terraces would be white before anything else.
phrases.very_cold: A very cold day for Cascais: the outdoor pool is empty, and guests sit indoors at the sea-facing restaurants instead.

phrases.mild_night: A mild, cloudy night, with the pool terrace lit and a few guests still outside at the marble tables.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today; from the sea-view rooms the water in front of the hotel is visible, but the horizon is not.
phrases.late_night: Guests in the sea-view rooms are likely asleep, a few shore lights on the water until dawn shows Cascais Bay again.
phrases.wet_evening: Anyone awake in the sea-view rooms sees rain on the glass and the lights of Cascais blurred across the bay.
phrases.grey_evening: Whoever has a sea-view room tonight can watch the lights of Cascais along the bay under low cloud before bed.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the karsts of Phang Nga Bay are dark shapes against a clear sky, seen from the villa balconies.
phrases.clear_morning: Floating breakfasts are going out to the villa pools this morning, with the limestone islands in full sun across the bay.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the shaded seating area beside the hilltop infinity pool is the sensible place to look at the karsts from.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun lights the limestone karsts from the side, and the outdoor dining deck has a clear view of all of them.
phrases.clear_night: On a clear night, a bonfire on the private beach is the main light, with stars over Phang Nga Bay.
phrases.partly_morning: Some clouds sit over the Andaman this morning, but from the Hilltop restaurant the karst islands are all in view.
phrases.partly_afternoon: Clouds pass over the bay this afternoon, so the karsts seen from the villa plunge pools move between sun and shade.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, broken cloud over the bay makes the candlelit beach dinner tables a good place to sit.
phrases.overcast: Under a grey sky the karsts look flatter from the infinity pool terrace, and the sea is more silver than blue.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on the jungle around the villas, and the karsts of Phang Nga Bay are softer grey shapes.
phrases.thunderstorm: A storm is over the bay, and from the living room terrace guests can watch lightning behind the limestone islands.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze over the Andaman today means the far karsts are faint from the hilltop pool, while the near ones stay clear.
phrases.snow: Snow on Ko Yao Noi would be a first; if it fell today, the villa balconies would face white karsts.
phrases.very_cold: Very cold weather is almost unknown here; the beach sun loungers would stay empty and the spa would be busy.
phrases.very_hot: It is very hot today, and most guests are in the hilltop infinity pool or their villa plunge pools rather than walking.
phrases.mild_night: The night is warm and cloudy, and the movie screening on the private beach goes ahead with no stars overhead.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today, so from the Hilltop restaurant the nearest karsts show but the far islands do not.
phrases.late_night: Guests in the villas fall asleep tonight with the curtain left open, so the Phang Nga Bay karsts show at first light.
phrases.wet_evening: Anyone awake in a villa bedroom now sees rain running down the glass where Phang Nga Bay showed at dusk.
phrases.grey_evening: Whoever is awake in a villa tonight sees low cloud over Phang Nga Bay, the water showing pale beneath it.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the balconies of the sea-view suites face a dark Ionian Sea, with Etna still a black shape.
phrases.clear_morning: From the rooftop terrace this morning, the coastline runs clearly from Calabria to Etna under a sky without cloud.
phrases.clear_midday: At midday the infinity pool and the Ionian Sea below it show the same strong blue under a cloudless sky.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: During aperitivo hour on the rooftop bar, the low sun gives Etna and the Bay of Naxos a warm orange colour.
phrases.clear_night: Under a clear night sky, stars show above Etna and the Bay of Naxos from the rooftop terrace bar.
phrases.partly_morning: Scattered clouds pass over Taormina Bay this morning, and the glass-enclosed terrace has its dining tables set facing the water.
phrases.partly_afternoon: If you stood on the rooftop terrace this afternoon, you would see a few clouds over Etna and sun on Taormina Bay.
phrases.partly_golden: In the last hour of sun, guests on the rooftop bar watch broken clouds over Etna turn pink during aperitivo.
phrases.overcast: Under full cloud today, the Ionian Sea seen from the suite balconies looks grey and flat rather than deep blue.
phrases.rain: Rain is falling on Corso Umberto, so the indoor spa pool under its vaulted ceiling is the busier choice right now.
phrases.thunderstorm: Lightning over the Ionian Sea is visible from the glass-enclosed terrace, where meals continue with a dry view of the storm.
phrases.fog_haze: Haze hangs over the bay, so Etna is only a faint grey shape from the rooftop terrace, if it shows at all.
phrases.snow: Snow is falling over Taormina, a rare sight, and the indoor spa pool under the vaulted ceiling is where most guests are.
phrases.very_cold: On a day this cold, the infinity pool terrace is empty, but Etna and the Calabrian coast are sharp from the rooftop.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot air sits over Taormina Bay, and most guests are either in the infinity pool or under the shaded terraces.
phrases.mild_night: Clouds cover the stars tonight, but the air is mild and the rooftop bar still serves aperitivo over the dark sea.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today, so the Calabrian coast across the sea is not visible from the rooftop, only the nearer bay.
phrases.late_night: If you were falling asleep in a sea-view suite now, you might leave the curtain open for the lights along the bay.
phrases.wet_evening: If you had a last drink at the rooftop bar tonight, you would see the coast lights toward Etna through the rain.
phrases.grey_evening: If you were having a last drink in a sea-view suite tonight, you would see Naxos Bay lit under cloud.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise, the lake below the Aurora Inn balconies is still dark, and the far bank is only a line.
phrases.clear_morning: Coffee on an Aurora Inn balcony right now comes with a clear view across Cayuga Lake to the far bank.
phrases.clear_midday: If you were there now, you would see kayaks leaving the guests-only waterfront north of Rowland House under a clear sky.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late sun drops toward the far bank, and the veranda of 1833 Kitchen & Bar fills for dinner.
phrases.clear_night: Stars are out over Cayuga Lake tonight, and the infinity pool is lit, with trees in silhouette between pool and water.
phrases.partly_morning: A few clouds move over the lake this morning, so the water changes color as seen from the Aurora Inn balconies.
phrases.partly_afternoon: From the spa's soaking pools on the hill, patches of sun cross Cayuga Lake between the clouds this afternoon.
phrases.partly_golden: The last hour of sun lights the clouds over the far bank, watched from the docks and the veranda.
phrases.overcast: Low grey cloud covers Cayuga Lake today, and the far bank shows faintly beyond the 1903 Rowland House boathouse.
phrases.rain: Wet day on Cayuga Lake, so the indoor spa pool with its floor-to-ceiling windows is where most guests are.
phrases.thunderstorm: A thunderstorm is over the lake, and lightning on the far bank is visible from the Aurora Inn balconies.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog covers Cayuga Lake today and hides the far bank, so from the veranda the docks are the only thing in view.
phrases.snow: Snow settles on the copper roofs of the five houses, and the soaking pools on the hill steam more than usual.
phrases.very_cold: Outside it is very cold, so the indoor spa pool, with its windows on Cayuga Lake, is the busiest room today.
phrases.very_hot: A very hot afternoon here, and guests are either in the infinity pool or out on Cayuga in kayaks.
phrases.mild_night: Warm cloudy night, no stars, and the lit infinity pool is the brightest thing between the houses and the lake.
phrases.reduced_visibility: The far bank of Cayuga Lake is not visible today from the balconies, only the docks and the nearest water.

phrases.wet_evening: If you had a late drink at 1833 Kitchen & Bar, you would see rain on the window and Cayuga Lake beyond.
phrases.grey_evening: If you took a last drink up to an Aurora Inn room tonight, you would see low cloud over Cayuga Lake.

phrases.clear_midday: At midday the sky over Midtown is fully blue, and the Empire State Building fills the Studio King window with no haze.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: If you were there now, you would see the low sun turn the Empire State Building a warm orange from the rooftop.

phrases.thunderstorm: During the thunderstorm, guests under the Refinery Rooftop glass roof watch lightning flash behind the rain-streaked Empire State Building.
phrases.fog_haze: Fog sits over Midtown today, and only the lower floors of the Empire State Building show from the Studio King window.
phrases.snow: Snow is coming down over Manhattan, and the arched window in the bar and lounge shows a white street outside.
phrases.very_cold: Through the Studio King window, the Empire State Building stands in hard winter light, frost at the glass edges.
phrases.very_hot: Very hot air hangs over Midtown, and the Empire State Building stands in full sun outside the Studio King window.
phrases.mild_night: After midnight on a mild cloudy night, the lit Empire State Building glows through the Refinery Rooftop's glass roof.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the Empire State Building is still clear from the rooftop but its top floors look washed out.

phrases.clear_predawn: Still dark over Manhattan, and from the west-facing windows the Empire State Building stands black against a cloudless sky.

phrases.clear_midday: At midday the coin binoculars on the rooftop terrace give a close look at the Empire State Building in full sun.
phrases.clear_golden_pm: Late afternoon sun falls on the striped bar of the sun deck while the Midtown towers turn orange in the distance.
phrases.clear_night: A clear night over Manhattan, and the Empire State Building's lights are easy to see from the rooftop terrace.

phrases.fog_haze: In haze the Empire State Building is only a pale shape from the rooftop, and One World Trade Center may not appear.
phrases.snow: Snow falls past the west-facing windows, twenty-one floors up, and blurs the outline of the Empire State Building.

phrases.very_hot: Very hot today on the sun deck, where the striped bar does better business than the loungers in full sun.
phrases.mild_night: A mild night with clouds, and the rooftop terrace is comfortable for sitting while the Midtown lights show below the clouds.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is short today, so the Empire State Building is faint from the rooftop and One World Trade Center cannot be seen.
phrases.late_night: After midnight the Empire State Building's spire fills the west-facing windows, and the Midtown lights are hard to stop watching.
phrases.wet_evening: Rain runs down the west-facing windows tonight, and the Empire State Building's spire shows against the wet Midtown lights.
phrases.grey_evening: The west-facing rooms look out after midnight on a hazy Midtown, city lights soft under the cloud around the Empire State Building.

phrases.clear_predawn: Before sunrise under a clear sky, the upper lake-facing windows show pale light spreading over Lake Geneva and the Alps.

phrases.mild_night: On a mild cloudy night, Lake Geneva outside the lake-view rooms is almost invisible, and the heated pool stays warm.
phrases.reduced_visibility: Visibility is low today, so the Alps cannot be seen from the upper floors, only the near part of Lake Geneva.

phrases.mild_night: A warm cloudy night, and guests are still out in the lantern-lit courtyard while the illuminated infinity pool shines nearby.

phrases.wet_evening: Guests in the villas are probably inside tonight, watching rain run down the glass where the Adriatic was blue this afternoon.

phrases.wet_evening: Whoever has the Gothic King Suite tonight can see rain on the window and the Cathedral's spires straight ahead.
phrases.grey_evening: Whoever has the Gothic King Suite tonight can see the Cathedral spires above the lit rooftops, low cloud over the Gothic Quarter.

phrases.grey_evening: Anyone awake in a Deluxe Terrace suite after midnight can watch cloud pass over the Gulf, coast lights along the water.
